a: The humps go floppy and flop to the side
8049.e: When the fat is used up, the humps go floppy. After good feeding they stand up again.
8049.m: Floppy humps show the fat has been used.

8050.q: How long does a young bearded vulture still depend on its parents after its first flight?
8050.e: Even after the young bearded vulture can fly, its parents still help feed it for a few months. Only then does it become fully independent.
8050.m: Parents help for a long time after the first flight.

8051.q: In which season does the robin's breeding season usually begin?
8051.e: In spring, when it gets warmer and there are more insects, the robin starts building its nest and breeding. That is the best time for raising young.
8051.m: The breeding season begins in spring.

8052.q: What do woodlice return to the soil when they eat leaves and droppings?
a: Nutrients that plants can take up again
8052.e: Their droppings contain nutrients that are processed further in the soil. In this way, woodlice help in nature's cycle.

8053.q: Which animal likes to hunt mosquitoes in the air?
8053.e: Bats fly at night and catch lots of mosquitoes. A single bat can eat a great many mosquitoes in one evening.

8054.q: What do young sea turtles often eat differently from adults?
a: They eat more small animals instead of plants
8054.e: While adult green sea turtles eat a lot of seagrass, the young feed more on small animals such as jellyfish or crabs. Only later do many switch to plant food.
8054.m: Young turtles often eat more animal food.

8055.q: What does the tawny owl mainly eat?
8055.e: Mice make up most of the tawny owl's food. It also eats small birds, insects and sometimes earthworms.

8057.q: What is the role of a salmon's fat reserves before its spawning migration?
a: Energy for the journey, as it hardly eats
8057.e: During the migration, salmon usually hardly eat at all. They live on the reserves they built up in the sea.
8057.m: Fat reserves give energy for the migration.

8058.q: Why should children always wear a helmet when riding a horse?
a: To protect their head if they fall
So that the horse recognises them
So that they don't get cold
8058.e: A riding helmet protects your head if you fall off the horse. This is very important when riding, because you sit quite high up.
8058.m: A helmet protects your head when riding.

8060.q: How does a seahorse snap up its prey?
a: Lightning fast with its tube-shaped snout
8060.e: Although the seahorse swims slowly, its snout can snap shut at lightning speed. That is how it catches its tiny prey in the water.
8060.m: The snout snaps shut lightning fast.

8061.q: What is the pool frog, the other parent species, usually like compared to the edible frog?
a: Smaller and with shorter back legs
Much bigger than any edible frog
8061.e: The pool frog usually stays smaller and has shorter back legs than the marsh frog and the edible frog. Even so, it is one of the two original species of the edible frog.
8061.m: The pool frog is daintier than the edible frog.

8062.q: Why do many male edible frogs often call at the same time in a loud chorus?
a: So that together their calls can be heard further away and attract females
So that they can fight each other
8062.e: When many males call at once, the overall sound gets louder and attracts females from further away. This croaking together is called chorusing.

8063.q: Which is usually heavier, a bison bull or a bison cow?
8063.e: Bulls are much bigger and stronger than cows. This is the case in many horned animals.

8064.q: What is often different about male bumblebees compared to workers?
8064.e: Male bumblebees often have slightly longer antennae than the workers. This sometimes helps tell them apart.

8065.q: What do llamas sometimes do when they feel threatened or annoyed?
8065.e: Llamas spit to defend themselves or to settle arguments. Usually they spit at other llamas.

8066.q: Why do bees from the same hive often smell similar?
a: They share a common hive scent
They only eat from one flower
They are always the same age
8066.e: Every bee colony has its own smell by which the bees recognise each other. This lets guard bees spot strange intruders.
8066.m: Every colony has its own smell.

8067.q: What role do dragonflies play in the ecosystem?
a: They keep mosquitoes and other insects in check
8067.e: Dragonflies eat lots of mosquitoes and small insects. At the same time they are food for other animals.
8067.m: As hunters, dragonflies keep insects in check.

8068.q: Which group of animals does the kangaroo belong to?
8068.e: Kangaroo mothers carry their babies in a pouch on their belly. That is why they are called marsupials.

8069.q: Why do emperor penguins often stand close together in winter?
8069.e: In icy cold, many penguins huddle very close together. That way they give each other warmth and shelter from the wind.
8069.m: Penguins huddle together against the cold.

8070.q: What sets the slow worm apart from a frog?
a: It has dry, scaly skin and lays no spawn
It has a tadpole larval stage
8070.e: Frogs are amphibians with moist skin and tadpoles. The slow worm is a reptile with scales.
8070.m: Reptiles have scales, amphibians have moist skin.

8071.q: Which order of birds does the carrion crow belong to?
8071.e: The carrion crow belongs to the perching birds, even though it is much bigger than a typical sparrow. Crows are the largest members of this order.

8072.q: What colour is the cross on the Swiss flag?
8072.e: The Swiss flag shows a white cross on a red background. It is one of the oldest flags in the world.
8072.m: The Swiss flag shows a white cross on a red background.

8073.q: Roughly how many eggs can a female edible frog lay in one season?
a: Several hundred to over a thousand
8073.e: A female edible frog can lay several hundred to over a thousand eggs in one breeding season. Even so, only a few of them survive to become adult frogs.
8073.m: Females lay a great many eggs.

8075.q: What is special about the striped hyena's coat?
a: Dark stripes on a pale background
8075.e: The striped hyena has grey to yellowish fur with dark stripes across it. On its neck and back it has a mane that it can raise.
8075.m: Striped hyenas have dark stripes in their fur.

8076.q: Roughly how many species of ladybird are there worldwide?
8076.e: There are many thousands of different ladybird species around the world. They differ in colour, size and number of spots.
8076.m: There are thousands of ladybird species.

8077.q: How can a tapir breathe when it dives underwater?
8077.e: Tapirs are mammals and have lungs. When diving they hold their breath, and sometimes they even walk along the bottom.

8078.q: What does it mean that female fire salamanders release larvae instead of eggs into the water?
a: The eggs develop inside the mother's body
The eggs are buried in the sand
The father carries the eggs on his back
The eggs develop in a bird's nest
8078.e: Unlike many other amphibians, the female does not release eggs but larvae that have already hatched into the water. So the eggs develop inside the mother's body.
8078.m: Larvae are released instead of eggs.

8079.q: What do many wild reindeer do over the course of the year?
a: They stay by the same tree all year
8079.e: Wild reindeer migrate between summer and winter pastures. Some herds cover very long distances.

8080.q: Which sense is especially well developed in the tapir?
8080.e: Tapirs find their way mainly with their nose and ears. Their eyes are rather small and they don't see particularly well.
8080.m: Tapirs rely on their nose and ears.

8081.q: What does a beech marten mainly eat?
a: Mice, birds, eggs, fruit and insects
8081.e: The beech marten eats almost anything and adapts its food to the seasons. In autumn it also likes sweet fruit such as cherries.
8081.m: The beech marten eats almost anything edible.

8082.q: What is the government of a canton usually called?
a: Government Council or Council of State
8082.e: Every canton has its own government. Depending on the canton, it is called the Government Council, the Council of State or something else.
8082.m: A cantonal government is often called the Government Council.

8083.q: What colour is the fur of the edible dormouse usually?
a: Grey fur with a pale belly
8083.e: The edible dormouse usually has grey fur on its back and a paler, almost white belly. This camouflage helps it in the forest.
8083.m: Its fur is grey with a pale belly.

8084.q: What sometimes happens when a squirrel can no longer find the nuts it hid?
a: New trees can grow from the nuts
8084.e: Forgotten nuts can sprout in the ground and grow into new trees. So the squirrel even helps the forest.

8085.q: Why does the robin often sing very early in the morning?
8085.e: With its song, the robin shows other birds that this area belongs to it. It also uses its song to look for a partner.

8086.q: What does the mother rabbit use to line the nest for her young?
8086.e: The mother rabbit plucks out soft fur and lines the nest with it. There the young are nice and warm.
8086.m: The nest is lined with her own fur.

8087.q: What are the young of a fox called?
8087.e: Young foxes are called cubs or kits. They are born in spring in the fox's den.

8088.q: What does the breast of an adult peregrine falcon usually look like?
a: Pale with fine dark bars across it
8088.e: The pale breast is crossed by fine dark bars. This pattern is typical of adult peregrine falcons.

8089.q: In which unit is frequency measured, for example of sound waves or alternating current?
8089.e: Frequency tells you how often something repeats per second, for example how often a wave vibrates. The unit is named after the physicist Heinrich Hertz.

8090.q: How do many blackbirds react when a person approaches in the garden?
a: They fly off quickly with loud calls
They stay completely still and keep singing
8090.e: When someone approaches, the blackbird usually flies off quickly with a loud alarm call. This protects it from possible danger.
8090.m: Blackbirds often flee calling when in danger.

8091.q: What happens to a brown bear's heart rate during its winter rest?
a: It stays exactly the same as in summer
8091.e: During winter rest, the bear's heart rate drops sharply to save energy. Even so, it can quickly become active again if disturbed.
8091.m: In winter rest the bear's heart beats more slowly.

8092.q: What does a ladybird larva look like?
a: Long, dark and a bit like a little crocodile
Soft and woolly like a caterpillar
8092.e: The larva has no spots but is long and dark, often with small orange patches. It looks completely different from the later beetle.

8093.q: Can a common buzzard briefly stay in one spot in the air like a kestrel?
a: Yes, occasionally, but not as skilfully as the kestrel
No, it can't fly at all
Yes, it hovers all day without stopping
8093.e: The common buzzard can occasionally hover briefly, almost flying on the spot, but it is less skilled at it than the kestrel. Usually it prefers to watch from a perch.
8093.m: It can hover, but rarely does.

8094.q: Where do wild budgerigars like to live best?
8094.e: Wild budgerigars like open, dry grassland with bushes. There they find seeds to eat.

8095.q: What is it called when a herd of bison runs off in panic?
8095.e: The word stampede comes from Spanish and describes a wild flight. The whole herd runs together.
8095.m: A panicked mass flight is called a stampede.

8096.q: In which country do bonobos live in the wild?
a: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo
8096.e: Bonobos live only in the rainforest of the Democratic Republic of the Congo in Africa. An important protected area is Salonga National Park.
8096.m: Bonobos live only in the Congo.

8097.q: What shape does the shell of a Roman snail show if you look closely?
8097.e: The Roman snail's shell grows in a beautiful spiral shape. The bigger the snail gets, the bigger the spiral becomes.
8097.m: The shell grows in a spiral.

8098.q: What is the difference between a series circuit and a parallel circuit?
a: In a series circuit the current has only one path, in a parallel circuit several paths
Both are built in exactly the same way
There is no current in a series circuit
8098.e: In a series circuit all the components are connected one after another; if one fails, the whole circuit goes off. In a parallel circuit components have their own paths, so they work independently of each other.
8098.m: A series circuit has one path, a parallel circuit several.

8099.e: Only female wasps have a sting. The male wasps, also called drones, therefore cannot sting.

8100.q: Are you allowed to keep a robin as a pet at home?
a: No, it is a protected wild bird
Yes, but only in a cage
8100.e: Because the robin is a protected wild bird, you are not allowed to catch it and keep it at home. It should live freely in nature.

8102.q: Where does the lowland tapir live?
8102.e: The lowland tapir is found in large parts of South America east of the Andes. It lives in forests and wetlands.
8102.m: Lowland tapirs live in South America.

8103.q: What does the blackbird build its nest from?
8103.e: For its nest, the blackbird collects grass, thin twigs and some mud. This makes the nest firm and cup-shaped.
8103.m: The blackbird's nest is made of grass and mud.

8105.q: Where do giraffe mothers often hide their calves in the first weeks?
a: In tall grass while they go off to feed
In the water of a lake
8105.e: In the first weeks, the calf often lies well hidden in tall grass or bushes. The mother feeds nearby and keeps coming back to suckle it.
8105.m: Giraffe calves hide in tall grass.

8106.q: The sea trout is the same species as the brown trout. What does it do differently?
a: It migrates to the sea and returns to rivers to spawn
It only lives in mountain lakes
8106.e: The sea trout feeds in the sea and grows bigger there. To spawn, it swims into rivers and streams.
8106.m: Sea trout spawn in fresh water.

8108.q: What kind of water does a trout absolutely need to survive?
a: Chlorinated water from the swimming pool
8108.e: Trout need lots of oxygen in the water to breathe well. That is why they prefer to live in fresh, flowing water.

8109.q: What are animals called that eat both meat and plants?
8109.e: Omnivores such as bears or wild boar eat both plant and animal food. Humans are omnivores too.

8110.q: How does the praying mantis usually hunt?
a: It lies in wait without moving and then strikes
It chases its prey for hours
8110.e: The praying mantis often sits completely still for a long time. When prey comes close enough, it grabs it at lightning speed.
8110.m: As an ambush hunter, the mantis waits still and then strikes.

8111.q: Up to what altitude above sea level is the European tree frog still found in Switzerland?
8111.e: In Switzerland, tree frogs are found mainly at lower altitudes, in some places up to around 1,000 metres. They are absent from the high Alpine regions.

8112.q: Which animal sits on a cactus in the centre of the Mexican coat of arms?
8112.e: Mexico's coat of arms shows an eagle sitting on a cactus and eating a snake. It goes back to an Aztec founding legend.
8112.m: Mexico's coat of arms shows an eagle with a snake.

8113.q: Where do jackals usually give birth to their pups?
a: In an earth burrow or a cave
8113.e: Jackals often use burrows in the ground as a place to give birth. There the pups are protected from weather and enemies.
8113.m: The pups grow up in a burrow.

8114.q: Which small animal is a close relative of the edible dormouse and also lives in Switzerland?
8114.e: The edible dormouse and the hazel dormouse both belong to the dormouse family. The hazel dormouse is smaller, has orange-brown fur and also hibernates for a long time.
8114.m: The hazel dormouse is related to the edible dormouse.

8115.q: Which country has the cockerel as a well-known national symbol, the “Gallic rooster”?
8115.e: The “Gallic rooster” is an old symbol of France. You can see it, for example, at sports events as a sign of the French team.

8116.q: What is the pattern on the ring-tailed lemur's tail?
8116.e: The tail has striking black and white rings. That is where the ring-tailed lemur gets its name.
8116.m: The ring-tailed lemur has a ringed tail.

8117.q: How often does the common raven usually use its nest?
a: It is often repaired and added to over several years
Only for a single brood, then never again
Only for a few hours a day
It builds a brand new nest every day
8117.e: Once built, a raven's nest is often used again for years and repaired when needed. This saves energy in the next breeding season.
8117.m: Nests are often reused for years.

8119.q: At what age can young barn swallows usually breed themselves?
a: Usually in their first year of life
Only when they are 20 years old
8119.e: Barn swallows are already able to breed in their first year of life. This is important because their lifespan is rather short anyway.
8119.m: Able to breed in their first year.

8120.q: What do young martens feed on before they eat solid food?
8120.e: Like other mammals, young martens first drink their mother's milk. Only after a few weeks do they start eating solid food such as small prey.
8120.m: Young martens drink their mother's milk first.

8121.q: Which senses help the wels catfish most in murky water?
8121.e: The wels catfish has small eyes and sees poorly. But its barbels and skin are very good at sensing touch and taste.
8121.m: The wels catfish feels its way through the water.

8122.q: On which continents is the red fox naturally common?
a: In large parts of Europe, Asia and North America
Only on a small island in the Pacific
8122.e: The red fox is one of the most widespread predators in the world and lives in large parts of Europe, Asia and North America. Its adaptability makes it very successful.
8122.m: The fox lives on many continents.

8123.q: What does a giraffe like to eat best?
8123.e: Giraffes eat only plants and especially like the leaves of acacias. With their long tongue they skilfully pluck the leaves from between the thorns.

8124.q: When does a red deer stag normally shed its old antlers?
a: Never, it keeps them for ever
8124.e: Towards the end of winter or in spring, the old antlers fall off. Straight afterwards, new ones start to grow.
8124.m: The antlers fall off in spring.

a: The period of time an elected parliament or government is in office
The length of a parliamentary sitting
8125.e: At federal level, a legislative period lasts four years. After that there are elections again.
8125.m: A legislative period is the parliament's term of office.

8126.q: How does the tawny owl usually eat a small mouse?
a: It chews it for a long time with its teeth
It first lets it soften in water
8126.e: The tawny owl usually swallows small prey such as mice whole. It later coughs up the bones and hair as a pellet.
8126.m: Tawny owls swallow small prey whole.

8127.q: A horse's eyes are on the sides of its head. Where can it see with them?
8127.e: Because their eyes are on the sides of the head, horses can see almost all of their surroundings. However, they see poorly right in front of and behind them.
8127.m: Horses see almost all the way round.

8128.q: How exactly does the Roman snail's foot move when it crawls?
8128.e: The snail's foot moves in fine waves from back to front. That is how it pushes itself forward bit by bit.
8128.m: Wave movements push the snail forwards.

8129.q: Which rhinoceros species is the smallest of all?
8129.e: The Sumatran rhino is the smallest of the five rhino species. It lives in dense forests in Asia and has some hair.
8129.m: The Sumatran rhino is the smallest.

8130.q: What is important so that a goldfish pond doesn't get too warm for the fish in summer?
a: Enough shade, for example from plants
Filling it with hot tap water
8130.e: When a pond gets too warm in summer, the water holds less oxygen and the fish suffer. Shade, for example from water lily leaves, helps keep the water cooler.
8130.m: Shade keeps the pond cooler in summer.

8131.q: What does it usually mean when a horse lays its ears back flat?
8131.e: Ears laid back often show that a horse feels uncomfortable or irritated. You should be careful then.
8131.m: Ears laid back show a bad mood.

8132.q: Roughly how much does a female red kite weigh?
8132.e: Female red kites are a little heavier than males and weigh just over a kilogram on average. This is typical of many birds of prey.
8132.m: A female red kite weighs just over a kilo.

8133.q: What is the development of the grasshopper called, in which there is no pupal stage?
8133.e: In grasshoppers, the young already look almost like the adults. They simply grow by shedding their skin, without becoming pupae.
8133.m: The nymph already looks almost like an adult.

8134.q: What is one difference between an elk (moose) and a reindeer?
a: The elk only lives in Africa
8134.e: Elk are much bigger and heavier than reindeer. Reindeer also often live in herds.

8135.q: Why is the okapi hard for researchers to observe?
a: It lives shyly in dense forest
8135.e: Okapis are shy and well camouflaged in the dense rainforest. That is why comparatively little is known about them.
8135.m: Okapis are shy and well hidden.

8136.q: What does the slow worm do in winter?
a: It rests through the winter in a frost-free hiding place
It stays as active as in summer
8136.e: As a cold-blooded animal, it becomes stiff in the cold. It looks for frost-free hiding places, for example in the ground or under stones.
8136.m: In winter it rests hidden from the frost.

8137.q: A rabbit is lying stretched out and calm in its enclosure. How does it usually feel?
a: It is relaxed and feels safe
It wants to play straight away
8137.e: When a rabbit lies stretched out and calm, it feels comfortable and safe. A frightened rabbit, on the other hand, crouches down small.
8137.m: Lying stretched out shows the rabbit is relaxed.

8138.q: What is the difference between the active and the passive right to vote?
a: Active means being allowed to vote, passive means being allowed to be elected
Active means only voting on issues, passive means only electing
8138.e: With the active right to vote, you may cast a vote yourself. With the passive right, you may stand for election yourself.

8139.q: Why doesn't a seahorse like to swim in strong currents?
a: Because it is a weak swimmer and prefers to hold on
Because it is afraid of water
8139.e: Because seahorses swim very slowly, a strong current would simply carry them away. That is why they prefer to hold on to plants with their tail.
8139.m: Better to hold on than swim against the current.

8140.q: What does an orca mainly eat?
a: Fish, seals and other sea animals
8140.e: The orca is a hunter and eats, for example, fish, seals and even other whales. It is a carnivore.

8141.q: How are a starfish's arms arranged?
a: Around a centre, like a star
Two at the front and two at the back
8141.e: A starfish's arms all start from the centre, like the rays of a star. That is why it is called a starfish.
8141.m: Starfish arms spread out from the centre.

8142.q: What is the best way to tell a jaguar's coat from a leopard's?
a: The rosettes usually have spots inside
8142.e: In the jaguar, the rosettes are usually bigger and often contain spots. In the leopard, the rosettes are smaller and usually have no spots inside.
8142.m: Jaguar rosettes often have spots inside.

8143.q: Where do praying mantises mainly live around the world?
a: In warm regions, especially the tropics
8143.e: Most species live in the tropics and subtropics. Only a few are found in temperate areas.

8144.q: How can you tell a stoat from a least weasel?
a: By the black tip of its tail
By its fur colour in summer
8144.e: The least weasel has no black tail tip and is also smaller than the stoat. This feature helps you recognise them in nature.
8144.m: A black tail tip marks the stoat.

8145.q: How loud can a European tree frog's call be?
a: In calm weather it can often be heard kilometres away
8145.e: The mating call of tree frogs is surprisingly loud and carries very far in still weather. Whole choruses of calling males can often be heard from a long way off.

8146.q: Which statement about the Persian leopard is true?
a: It lives mainly in the Caucasus and Iran
It only lives in South America
It lives at the North Pole
8146.e: The Persian leopard is a subspecies found in Western Asia, for example in Iran and the Caucasus. It is one of the biggest subspecies.
8146.m: The Persian leopard lives in Western Asia.

8147.q: What are the little turtles called shortly after hatching?
8147.e: The tiny turtles that have just hatched from the egg are called hatchlings. They set off for the sea straight away.
8147.m: Freshly hatched turtles are called hatchlings.

8148.q: In which European country are there still wild forest reindeer?
8148.e: In Europe, wild forest reindeer live mainly in Finland and Russia. There are no wild reindeer in Switzerland.
8148.m: Wild reindeer live in the far north.

8149.q: What do the scales of a European perch feel like?
a: Rough, because they have tiny teeth on the edge
Soft and slimy, with no scales at all
As big as coins and completely smooth
8149.e: The perch has ctenoid scales with fine little teeth on the edge. That is why its skin feels quite rough.
8149.m: Toothed scales make the perch rough.

8150.q: What does an adult edible frog mainly eat?
a: Insects, spiders and other small invertebrates
8150.e: Adult edible frogs are carnivores and hunt insects, spiders, worms and other small animals. Sometimes they even catch small vertebrates.
8150.m: Edible frogs eat small insects and spiders.

8151.q: Why does the adder often bask on stones?
a: It wants to take in vitamins from stones
8151.e: Its body temperature depends on its surroundings. By basking in the sun it becomes active and can hunt and digest.
8151.m: Cold-blooded animals soak up the sun's warmth.

8153.q: How does the cuckoo's flight differ from a pigeon's?
a: With its pointed wings it looks more like a falcon
It flies much more slowly than a snail
8153.e: The cuckoo has pointed wings and a long tail, which makes it look like a small falcon in flight. Some host birds mistake it for a dangerous bird of prey.
8153.m: A flying cuckoo looks like a falcon.

8154.q: What does a polar bear do to cool down or keep clean?
a: It just shakes itself dry without snow
8154.e: Polar bears like to roll in the snow to clean their fur and cool down. This also keeps their fur well insulating.
8154.m: The polar bear rolls in the snow.

8155.q: How can you often tell which species a ladybird belongs to?
a: By the number and pattern of its spots
By the smell of its feet
By the size of its eyes
By the colour of its antennae
8155.e: Different ladybird species have different numbers of spots and patterns on their wing cases. This helps experts tell the species apart.
8155.m: Spot patterns give away the species.

8156.q: How many toes does a rhinoceros have on each foot?
8156.e: A rhino has three toes on each foot, covered with small hooves. You can see this clearly in its footprints.
8156.m: Rhinos have three toes per foot.

8157.q: What colour are the eyes of adult kestrels usually?
8157.e: The kestrel's eyes are dark brown and very large for the size of its head. These big eyes help it spot prey from far away.

8158.q: Which animal is the polar bear's closest relative?
8158.e: The polar bear is descended from brown bears and is closely related to them. Both belong to the bear family.
8158.m: The brown bear is the closest relative.

8159.q: What role did the hamadryas baboon play in ancient Egypt?
a: It was considered a sacred animal
It was banned as a pet
It was seen only as a pest
8159.e: In ancient Egypt, the hamadryas baboon was linked with the god Thoth and worshipped. It appears in pictures and has been found as mummies.
8159.m: In ancient Egypt it was sacred.

a: A place where people who have fled live for a while
A holiday camp for school classes
8160.e: People who have fled from war or danger find a roof over their heads, food and help from a doctor in a refugee camp.
8160.m: Refugee camps offer protection from danger.

8161.q: What kind of weather do donkeys particularly dislike?
8161.e: Donkeys don't have water-repellent coats like horses and get wet more quickly in the rain. That is why they need a dry shelter.

8162.q: What are the long threads around the mouth of the wels catfish called?
8162.e: The wels catfish has six barbels, two long ones on the upper jaw and four short ones on the lower jaw. It uses them to feel and taste its surroundings.

8163.q: What threatens the little turtles most just after they hatch?
a: Predators such as crabs and birds
Weather that is too cold in summer
8163.e: On the short way from the nest to the water there are many dangers. Sadly, crabs, birds and other animals eat many of the tiny hatchlings.
8163.m: Crabs and birds hunt the hatchlings.

8164.q: How does the beech marten's way of life in towns differ from that in the countryside?
a: In towns it often uses lofts and cars as shelter
In towns it lives only in water
In the countryside it eats only fish
8164.e: In towns and villages, the beech marten adapts and uses buildings and vehicles as shelter. In the countryside it tends to find natural hiding places such as rock crevices.
8164.m: Beech martens adapt easily to towns and villages.

8165.q: What colour are the white stork's feathers usually?
8165.e: The white stork has white feathers, only the wing tips are black. This makes it easy to recognise in the sky.

8166.q: Do wild rabbits usually live alone or in groups?
8166.e: Wild rabbits live sociably together in colonies with many other rabbits. This way they can warn each other of enemies more easily.

8167.q: On which famous building in Basel are peregrine falcons known to breed?
8167.e: A pair of peregrine falcons has been breeding successfully on Basel Minster for years. The brood is often watched there with a camera.
8167.m: Basel Minster is a falcon nesting site.

8168.q: What is special about the beaver's back feet for swimming?
8168.e: The beaver has webbing between the toes of its back feet, which work like paddles. The front feet stay nimble for carrying and building with material.
8168.m: Webbed feet power the beaver along.

8169.q: Roughly how many cats are kept as pets in Switzerland?
8169.e: An estimated well over 1.5 million pet cats live in Switzerland. This makes cats by far the most common pet in the country.
8169.m: Over 1.5 million cats live in Switzerland.

8170.q: What happens to a red deer's antlers every year?
a: They fall off and grow back
They stay the same for ever
8170.e: Every spring the stag sheds its old antlers. Then new, often bigger ones grow back.

8171.q: Roughly how many chicken breeds are there worldwide?
8171.e: Over time, a great many different chicken breeds have been bred around the world. They differ in size, colour and feathers.
8171.m: There are very many chicken breeds.

8172.q: Against whom did the Communist Party of China fight in the Chinese Civil War before taking power in 1949?
8172.e: From 1927 to 1949 the communists and the nationalist Kuomintang fought for power in China. In the end the communists won, and the Kuomintang fled to Taiwan.
8172.m: The communists defeated the Kuomintang in 1949.

8174.q: What does a grasshopper like to eat best?
8174.e: Most grasshoppers eat plants. They like fresh green grass.

8175.q: How does a mother cheetah communicate with her cubs?
8175.e: Mother cheetahs call their cubs with special chirping sounds that sound like birdsong. This way mother and cubs find each other even in tall grass.
8175.m: Cheetahs call each other with chirps.

8176.q: What are materials called that conduct electric current well?
8176.e: Conductors such as metals let electric current flow through easily. Insulators such as rubber or plastic do the opposite and block the current.

8177.q: What is the large national park in Tanzania called, where especially many lions live?
8177.e: Many lion prides live in the Serengeti National Park in Tanzania. There are huge herds of zebras and wildebeest there as prey.
8177.m: The Serengeti is known for its many lions.

8178.q: What is an animal called that comes from a male horse and a female donkey?
8178.e: Crossing a male horse with a female donkey produces a hinny. It looks similar to a mule but is a little different.
8178.m: Male horse plus female donkey makes a hinny.

8179.q: Roughly how many eggs does a female sand lizard lay per clutch?
8179.e: The number varies with the size and age of the female but is usually in this range. Some females even lay twice a year.
8179.m: A clutch has about 5 to 14 eggs.

8180.q: Which prey animals do spotted hyenas often hunt?
8180.e: Hunting in groups, spotted hyenas also catch large hoofed animals such as wildebeest and zebras. They often attack young animals.
8180.m: Spotted hyenas hunt wildebeest and zebras.

8181.q: How does a praying mantis usually hang when it sheds its skin?
a: Upside down from something to hold on to
Lying on its back in water
Sitting on a stone in the sun
8181.e: Hanging upside down, it can easily slip out of its old skin. Afterwards its new body has to harden.

8182.q: Roughly how old can dolphins such as the bottlenose dolphin get?
8182.e: Bottlenose dolphins can often live 40 to 50 years in the wild. That is quite a long life for a sea animal.
8182.m: Bottlenose dolphins often live over 40 years.

8183.q: What is dabbling, as many ducks do it?
a: Looking for food with the head underwater and tail in the air
Running very fast across the water
Swimming in circles around other ducks
Beating the water with the wings
8183.e: When dabbling, the duck puts its head and neck underwater while its tail sticks up in the air. This lets it reach plants and small animals on the bottom.
8183.m: When dabbling, the head goes under.

8184.q: What do two like magnetic poles do when you bring them together?
8184.e: Two north poles or two south poles push each other away. Only different poles attract each other.
8184.m: Like poles push each other away.

8185.q: What does a Roman snail like to eat best?
8185.e: Roman snails mainly eat leaves, lettuce and other plants. But they can also eat wilted plant remains.
8185.m: Snails like to eat green plants.

8186.q: What helped Swiss lakes to recover?
a: Cutting down the trees on the shore
8186.e: Sewage treatment plants hold back phosphorus from waste water. This means less of it gets into the lakes, and the water became cleaner again.
8186.m: Sewage treatment plants made the lakes clean again.

8187.q: Roughly how old can a blackbird get in the wild?
a: Often only a few years, some over 10 years
8187.e: Many blackbirds live only a few years because life in nature is dangerous. But some blackbirds manage to live more than ten years.
8187.m: Blackbirds often live only a few years.

8188.q: How does the ibex's coat change over the year?
a: In summer it is rather brownish, in winter thicker and greyish brown
It stays jet black all year
It turns white in summer like a mountain hare's
It loses all its hair in winter
8188.e: In summer the ibex has a short, rather brownish coat; in winter it grows a thicker, greyish brown winter coat. This protects it well from the cold.
8188.m: The coat adapts to the seasons.

8189.q: Which large group of whales does the blue whale belong to?
8189.e: The blue whale belongs to the baleen whales because it has baleen plates instead of teeth. Sperm whales, on the other hand, are toothed whales.

8190.q: How many eggs does a female peregrine falcon usually lay per brood?
8190.e: The female usually lays three to four eggs in the nest hollow. Both parents then help care for the brood.
8190.m: Usually three to four eggs per brood.

8191.q: How soon after birth can a dromedary calf stand up?
8191.e: Dromedary young are well developed at birth. The calf can soon stand and follow its mother.

8192.q: What is a young Bactrian camel called?
8192.e: Young camels are called calves. They can stand and walk shortly after birth.

8193.q: What does the wood mouse do to protect itself from enemies?
a: It digs lots of escape tunnels in its burrow
It plays dead and lies still for days
8193.e: Its burrow has several tunnels so that it can escape quickly when an enemy comes.

8194.q: Which beetle species lives in Switzerland alongside the common cockchafer?
8194.e: In Central Europe there are the common cockchafer and the forest cockchafer. They look similar but differ in the tip of the abdomen.
8194.m: The common and forest cockchafers are related.

8195.q: What do young common ravens that don't have a partner yet often form?
a: Strict territories of their own while still young
Permanent family groups with their parents
No groups, they always live alone
8195.e: Young ravens that have not yet found a partner often join together in large groups. In these groups they look for food together.

8196.q: What do chimpanzees often use as a tool to get food?
8196.e: Chimpanzees are clever and use sticks, for example, to get at food. This is called tool use.

8197.q: What happens to the prey a sand lizard has caught?
a: It is usually eaten straight away, whole or in pieces
It is taken to the young in the nest
It is washed in water first
8197.e: The sand lizard eats its prey right after catching it, often breaking it up with a few bites. It does not store food and does not look after its young.
8197.m: Prey is eaten at once, not stored.

8198.q: What is the status of the stag beetle in Switzerland?
a: The most common beetle of all
8198.e: It is protected because old oak forests and dead wood have become rare. You are not allowed to catch or kill it.
8198.m: Stag beetles are protected and endangered.

8199.q: Roughly how long can an okapi live in captivity?
8199.e: In zoos, okapis often live to around 20 years. Wild animals usually don't live quite as long.

8200.q: How far away can the loud chorus of edible frogs sometimes be heard?
a: Often from far off, over many metres
Never more than a centimetre away
8200.e: The croaking of many edible frogs together at a pond can often be heard from far away. Especially on warm evenings, the chorus carries a long way.
8200.m: An edible frog chorus can often be heard far away.

8201.q: What behaviour do swifts often show on warm summer evenings above towns, recognisable by their loud calls?
a: They fly around in loud, screaming groups
They sit quietly on roofs and sing softly
They look for water to drink together on the ground
They build a huge nest together
8201.e: Such screaming group flights are typical summer behaviour. The birds often hunt insects together high up.
8201.m: In the evening, swifts often scream in groups.

8202.q: What was the feared secret police of East Germany called?
8202.e: The Stasi secretly watched many people in East Germany. Its job was to stop criticism of the government.
8202.m: The Stasi spied on East German citizens.

8203.q: What is an important difference between a roe deer and a red deer?
a: The roe deer is much smaller
The roe deer is bigger than a red deer
8203.e: Roe deer and red deer look a little alike, but the roe deer is much smaller. The roebuck's antlers are also smaller than the stag's.
8203.m: Roe deer are smaller than red deer.

a: During the day and also at night
Only at midday in the greatest heat
8204.e: African buffaloes can feed both by day and by night. In great heat, they move their feeding to cooler hours.
8204.m: Buffaloes often eat at night too.

8205.q: What does immunity mean for members of parliament?
a: During their term they are protected from certain prosecutions
They don't have to pay taxes
8205.e: Immunity protects members of parliament from being prosecuted for what they say in the chamber. This way they can speak their minds freely.
8205.m: Immunity protects members of parliament while in office.

8206.q: Roughly how big are most aphids?
8206.e: Most aphids are only a few millimetres long. You usually see them in large groups on shoots.
8206.m: Aphids are only a few millimetres long.

8207.q: Why is a lack of oxygen on the lake bed dangerous for whitefish spawn?
a: The eggs lie on the bottom and can suffocate
The eggs melt in the water
8207.e: The eggs need oxygen to develop. If there is none on the bottom, the embryos die.

8208.q: On which continent does the American bison naturally live?
8208.e: The American bison used to live in large herds on the prairies of North America. Today there are still herds there in protected areas and on farms.
8208.m: The American bison comes from North America.

8209.q: Roughly how much does a kestrel weigh?
8209.e: Depending on whether it is male or female, a kestrel weighs about 150 to 300 grams. Females are usually a little heavier than males.
8209.m: A kestrel weighs only a few hundred grams.

8210.q: What does the barn swallow's nest look like compared to the house martin's?
a: It is open at the top like a small bowl
It is completely closed with a small hole
It hangs freely from a branch
8210.e: The barn swallow's nest is open at the top and bowl-shaped. The house martin, on the other hand, builds a closed nest with a small entrance hole.
8210.m: An open bowl nest, unlike the house martin's.

8211.q: How is the eel classified by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)?
8211.e: The European eel has declined sharply and is considered critically endangered. The reasons are overfishing, weirs and diseases.
8211.m: The European eel is severely threatened.

8213.q: How did the canton of Jura come about?
a: Through a popular vote in which areas separated from the canton of Bern
Through a decision by the UN
Through a merger of two cantons
8213.e: In 1978 the Swiss people agreed to the creation of a new canton, after parts of the canton of Bern had decided to separate. The canton of Jura was officially founded in 1979.
8213.m: The canton of Jura was created by a vote in 1979.

8214.q: Which is the largest wild cat in Switzerland?
8214.e: Two wild cat species live in Switzerland: the lynx and the much smaller European wildcat. The lynx was wiped out and reintroduced from the 1970s onwards.
8214.m: The lynx is Switzerland's largest wild cat.

8215.q: What does a sheep show when it lies calmly in the meadow, chewing contentedly?
a: It is ill and needs a vet immediately
8215.e: When a sheep lies calmly and contentedly chews its food a second time, it is usually doing well. It is a sign of relaxation.
8215.m: Calm chewing shows the sheep is content.

8216.q: Why should you keep an adult golden hamster on its own?
a: Because it often attacks other hamsters
Because otherwise it eats too much
8216.e: Golden hamsters are loners and usually don't get on with other hamsters as adults. They then fight each other.
8216.m: Golden hamsters prefer to live alone.

8217.q: What is the little house called where a dog can live outdoors?
8217.e: A kennel protects the dog from rain, wind and cold. It is usually small and cosy.
8217.m: Outdoors, a dog lives in a kennel.

8218.q: Apart from grey, what colour do some female cuckoos have that males don't?
8218.e: Some female cuckoos have a reddish brown colour form that does not occur in males. This makes them look a little different from the grey males.

8219.q: How do bumblebees mainly communicate in the nest?
8219.e: Bumblebees signal to each other in the nest through touch and scents. They don't do the famous waggle dance of honeybees.

8220.q: Where does the blackbird like to build its nest best?
a: In open meadows with no cover
8220.e: Blackbirds like to build their nests hidden in bushes or hedges. There the eggs and chicks are well protected.

8221.q: Roughly how much does an adult hedgehog weigh in summer?
8221.e: A healthy adult hedgehog usually weighs between 700 grams and one and a half kilograms in summer. Before hibernation it puts on a good amount of weight.
8221.m: Hedgehogs usually weigh under two kilograms.

8222.q: Roughly how long is a young okapi suckled?
8222.e: The mother suckles her calf for several months. After that it eats more and more plants.
8222.m: Okapi calves drink milk for months.

8223.q: What is often involved when a llama spits?
8223.e: The saliva is often mixed with stomach contents. It smells unpleasant.
8223.m: Llama spit often contains stomach contents.

8225.q: When is the European pond turtle active?
8225.e: It needs the sun to warm up and is therefore active during the day. At night it usually rests in the water or in a hiding place.
8225.m: Pond turtles are active by day.

8226.q: How do leopards usually move around?
a: On four paws, quietly and smoothly
8226.e: Leopards walk on soft paws into which they can pull their claws. This lets them move almost silently.

8228.q: Where is a good place to watch pond skaters?
a: On the bank of a calm pond in sunshine
8228.e: In warm weather the insects are easy to see on the surface of the water. If you keep still, you can watch them glide and hunt.
8228.m: Calm ponds are good places to watch them.

8229.q: Why are pigs considered clean animals despite their mud baths?
a: They clearly separate their sleeping, eating and toilet areas
They wash with soap every day
They don't like mud at all
They clean themselves with their tongue like cats
8229.e: In their pen, pigs pay close attention to where they sleep, eat and go to the toilet. This clear separation shows their natural cleanliness.
8229.m: Pigs keep sleeping and toilet areas apart.

8230.q: What is the European relative of the American bison called?
8230.e: The wisent is the largest land mammal in Europe. It is the closest living relative of the American bison.

8231.q: What does a bee need its antennae for?
8231.e: With its antennae, the bee smells the scent of flowers and feels its surroundings. This is also how bees find their way in the dark hive.
8231.m: Antennae are for smelling and feeling.

8232.q: Roughly how many brown bears live worldwide, if you add up rough estimates?
8232.e: The number of brown bears worldwide is estimated at several hundred thousand. Most of them live in Russia and North America.
8232.m: There are several hundred thousand brown bears worldwide.

8233.q: Where are you most likely to see dragonflies in Switzerland?
a: At ponds, lakes and slow streams
8233.e: Dragonflies need water for their development. You often see them on banks, in bogs and in marshy areas.

8234.q: What is the process called in which cells turn glucose into energy with the help of oxygen?
8234.e: In cellular respiration, cells use oxygen to get energy from glucose. Carbon dioxide and water are produced as by-products.
8234.m: Cellular respiration gets energy from glucose.

8235.q: What sound does a pig typically make?
8235.e: Pigs make grunting sounds to communicate with each other. This way they show, for example, whether they are content.

8236.q: How many ducklings usually hatch from a mallard's clutch?
8236.e: Since a clutch usually has eight to twelve eggs, that many ducklings hatch too. But not all of them always survive until they are grown up.
8236.m: Usually many ducklings hatch at once.

8237.q: How does a sheepdog help the shepherd with the flock?
a: It drives the sheep in the right direction
It eats grass together with the sheep
8237.e: A well-trained sheepdog runs around the flock and drives the sheep in the direction the shepherd wants. That way the shepherd doesn't have to run himself.

8239.q: Is the slow worm dangerous to people?
a: No, it is harmless and not venomous
Yes, it stings with its tail
8239.e: It is not venomous and is shy. It tries to escape rather than bite.
8239.m: Slow worms are harmless and not venomous.

8240.q: What does the honeybee collect from flowers?
8240.e: The bee flies from flower to flower collecting sweet nectar and flower dust, called pollen. Later it makes honey from it.

8241.q: Which group of birds does the swift belong to?
8241.e: The swift belongs to the group of birds that also includes the hummingbirds. Despite looking similar, it is not closely related to swallows.
8241.m: Swifts belong to their own bird group.

8242.q: What helps many sharks not to sink in the water?
a: A swim bladder full of air
Air that stays in the gills
8242.e: Sharks have no swim bladder. Their large liver is full of oil, which is lighter than water, and helps them not to sink.
8242.m: The liver helps the shark float.

8243.q: What is the polar bear's thick layer of fat for?
a: It keeps it warm in the cold
8243.e: The thick layer of fat under the fur protects the polar bear from the extreme cold. Without it, it would freeze in the Arctic.
8243.m: Fat protects the polar bear from the cold.

8244.q: Who invented printing with movable type?
8244.e: Around 1450 Johannes Gutenberg developed printing with movable type. This meant books could be made much faster.

8245.q: What does the veto in the UN Security Council mean?
a: A permanent member can block a resolution on its own
Every country in the world has a veto
The veto only applies to economic questions
It is the right to postpone meetings
8245.e: China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the USA can prevent a Security Council resolution with a single no vote. This veto makes reforms of the Security Council very difficult.
8245.m: Permanent members can block with a veto.

8246.q: What pattern do meerkats have on their backs?
8246.e: Several dark stripes run across the back. The basic colour of the fur is sandy to light brown.
8246.m: The back has dark stripes across it.

8247.q: Which group of animals does the wood mouse belong to?
8247.e: The wood mouse is a rodent, just like squirrels and hamsters. Its teeth keep on growing.
8247.m: The wood mouse is a rodent.

8248.q: How can you often recognise a female mallard in flight?
a: By her loud quacking and brown feathers
By black dots above the eye
8248.e: Even in flight, you can recognise the female by her plain brown feathers. You also often hear her loud quacking.
8248.m: Brown feathers show it's a female.

8249.q: What is meant by transpiration in plants?
a: Giving off water vapour through the leaves
Taking in carbon dioxide through the roots
8249.e: Plants constantly lose water through tiny openings in their leaves, the stomata. This process helps to carry water and nutrients from the roots up into the leaves.
8249.m: In transpiration plants lose water through their leaves.

8250.q: How does the African wild dog usually hunt?
a: As a team in a pack
Only at night in the water
8250.e: The animals hunt together and often chase their prey for a long time. Thanks to their teamwork they are very successful.
8250.m: Hunting together makes wild dogs successful.

8251.q: How does the slow worm move around?
a: It hops on its back legs
8251.e: It glides over the ground by moving its body from side to side. It has no legs.

8253.q: Which sex is usually a little heavier in the common buzzard?
a: Both always weigh exactly the same
8253.e: In most birds of prey, including the common buzzard, the female is a little bigger and heavier than the male. This kind of difference between the sexes is common in birds of prey.
8253.m: Females are usually a little heavier.

8254.q: How well does a lynx see at night?
a: Very well, much better than a human
Not at all, it is blind then
8254.e: Large eyes and a light-sensitive retina give the lynx excellent night vision. This lets it hunt well even in low light.
8254.m: A night hunter with sharp eyes.

8255.q: Which threat to the great crested grebe's habitat is particularly important in Switzerland?
a: The loss of reed beds on lakes
Climate that is too cold in summer
8255.e: Reed beds offer important habitat and nesting sites, but they are shrinking on many lakes in Switzerland. This threatens the great crested grebe's chances of breeding.
8255.m: Less reed means fewer nesting sites.

8256.q: Roughly how long are jackals pregnant?
8256.e: Jackals are pregnant for about 60 days. That is similar to many other members of the dog family.
8256.m: Jackal pregnancy lasts around two months.

8257.q: What was the “Great Leap Forward” under Mao Zedong?
a: A failed attempt to industrialise China quickly, which caused a devastating famine
A reform of the education system
8257.e: Between 1958 and 1962 Mao tried to modernise China rapidly through collectivisation and industrialisation. The policy failed and led to a famine with millions of deaths.
8257.m: The Great Leap was a failed policy that led to a famine.

8258.q: What effect did the selective breeding of many pedigree dogs from the 19th century onwards have on their genetic diversity?
a: In many breeds it fell sharply because of breeding for outward features
It rose sharply as a result
Pedigree dogs have stayed genetically identical to wild wolves
There was no effect at all on genetics
8258.e: Strict breed standards and frequent inbreeding within small populations reduced the genetic diversity of many modern dog breeds. This can encourage certain inherited diseases within a breed.

8259.q: Where is the pill woodlouse sometimes kept as a pet?
a: In terrariums, as a floor cleaner
8259.e: In terrariums, woodlice help break down leftovers and scraps of food. This keeps the floor cleaner.

8260.q: What does the barn swallow mainly eat?
8260.e: The barn swallow feeds almost entirely on flying insects such as mosquitoes and flies. It catches them directly in the air.
8260.m: Flying insects are its main food.

8261.q: Where do gorillas live in the wild?
a: In the jungle of South America
8261.e: Gorillas live only in Central Africa, in dense rainforests. There they find lots of plants to eat.

8262.q: Why is the hedgehog useful in the garden?
a: It loosens the soil like an earthworm
8262.e: The hedgehog likes to eat slugs, beetles and other garden pests. That is why many gardeners are happy when a hedgehog visits.
8262.m: Hedgehogs eat lots of garden pests.

8263.q: How does the colour of the red kite's head look compared to the rest of its body?
a: Just as reddish brown as the body
8263.e: The red kite's head is much paler than its reddish brown body and looks almost greyish white. This helps when identifying it in the field.
8263.m: The red kite has a pale head.

8264.q: What should you do if you see an adder in nature?
a: Stay calm and keep your distance
Pick it up by the tail
Scream loudly and run towards it
8264.e: The snake is shy and only bites if it feels threatened. If you keep your distance, you are safe.
8264.m: Keep your distance and nothing will happen.

8265.q: What does a hamster show when it lies on its side breathing very calmly?
8265.e: A hamster sleeping in a relaxed way often lies very still on its side. This is completely normal and shows deep sleep.
8265.m: Hamsters lying still are just sleeping.

8266.q: Which animal is considered the largest land animal in the world?
8266.e: No other land animal gets as big and heavy as the African elephant. It is even heavier than giraffes and rhinos.
8266.m: The elephant is the largest land animal.

8267.q: What are young leopards like straight after birth?
a: Almost as big as their mother
8267.e: Newborn leopards are blind and must be hidden and cared for by their mother. They only open their eyes after a few days.

8268.q: Which animal is shown on the coat of arms of the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden?
8268.e: Like Appenzell Innerrhoden, Appenzell Ausserrhoden also has an upright black bear on its coat of arms. The two cantons used to be a single canton of Appenzell.
8268.m: Ausserrhoden also has a bear on its coat of arms.

8269.q: Where do harbour seals like to rest?
a: On high rocks in the mountains
8269.e: At low tide, harbour seals like to lie together on sandbanks that stick out of the water. There they rest and warm up in the sun.

8270.q: What do blackbirds sometimes do in the garden on cold winter days?
a: They look for food at bird feeders
8270.e: On cold days, blackbirds like to visit bird feeders when there are hardly any worms left in the ground. There they find apples or other scraps.
8270.m: In winter, blackbirds also visit bird feeders.

8271.q: What does an edible frog often use to catch small prey?
a: Its quick tongue or a fast snap of its mouth
8271.e: Edible frogs often snap up prey at lightning speed with their mouth or tongue. Small insects hardly have a chance to escape.
8271.m: Tongue and mouth catch prey lightning fast.

8272.q: Where does the grass snake often hide during the day?
a: Under stones and piles of wood
8272.e: There it finds protection and warmth. Piles of branches and walls are also popular spots.
8272.m: Hiding places offer protection and warmth.

8273.q: In which layer of the atmosphere is the ozone layer?
8273.e: The stratosphere lies above the troposphere, where the weather happens. It contains the ozone layer, which filters UV radiation.
8273.m: The ozone layer is in the stratosphere.

8274.q: Why do many people in Switzerland like fishing for trout?
a: Because they are kept as pets
Because they are pests in the stream
8274.e: Many people like the taste of trout, so it is often caught. In Switzerland there are special fishing rules and seasons for it.
8274.m: Trout are popular fish to catch and eat.

8275.q: What is the best description of the golden eagle's overall appearance?
a: A large, powerful bird of prey with dark feathers
A water bird with webbed feet
8275.e: The golden eagle is a large, powerfully built bird of prey with mostly dark brown feathers and a golden brown shimmer on its neck. These features make it easy to recognise.
8275.m: It is a large, dark bird of prey.

8276.q: Where does a pike often stay in winter?
a: In deeper parts of the water
In the treetops on the bank
8276.e: In winter, pike often withdraw to deeper, calmer parts of the lake. There the water is more even and more sheltered.
8276.m: In winter, pike look for deep water.

8277.q: What sound does a chamois make to warn others of danger?
8277.e: When in danger, a chamois gives a sharp, whistling sound. This warning whistle immediately alarms the whole group.
8277.m: Chamois warn with a loud whistle.

8278.q: Roughly how old can a chicken get?
8278.e: When well looked after, chickens can get surprisingly old. Some even live longer than ten years.

8279.q: Roughly how long does an alpine marmot hibernate?
8279.e: From autumn to spring, marmots spend around half the year hibernating. This is how they survive the cold time in the mountains when there is little food.
8279.m: Hibernation lasts almost half a year.

8281.q: What is the famous opera about a magpie that supposedly steals called?
8281.e: The opera “La gazza ladra” (The Thieving Magpie) was written by the Italian composer Gioachino Rossini. It is about the popular belief that magpies steal.

8282.q: What feature do baboons have compared to great apes?
8282.e: Baboons have a tail, while great apes such as gorillas and chimpanzees do not. In baboons the tail is often curved upwards.
8282.m: Baboons have tails, great apes don't.

8283.q: Why should you be careful when lending money to a friend?
a: You might not get it back
8283.e: If you lend money, you might not get it back, and that can lead to an argument. So you should think carefully.
8283.m: Money you lend does not always come back.

8284.q: When is the common earwig mainly active?
a: Only in the depths of winter
8284.e: The earwig is active at night. During the day it usually hides.

8285.q: How do dolphins communicate with each other?
a: With the colours of their skin
8285.e: Dolphins make lots of different sounds, for example whistles and clicks. They use them to exchange information.
8285.m: Dolphins talk with whistles and clicks.

8286.q: What is the young of a bison called?
8286.e: Bison cows usually have a single calf. It is fed on milk.
8286.m: A young bison is called a calf.

8287.q: What is it called when a budgerigar loses its old feathers and new ones grow?
8287.e: When moulting, the budgie gradually swaps its old feathers for new ones. This happens regularly throughout its life.

8288.q: Which animal is the smallest of the South American camels?
8288.e: The vicuña is the smallest member of the camel family. It lives wild in the highlands of the Andes.
8288.m: The vicuña is the smallest camel.

8289.q: Which large bird often stands motionless in the water and catches trout?
8289.e: The grey heron waits quietly in shallow water. Then it strikes like lightning with its long beak.
8289.m: The grey heron lies in wait in shallow water.

8290.q: How does the grey heron's flight differ from the stork's?
a: The heron pulls its neck in, the stork stretches it out
8290.e: In flight, the grey heron is easy to recognise by its pulled-in neck. The stork, on the other hand, always stretches its neck straight forwards when flying.
8290.m: Neck in means heron, neck out means stork.

8291.q: In which city is CERN, the world’s largest research centre for particle physics?
8291.e: CERN is on the border between Switzerland and France, near Geneva. There scientists use a huge particle accelerator to study the structure of matter.

8292.q: Where are baby hippos often born?
8292.e: Hippo mothers often give birth to their calves in shallow water. The baby can then swim or move underwater almost straight away.
8292.m: Baby hippos are often born in water.

8293.q: What does it show when guinea pigs make quiet gurgling or rumbling sounds?
a: They are content or chatting with each other
8293.e: Guinea pigs have many different sounds they use to communicate. A quiet gurgle or rumble often sounds content and relaxed.

8294.q: From which wildcat species is the domestic cat probably descended?
a: From the African wildcat (Felis silvestris lybica)
From the European wildcat (Felis silvestris silvestris)
8294.e: Genetic studies show that the domestic cat is descended mainly from the African wildcat. This subspecies of wildcat was already living near human settlements thousands of years ago.
8294.m: The African wildcat is the ancestor of the domestic cat.

8295.q: What happens to the stoat's winter coat in areas with little snow?
a: It stays partly brown or patchy
8295.e: In mild areas with little snow, a completely white coat is less useful as camouflage. There, some stoats keep a patchy brown and white in-between coat.
8295.m: Where there is little snow, the stoat has a patchy coat.

8296.q: Roughly how many penguin species are there in the world?
8296.e: There are about 18 different penguin species in the world. They differ in size, colour and habitat.

8297.q: Which European animal is considered one of the smallest predators of all?
8297.e: The least weasel is Europe's smallest predator and usually weighs only about 30 to 250 grams. Despite its small size, it is a skilful hunter.
8297.m: The least weasel is tiny but fierce.

8298.q: Why are you not allowed to destroy a red wood ant mound?
a: Because the wood ant is protected
Because it belongs to the forester
Because a fox is sleeping under it
8298.e: The red wood ant is protected in Switzerland. Its nests must not be destroyed.

8299.q: When are young foxes usually born?
a: In the middle of winter in the snow
8299.e: Most fox cubs are born in March or April. Then it is warm enough and there will soon be more food again.

8300.q: Roughly how many eggs can a female housefly lay at once?
8300.e: A female usually lays around a hundred eggs at a time. She does this several times in her life.
8300.m: Flies lay many eggs at once.

8301.q: Where are the pike's eyes usually?
a: Only one, hidden in the mouth
8301.e: The pike's eyes are high up on its head. This lets it look forwards and upwards well while lying in its hiding place.
8301.m: Pike eyes sit high on the head.

8302.q: Which sex usually has the larger ossicones?
a: Both are always the same size
8302.e: Male giraffes often have thicker and balder ossicones than females. This is because they butt heads more often when fighting.

8303.q: Which group of animals does the grass snake belong to?
8303.e: The grass snake is a snake and belongs to the reptiles. It has dry, scaly skin and lays eggs.

8304.e: Hedgehogs are surprisingly good swimmers. They sometimes use this to cross a pond, for example.

8305.q: What kind of coat do many Swiss goat breeds have compared to many sheep?
8305.e: Many local goats have a short, smooth coat, while sheep often have thick wool. This makes them easy to tell apart.
8305.m: Goat hair is usually short and smooth.

8306.q: How does a meerkat usually stand when keeping watch?
a: Flat on its belly in the sand
8306.e: Meerkats stand up on their back legs and often prop themselves up with their tail. This gives them a good view.
8306.m: Meerkats stand upright to keep watch.

8307.q: Why is the ivory trade banned in many countries?
a: Because there are too many elephants
8307.e: Elephants are killed illegally for their ivory. Bans are meant to protect their numbers.

a: A border meant to stop East German citizens fleeing to the West.
A tourist attraction from the start.
A bridge between East and West.
8308.e: The Berlin Wall was built by East Germany in 1961 to stop people escaping to the West. Many people died trying to get across it.
8308.m: The Wall stopped people escaping to freedom.

8309.q: How do ibex mainly communicate with each other?
a: Mainly through posture and gestures, less through sounds
Only by loud roaring over long distances
By changing the colour of their coat
8309.e: Ibex are rather quiet animals and communicate mainly through posture, head movements and looks. Loud calls are rather rare.
8309.m: Body language matters more than calls.

8310.q: How does the common raven's beak differ from a carrion crow's?
a: It is much bigger and stronger
It is much smaller and more pointed
It is a different colour, bright red
The raven has almost no beak
8310.e: Compared to the carrion crow's, the raven's beak is strikingly massive and strong. With it, it can also deal with tough carrion and bigger prey.
8310.m: Its beak is bigger than the crow's.

8311.q: Where does the bearded vulture usually build its nest?
a: In rock niches on high cliffs
On the ground in the forest
8311.e: Bearded vultures build their large nests sheltered on steep cliffs. There they are well protected from enemies.

8312.q: Is the koala a rodent like a mouse?
a: Yes, it is a large rodent
Yes, it belongs to the mouse family
8312.e: Even if you might sometimes think so, the koala is not a rodent. Instead, it belongs to the marsupials.

8314.q: In which protected area on the North Sea do especially many harbour seals live?
8314.e: The Wadden Sea on the North Sea coast is a large protected area with a great many harbour seals. There are sandbanks there where they can rest.
8314.m: Many harbour seals live in the Wadden Sea.

8315.q: What does it mean when people say African wild dogs are very social?
a: They stick closely together and help each other
They fight each other all the time
8315.e: Social means that the animals live closely together and support each other. This shows in hunting, raising young and caring for each other.

8317.q: Why are regular, competitive elections seen as an important protection against dictatorship?
a: They allow a peaceful change of power and limit terms of office.
They guarantee that the same party always wins.
They prevent any criticism of the government.
8317.e: When elections are free and fair, the people can vote out incompetent or abusive governments. This prevents a single person from holding unchecked power permanently.
8317.m: Fair elections make a change of power possible.

8318.q: How does the severed tail of a common wall lizard often react right after it comes off?
a: It keeps twitching for a while and distracts enemies
It vanishes without a trace immediately
It instantly becomes a new animal
8318.e: The muscles in the severed tail keep moving for a few seconds. This movement distracts the enemy from the fleeing lizard.
8318.m: The tail twitches as a distraction.

8319.q: Which part of the stoat's body stays black all year round?
8319.e: Whether summer or winter, the tip of the stoat's tail always stays black. This helps researchers tell it apart from similar animals.
8319.m: The tail tip is always black.

8320.q: How old do stoats usually get in the wild?
8320.e: In nature, stoats often live only 1 to 2 years because they have many enemies. In captivity, some animals can live a little longer.

8321.q: Which two parts make up a tortoise's or turtle's shell?
a: The upper shell and the belly shell
A head shell and a tail shell
An inner shell and an outer shell
A front shell and a back shell
8321.e: The domed upper shell protects the back, the flat belly shell the underside. The two are joined at the sides.
8321.m: The shell has a back part and a belly part.

8322.q: How many eggs does a female grey heron usually lay per brood?
8322.e: A grey heron's clutch usually has three to five pale bluish green eggs. Both parents then look after the brood.
8322.m: She usually lays three to five eggs.

8323.q: What is typical of the lynx's side whiskers (cheek ruff)?
a: Long hair on the cheeks that makes the face look wider
They fall out completely in summer
8323.e: The cheek ruff gives the lynx's head its striking look. Both males and females have this eye-catching hair on their face.
8323.m: The cheek ruff shapes the lynx's face.

8324.q: What do newly hatched kingfisher chicks look like?
8324.e: The chicks hatch blind and naked and depend completely on their parents. Only after a few weeks do they get feathers and open their eyes.

8325.q: In which habitats does the common raven feel especially at home?
a: In forests, mountains and increasingly in farmland
Only in big cities with skyscrapers
8325.e: The common raven is very adaptable and lives in all kinds of habitats. From dense forests to rocky mountain regions, it finds suitable places.
8325.m: It lives in forests, mountains and farmland.

8326.q: Which tree is the stag beetle particularly closely linked to?
a: The maple in the high mountains
8326.e: Oaks provide sap for the beetles and rotting wood for the larvae. That is why in German it is also called the “oak beetle”.
8326.m: The stag beetle is closely linked to oaks.

8327.q: Is the European badger closely related to the otter?
a: Yes, both belong to the weasel family
No, it is related to fish
8327.e: Badgers and otters both belong to the large weasel family. Even so, they live very differently; the otter, for example, lives mainly in the water.
8327.m: Badgers and otters both belong to the weasel family.

8328.q: What role do organisations such as the Swiss Ornithological Institute in Sempach play for the eagle owl in Switzerland?
a: They support the protection and reintroduction of the eagle owl
They only catch eagle owls for zoos
They fight the eagle owl as a pest
They have nothing to do with the eagle owl
8328.e: Organisations such as the Swiss Ornithological Institute in Sempach support the protection and monitoring of the eagle owl in Switzerland. Thanks to such programmes, populations have been able to recover.
8328.m: The institute supports eagle owl protection projects.

8329.q: Where does the European garden spider usually wait for prey?
a: In the middle of its web
8329.e: The garden spider often sits right in the middle of its web. From there it immediately feels when something gets caught.
8329.m: It waits in the middle of the web.

8330.q: What is a hike called on which a donkey carries the luggage?
8330.e: On a donkey trek, people hike together with a donkey that carries the heavy things. This is especially popular in the mountains.
8330.m: That is what hiking with donkeys is called.

8331.q: Roughly how tall is an adult wolf at the shoulder?
8331.e: At the shoulder, wolves reach a height of about 70 to 90 centimetres. This makes them much bigger than most pet dogs.
8331.m: Wolves are up to 90 cm tall at the shoulder.

8332.q: What is typical of the African wild dog's coat?
a: Every animal has its own pattern of patches
It has stripes like a zebra
All the animals look exactly the same
8332.e: The coat is patterned with black, yellow and white patches. The pattern is different on every animal, a bit like a fingerprint.

8333.q: What do you call the farmer who looks after the cows on the alpine pasture?
8333.e: In summer, the alpine herdsman, called a Senn or Älpler in Swiss German, looks after the cows on the alpine pasture and often makes cheese there too. This is a typical Swiss tradition.
8333.m: The alpine herdsman looks after the cows.

8334.q: What does the beech marten use its whiskers, also called vibrissae, for?
a: For finding its way in the dark
8334.e: The vibrissae help the beech marten feel obstacles and narrow gaps even in complete darkness. This is especially important when squeezing through tight holes.
8334.m: Whiskers help it feel its way in the dark.

8335.q: Which bird is most closely related to the barn swallow?
8335.e: Like the barn swallow, the house martin belongs to the swallow family. The swift looks similar but is not closely related.
8335.m: Barn swallows and house martins are both swallows.

8336.q: Which famous scientist carefully studied how important earthworms are for the soil?
8336.e: Charles Darwin observed earthworms for many years. He even wrote a whole book about their importance for the soil.

8337.q: Why should you drink plenty of water?
a: Your body needs water to work properly
8337.e: Your body is made largely of water. It helps, for example, with carrying nutrients around.
8337.m: Water is important for your body.

8338.q: When are roe deer most active?
a: At dawn and dusk, in the morning and evening
In the middle of the day
8338.e: Roe deer are active mainly at dawn and dusk, early in the morning and in the evening. During the day they often rest in hiding.
8338.m: Roe deer are active at dawn and dusk.

8339.q: Roughly how big can a wasp colony get in summer?
8339.e: In summer a wasp colony grows a lot. Then several thousand wasps often live in a single nest.
8339.m: A colony often has thousands of wasps.

8340.q: What does an octopus use to hold on to stones?
8340.e: There are lots of small suckers on the octopus's arms. With them it holds on to stones and grabs its prey.
8340.m: The octopus has suckers on its arms.

8341.q: How many toes does a fire salamander have on its front feet?
8341.e: The fire salamander has only four toes on its front feet, while its back feet have five. This is typical of many salamanders and newts.
8341.m: The front feet have four toes.

8342.q: What does the cockerel use its beak for most?
8342.e: With its beak, the cockerel pecks grain, worms and insects from the ground. It has no teeth.

8343.q: Roughly how old can a carp get?
8343.e: Carp can get very old, some even over 30 or 40 years. That is a very great age for a fish.
8343.m: Carp can live a very long time.

8344.q: Why are salmon important for river ecosystems?
a: Their bodies provide nutrients for animals and plants
They fertilise the desert with eggs
8344.e: When salmon die, lots of nutrients enter the ecosystem. Animals, plants and tiny organisms all benefit.
8344.m: Salmon bring nutrients into the river system.

8345.q: How many larval stages does the cockchafer grub go through?
8345.e: The grub sheds its skin twice and so goes through three larval stages. Then it becomes a pupa.
8345.m: Cockchafer grubs have three larval stages.

8346.q: What shape are the pupils in a common toad's eyes?
8346.e: The common toad's pupil is a horizontal slit. This is a good way to recognise this animal.

8347.q: How can you recognise beech marten tracks in the snow?
a: The prints often lie in pairs side by side
There is just one long drag mark
A beech marten leaves no tracks
8347.e: The beech marten usually moves by bounding. It places its back paws exactly in the prints of its front paws, so the tracks often lie in pairs side by side.
8347.m: Marten tracks often lie in pairs.

8348.q: In which parts of Switzerland can foreign nationals partly vote at municipal or cantonal level?
a: In some municipalities of French-speaking Switzerland, for example in the cantons of Jura and Neuchâtel
8348.e: Some cantons such as Neuchâtel and Jura, as well as some municipalities, give foreign nationals the right to vote at municipal or cantonal level under certain conditions.
8348.m: Voting rights for foreigners exist in a few local places.

8349.q: What does the golden eagle mainly use to kill its prey?
8349.e: The golden eagle grabs its prey with the powerful talons on its feet and kills it that way. The beak is used mainly for tearing the prey apart afterwards.

8350.q: Where in the world do whitefish and their close relatives live?
a: In the north of Europe, Asia and North America
8350.e: This group of fish lives in the cooler regions of the northern hemisphere. There are many lakes with cold water there.
8350.m: Whitefish live in the cool north.

8351.q: What is the big pasture high in the mountains called, where cows graze in summer?
8351.e: In summer, many cows are taken up to the alp, a lush green pasture high in the mountains. The grass there is especially tasty.
8351.m: In summer, cows graze on the alp.

8352.q: Where does a pike like to live best?
a: In still lakes and rivers with plants
8352.e: Pike like calm water with lots of plants, where they can hide well. From there they lie in wait for prey.
8352.m: Pike love calm waters full of plants.

8353.q: What does the harbour seal mainly use its front flippers for in the water?
8353.e: With its front flippers, the harbour seal can steer well in the water and change direction. The power for swimming forwards comes from its back flippers.

8354.q: What does the stoat use its slim, long body for?
a: To follow rodents into narrow tunnels
8354.e: Thanks to its slim body, the stoat can easily get into the narrow tunnels of mice and voles. So its prey cannot escape there.
8354.m: A slim body helps it hunt mice.

8355.q: Why shouldn't dogs take a common toad in their mouth?
a: Because the skin secretion irritates and tastes bad
Because the toad eats the dog
Because the toad is as hot as chilli
8355.e: The common toad's poisonous secretion can cause irritation in a dog's mouth. That is why it is better to keep dogs away from toads.
8355.m: Toad secretion irritates mouth and eyes.

8356.q: Roughly how heavy can a blue whale get?
8356.e: A large blue whale can weigh as much as about 30 elephants put together. That also makes it the heaviest animal in the world.

8357.q: Which centipede is common under stones and wood in Central Europe?
8357.e: Brown centipedes are brown and flat and live under stones, leaves and wood. At night they hunt small arthropods.
8357.m: The stone centipede is a centipede.

8358.q: When is the edible dormouse active and looking for food?
8358.e: The edible dormouse is a nocturnal animal. During the day it usually hides and sleeps in holes.
8358.m: The edible dormouse is a night animal.

8359.q: How does the peregrine falcon usually kill its prey?
a: With a powerful bite to the neck, using a tooth on its beak
8359.e: The peregrine falcon has a tooth-like point on its beak, which it uses to cut through the neck of its prey. This kills it quickly and precisely.
8359.m: The falcon's tooth kills with one bite.

8360.q: How does the tawny owl typically hunt?
a: It watches from a raised perch and then swoops on its prey
It runs along the ground chasing its prey
It digs tunnels to catch prey
8360.e: The tawny owl often sits still on a branch or post, watching its surroundings. As soon as it spots prey, it swoops down silently.
8360.m: Tawny owls hunt from a perch.

8361.q: What kind of paws does a red fox have that help it creep quietly?
a: Feet with claws like a bird's
Hard horny paws like a cow's
