8361.e: The fox's soft paw pads help it move very quietly through forests and fields. This way it can creep up on its prey unnoticed.

8362.q: How can you recognise an infestation of black bean aphids?
a: By dense black colonies on the shoot tips
By big holes in the beans
By white webs on the roots
By red spots on the flowers
8362.e: The black bean aphid sits in dense groups on the young shoots of beans and other plants. It is a common garden pest.
8362.m: Black bean aphids form dense colonies.

8363.q: How big is a cuckoo's egg compared to the eggs of the much smaller host bird?
8363.e: Although the cuckoo is usually bigger than its host bird, the size of its egg is often well matched to the eggs of the small host. This makes the trick even better.
8363.m: The cuckoo's egg matches in size.

8364.q: Which statement about pumas and swimming is true?
a: It can swim well when it needs to
8364.e: Pumas don't avoid water as a rule. They cross rivers and lakes when they need to.

8365.q: Apart from jumping, how else does a grasshopper move around?
a: It walks, and some species also fly
It rolls up like a ball
8365.e: Grasshoppers can also walk quite normally. Many species also use their wings to fly.
8365.m: Grasshoppers walk, jump and sometimes fly.

8366.q: What happens when you stir sugar into warm water?
8366.e: Sugar dissolves in water and is then no longer visible, even though it is still there. You can taste it but no longer see it.

8367.q: What is the fastest gait of a horse called?
8367.e: A horse is at its fastest when galloping. Walk and trot are slower.
8367.m: The gallop is the fastest gait.

8368.q: Which fruit does the edible dormouse sometimes eat in gardens, to the annoyance of the owners?
8368.e: In gardens, the edible dormouse sometimes eats ripe cherries or apples straight from the tree. This can be annoying for fruit growers.
8368.m: It likes cherries and apples from gardens.

8369.q: What is a lead for when walking a dog?
a: So that the dog can be guided safely
So that it can smell better
8369.e: A lead helps you guide the dog safely, for example near roads. This way it can't frighten anyone or put itself in danger.
8369.m: The lead guides the dog safely.

8370.q: What else are elephants' big ears used for?
8370.e: A lot of blood flows through the ears. When the elephant flaps its ears, the blood cools down.
8370.m: Ears help the elephant cool down.

8371.q: Roughly how big does an adult alpine salamander get?
8371.e: The alpine salamander is a rather small animal, around 10 to 15 centimetres long including its tail. That makes it shorter than a cat's tail.
8371.m: It grows to about 10 to 15 centimetres.

8372.q: Why do pigs like to roll in mud?
a: To cool down and protect their skin
Because they are afraid of water
So that they can run faster
8372.e: Pigs can hardly sweat, so the mud cools their skin. It also protects them from sunburn and annoying insects.
8372.m: Mud cools and protects pig skin.

8373.q: What do young edible frog tadpoles mainly feed on?
8373.e: Unlike adult edible frogs, tadpoles mainly eat algae and plant material in the water. Only after their metamorphosis do they become meat-eaters.

8374.q: How does the jaguar often kill its prey?
a: With a bite to the skull or neck
By strangling it with its tail
By drowning it in the river
8374.e: The jaguar often bites through the skull or into the neck of its prey. This sets it apart from many other big cats, which tend to bite the throat.
8374.m: Jaguars often bite the skull or neck.

8375.q: Where does the barn owl often have its nest?
a: In the reeds by the lake
In a hole in the ground
8375.e: The barn owl likes dark, quiet places such as old barns or towers. There it feels safe.
8375.m: Barns are popular barn owl hideouts.

8376.q: Roughly how old can a hippopotamus get in the wild?
8376.e: Hippos can get quite old in the wild, often around 40 years. In zoos some live even longer.

8377.q: On which continent do the black-backed jackal and the side-striped jackal live?
8377.e: Both species are at home in Africa. They live in savannahs, bushland and similar habitats.
8377.m: Side-striped and black-backed jackals live in Africa.

8378.q: What do many wild geese do in autumn?
a: They dig themselves into the ground
8378.e: To find enough food in winter, many wild geese fly to warmer countries. They come back again in spring.
8378.m: Wild geese fly away in autumn.

8379.q: Which stage of development comes directly after the larva in mosquitoes?
8379.e: After the larval stage, the mosquito turns into a pupa, which also lives in water. The fully grown adult mosquito then emerges from the pupa.
8379.m: After the larva comes the pupa.

8380.q: What does an alpaca mainly eat?
8380.e: Alpacas eat plants, mainly grasses. In the stable they usually get hay.

8381.q: What happens to the stag beetle in winter?
a: The adults have already died, the larvae survive in the ground
It sleeps in an ants' nest
8381.e: The beetles die after the breeding season. The larvae survive the winter in the ground.
8381.m: In winter only the larvae survive.

8382.q: Which sex of European perch grows bigger on average?
a: Both the same size, no difference
8382.e: Female perch grow faster and get bigger than the males. Especially big perch are therefore usually females.

8383.q: How do African wild dogs usually kill their prey?
a: By biting and pulling it down as a pack
By strangling it with their paws
8383.e: The pack members grab the prey and pull it down. The kill usually happens quickly.
8383.m: The pack pulls the prey down.

8384.q: Are there pike in Swiss lakes too?
a: Only in the ocean, not in Switzerland
8384.e: Pike live in many Swiss lakes and rivers. They are a popular fish with anglers.
8384.m: Pike live in Swiss lakes too.

8385.q: What happens to the spots in its coat when a cheetah grows up?
a: They stay the same all its life
8385.e: Each cheetah's pattern of spots stays the same all its life, a bit like a fingerprint. Every cheetah has a unique pattern.
8385.m: Every cheetah has a unique spot pattern.

8386.q: What does a common toad's skin feel like?
8386.e: Unlike frogs, the common toad has dry, warty skin. This helps it cope well on land too.
8386.m: Toad skin is warty, not slippery.

8387.q: Why are cats and cars dangerous for squirrels in towns and villages?
a: They can injure or kill the squirrel
They are completely harmless to squirrels
8387.e: In towns and villages, cats and road traffic are big dangers for squirrels. Many animals are harmed this way.
8387.m: Cats and cars are dangerous where people live.

8388.q: How many eggs does a goose usually lay in a clutch?
8388.e: A goose usually lays four to eight eggs before she starts sitting on them. All the eggs hatch at about the same time.
8388.m: A goose's clutch usually has four to eight eggs.

8389.q: How does the way a pond skater walks on water differ from the basilisk lizard?
a: The pond skater is carried by surface tension
Both run on cushions of air
The pond skater regularly dives under
8389.e: The basilisk lizard runs across the water with very fast steps. The light pond skater is carried by surface tension.
8389.m: The pond skater is carried by the water.

8390.q: Where does the common raven usually build its nest?
a: On rock ledges or in tall trees
In thick bushes on the ground
8390.e: The common raven prefers well-protected, high places for its nest. Cliffs and old, tall trees offer ideal conditions.
8390.m: Nests are usually on rocks or in trees.

8391.q: Which type of joint lets the arm move in almost every direction?
a: The ball-and-socket joint in the shoulder
The hinge joint in the knee
A fixed joint in the top of the skull
There is no movable joint in the arm
8391.e: The ball-and-socket joint of the shoulder allows a very wide range of movement. Other joints, such as the knee, only move in one direction.
8391.m: Ball-and-socket joints allow lots of movement.

8392.q: What is typical of bonobos' hands?
a: They are grasping hands with a movable thumb
8392.e: With their hands, bonobos can grip fruit, branches and food well. The thumb can be placed opposite the other fingers.
8392.m: Bonobos grip skilfully with their hands.

8393.q: Is it allowed to hunt golden eagles in Switzerland?
a: No, the golden eagle is protected
Yes, if it flies near sheep
8393.e: In the past, the golden eagle was heavily persecuted and almost wiped out. It has been protected in Switzerland since 1953, so its numbers have recovered.
8393.m: The golden eagle is protected in Switzerland.

8394.q: What is typical of a cheetah's legs?
a: They are very long and strong
They are very short and thin
They have no muscles at all
8394.e: The cheetah's long, strong legs are the reason for its great speed. With each bound it covers many metres.
8394.m: Long legs make the cheetah so fast.

8395.q: Which animals are natural enemies of the least weasel?
a: Birds of prey, owls, foxes and cats
None, it has no natural enemies
8395.e: Because it is so small, the least weasel is itself prey for many other animals. Birds of prey and owls in particular catch it from the air.

8396.q: Because of delayed implantation, roughly how long does a stoat's whole pregnancy last?
8396.e: Because of delayed implantation, the whole pregnancy stretches over almost a year. So the young are not born until the next spring.

8397.q: Roughly how much does a male jaguar weigh?
8397.e: Adult males usually weigh between about 56 and 96 kilograms. Some animals can be even heavier.
8397.m: Male jaguars weigh up to over 90 kilograms.

8398.q: How do wild dogs mainly find their prey?
a: With heat sensors on their paws
8398.e: They use their senses, especially their good eyesight in open country. Then the pack chases the prey.
8398.m: Their senses help wild dogs hunt.

8399.q: Is the grey heron protected in Switzerland?
a: No, it may be hunted freely
It is only protected in summer
Only the young birds are protected
8399.e: The grey heron is one of the protected bird species in Switzerland. So it must not be hunted or disturbed.

8400.q: Which animal has been a symbol of imperial power and good fortune in Chinese culture for thousands of years?
8400.e: In Chinese culture the dragon has been a symbol of power, good fortune and the emperor for thousands of years. Unlike in Europe, it is usually shown in a positive light.
8400.m: In China the dragon stands for power and good fortune.

8401.q: What happens when a strange male lion takes over the pride?
a: He drives out the old leader
He immediately becomes friends with him
He builds a second pride of his own next to it
8401.e: When a new, stronger lion wants to take over a pride, he often fights the current leader. The loser has to leave the pride.
8401.m: A new lion drives out the old leader.

8402.q: What is it called when fish release their eggs into the water?
8402.e: When spawning, fish release their eggs and the males fertilise them. The eggs are also called spawn.

8403.q: Which order of mammals do tapirs belong to?
8403.e: Tapirs belong to the odd-toed ungulates. This makes them more closely related to horses and rhinos than to pigs.
8403.m: Tapirs are odd-toed ungulates, related to horses.

8404.q: What does research show about the bearded vulture's flying technique in the mountains?
a: It uses updrafts along cliffs to climb
It only flies in a straight line just above the ground
It can't fly higher than ten metres
It only flies backwards in the wind
8404.e: The bearded vulture skilfully uses the thermals and updrafts that form along steep cliffs. This lets it climb effortlessly to great heights without using much energy.

8406.q: Roughly how long is a least weasel's tail?
a: Very short, only a few centimetres
As long as its whole body
It has no visible tail at all
8406.e: The short tail without a black tip is an important way to recognise the least weasel. The stoat's tail is much longer.

8407.q: Roughly since when have guinea pigs been known as pets in Europe?
8407.e: Spanish and other seafarers brought guinea pigs from South America to Europe several hundred years ago. Since then they have been popular pets here.
8407.m: Seafarers brought guinea pigs to Europe.

8408.q: What does the state's monopoly on the use of force mean?
a: Only the state may lawfully use force, for example through the police and courts.
Only the dictator may break laws.
Force is forbidden in all cases.
8408.e: In a state under the rule of law, the monopoly on force lies with state institutions that are bound by laws. In dictatorships this monopoly is often abused to intimidate critics rather than to enforce the law.
8408.m: Only the state may lawfully use force.

8409.q: How many cubs does a tigress usually have at once?
8409.e: A tigress usually has two to four cubs at the same time. These are called a litter.

8410.q: Which group of birds does the common raven belong to, even though it croaks?
8410.e: Biologically, the common raven is a songbird, even though it doesn't sing beautifully. It is actually the largest songbird.
8410.m: The common raven is a songbird.

a: No, it always lives in large groups
It lives in families with grandparents
8411.e: Hedgehogs are loners and only meet other hedgehogs in the breeding season. Otherwise they roam around on their own.

8412.q: Is the red kite a typical migratory bird or a resident bird?
a: A partial migrant, only some fly away
A pure resident that never migrates
A pure migrant, they all fly away
A bird that lives only in water
8412.e: Not all red kites fly away. In mild winters some stay in Switzerland, which is why it is called a partial migrant.
8412.m: The red kite is a partial migrant.

8413.q: What is the red deer's mating season in autumn called?
8413.e: The rut begins in autumn. Then the stags look for females and fight over them.
8413.m: The mating season is called the rut.

8414.q: What are the small drops of water lying on the grass on cool mornings called?
8414.e: On cool nights the air cools down and water vapour settles on plants as droplets. This is called dew.

8415.q: Which endangered big cat lives in the high mountains of Central Asia and often hunts at over 4,000 metres?
8415.e: The snow leopard lives in the high mountains of Central Asia, for example in the Himalayas and the Altai. Because of poaching and loss of habitat it is endangered today.
8415.m: The snow leopard lives in the high mountains of Asia.

8416.q: Why can't a cheetah roar like a lion?
a: Its voice box is built differently
It is afraid of its own roar
8416.e: The cheetah's voice box is built differently from that of lions and tigers. That is why it can only purr and chirp instead of roaring.
8416.m: The cheetah's voice box doesn't allow roaring.

8417.q: Which animal is a natural enemy of the great tit?
8417.e: The sparrowhawk is a small bird of prey that likes to hunt small birds such as the great tit. Cats can also be dangerous for great tits.
8417.m: The sparrowhawk hunts small birds like great tits.

8418.q: Why are dung beetles useful for pastures?
a: They break down dung and mix it into the soil
They drive away all the cows
8418.e: By burying the dung, they get nutrients into the soil. Cowpats also disappear more quickly.
8418.m: Dung beetles break down dung and fertilise the soil.

8419.q: How soon can a chamois kid follow its mother?
a: Just a few hours after birth
8419.e: Chamois kids are well developed at birth and can follow their mother soon afterwards. This is vital for survival on steep ground.
8419.m: Kids follow their mother after just hours.

8420.e: The grasshopper has six legs and three body parts. These are typical features of an insect.

8421.q: Which body parts especially help the polar bear swim?
a: Its wide front paws, used like paddles
8421.e: The polar bear's wide front paws work like paddles in the water. With them it can push itself forward powerfully.

8422.q: Which bird has a long beak and likes to eat frogs?
8422.e: The stork has long legs and a long beak, which it uses to search meadows and marshes for frogs and insects. In Switzerland it can be seen more often again.
8422.m: The stork probes for frogs with its beak.

8423.q: What role does the beaver play in protecting wetlands?
a: It is an important keystone species that creates and maintains wetlands
It drives away all other animals
8423.e: Thanks to its dams, the beaver creates new wetlands that provide a home for many rare plants and animals. That is why it is considered an important keystone species in conservation.

8424.q: How many pairs of chromosomes does a normal human body cell have?
8424.e: Human body cells contain 23 pairs of chromosomes, that is 46 chromosomes in total. They carry all of the cell's genetic information.
8424.m: Body cells have 23 pairs of chromosomes.

8425.q: Which water bird also eats whitefish?
8425.e: The cormorant dives and hunts fish. Mute swans and greylag geese mainly eat plants.

8426.q: How many young does a female beaver usually have per litter?
8426.e: A female beaver usually gives birth to 2 to 4 young per litter, once a year in spring. The little beavers can swim shortly after birth.

8427.q: Roughly how long can a tiger be, including its tail?
8427.e: A large tiger can be up to three metres long including its tail. That is longer than a car is wide.
8427.m: Tigers grow up to 3 metres long.

8428.q: Roughly how much does a newborn elephant calf weigh?
8428.e: Even baby elephants are very big and heavy. Yet they can already stand and walk shortly after birth.
8428.m: Elephant calves are big even at birth.

8429.q: What happens to a mosquito's belly when it has drunk lots of blood?
8429.e: When a mosquito has drunk a lot of blood, its belly fills up and becomes fat and round. You can sometimes even see this when a mosquito has just bitten.
8429.m: A full belly after sucking blood.

8430.q: When do most whitefish spawn in Swiss lakes?
8430.e: Whitefish spawn when the water is cold, usually from November into January. This is different from many other fish.
8430.m: Whitefish spawn in the cold winter.

8431.q: What colour is the snow leopard's coat usually?
a: Light grey to cream with dark ring-shaped spots
8431.e: Its thick coat is pale with dark rosettes. This makes it almost invisible among rocks and snow.
8431.m: Its coat camouflages it in the mountains.

8432.q: Roughly how tall is an adult cheetah at the shoulder?
a: About as tall as a big dog
8432.e: An adult cheetah is about 70 to 90 centimetres tall at the shoulder. That is about as tall as a big dog.
8432.m: Cheetahs are about as tall as a dog at the shoulder.

8433.q: What do male koalas do during the mating season to attract females?
8433.e: Male koalas make loud, deep calls during the mating season. For their size, these calls sound surprisingly loud and deep.
8433.m: Male koalas call loudly and deeply.

8434.q: What does a European tree frog's skin feel like?
a: Leathery and hard like a tortoise's
8434.e: The tree frog's skin is smooth and usually stays moist. This moisture is important so that the skin can also help with breathing.
8434.m: Its skin is smooth and moist.

8435.q: What special ability do fire salamanders have when injured?
a: They can change colour like a chameleon
8435.e: If a fire salamander loses a leg or its tail, it can regrow that body part over time. This ability is called regeneration.

8436.q: Which well-known conservation symbol shows a panda?
8436.e: The WWF uses the panda as a symbol for protecting endangered animals. The logo is known all over the world.
8436.m: The panda is the WWF symbol.

8438.q: How do baboons warn each other of danger?
8438.e: Baboons have many sounds, for example warning barks when predators are near. This way the whole group reacts quickly.

8439.q: Which birds often sit on a rhinoceros's back?
8439.e: Oxpeckers are small birds that sit on the rhino's back and eat ticks and insects there. This helps both animals.

8440.q: What can you use to find out whether an object conducts electricity?
a: A circuit with a small bulb
8440.e: If you put the object into a circuit with a small bulb and the bulb lights up, the object conducts electricity. If it does not light up, it is an insulator.
8440.m: A small bulb shows whether electricity is flowing.

8441.q: What was the patterned shell of the hawksbill turtle used for in the past?
8441.e: The beautifully patterned shell of the hawksbill turtle used to be made into jewellery and combs. Today this trade is banned.
8441.m: Its shell was once used for jewellery.

8442.q: Which bird family does the red kite belong to?
8442.e: Like eagles and buzzards, the red kite belongs to the hawk and eagle family. Falcons form a completely different family.
8442.m: The red kite belongs to the hawk and eagle family.

8443.q: What is special about the edible dormouse's eyes?
a: They are big and black, good for seeing at night
They are tiny and almost invisible
They glow red during the day
8443.e: The big, dark eyes help the edible dormouse find its way at night. This suits its nocturnal way of life.
8443.m: Big eyes help with seeing at night.

8444.q: What does the kestrel eat most often?
8444.e: Common voles make up most of its food. It also hunts insects, small birds and lizards.
8444.m: Voles are the kestrel's main prey.

8445.q: Where do European swifts spend the winter?
a: They stay in Switzerland all winter
8445.e: In August, swifts fly from Switzerland towards Africa. There, south of the Sahara, they find enough insects even in winter.
8445.m: Swifts spend the winter in southern Africa.

8446.q: Which place in Switzerland is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
8446.e: Bern’s Old Town with its arcades and fountains has been a World Heritage Site since 1983. UNESCO protects places that are important for all of humanity.
8446.m: Bern’s Old Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

8447.q: Why does the European garden spider often build its web freely between two plants?
a: So that flying insects can fly into it
So that it can swim well
So that it is protected from rain
So that it can sleep in the shade
8447.e: A web hanging freely between plants is especially good at catching flying insects. Flies and wasps can't easily get past it there.

8448.q: Roughly how long does it take for a mosquito egg to become an adult mosquito?
8448.e: When it is warm enough, a mosquito develops from egg to adult in just one to two weeks. That is why mosquitoes can multiply so quickly.

8449.q: In which season does the red deer's rut take place?
8449.e: The rut takes place in autumn, usually in September and October. Then you can hear the stags roaring loudly in the forest.

8452.q: What do the fine touch-sensitive hairs on the mole's nose help it with?
a: They sense prey in the dark
They show it which way is north
8452.e: The mole's nose has lots of fine touch-sensitive hairs. With them it feels every little movement in its dark tunnel.
8452.m: Touch hairs sense prey in the dark.

8453.q: What is a duet song in gibbons?
a: Male and female sing in time with each other
A gibbon sings only at night
8453.e: In many species, pairs sing together, often closely matched to each other. This strengthens their bond and marks their territory.
8453.m: Gibbon pairs often sing in duets.

8454.q: Roughly how long can spotted hyenas live in captivity?
8454.e: In captivity, spotted hyenas can live for over 20 years. In the wild they often live shorter lives.

8455.q: What is the slime on a goldfish's skin for?
a: It protects against disease and injury
8455.e: The slime on the skin forms a protective layer against germs and small injuries. That is why you should avoid touching a goldfish with your hands.

8456.q: Roughly how many hours a day does a lion sleep or rest?
8456.e: Lions are very lazy and spend most of the day sleeping and resting. They usually hunt at dusk or at night.

8457.q: What is a device that stores electricity called?
8457.e: A battery stores energy that it can give off as electricity. That is why many toys work with batteries.
8457.m: A battery stores electricity for later.

8458.q: What helps brown trout when a stream is restored to its natural state?
8458.e: Gravel beds serve as spawning sites, and roots and stones as hiding places. A straightened concrete stream, on the other hand, offers hardly any habitat.

8459.q: Why are dragonflies good indicators of clean water?
a: Many species need healthy waters to develop
They clean the water with their wings
They only live in salt water
They eat dirt in the water
8459.e: Many species depend on natural, clean waters. Their presence therefore shows the condition of a habitat.

8460.q: How does the European tree frog's way of life in summer differ from that in winter?
a: In summer it is active in bushes, in winter it rests buried
In winter it is most active
8460.e: In summer the tree frog actively hunts insects in shrubs. In winter, on the other hand, it goes into a resting phase on land.
8460.m: Active in summer, resting in winter.

8461.q: What do adult cockchafers mainly feed on?
8461.e: The adult beetles eat the leaves of broadleaved trees such as oaks, beeches or maples. They leave signs of feeding behind.
8461.m: The beetles eat leaves of broadleaved trees.

a: Yes, it is a true bear
Yes, it is a species of bear
8462.e: Although koalas are often called koala bears, they are not bears. Like the kangaroo, they are marsupials.

8463.q: What does the Schengen Agreement, which Switzerland also takes part in, lay down?
a: Removing passport checks at shared borders
8463.e: Thanks to Schengen, travellers can move between many European countries without passport checks at the border. Switzerland has taken part since 2008, even though it is not an EU member.
8463.m: Schengen allows travel without border checks.

8464.q: Roughly how many eggs can a female common toad lay?
8464.e: A female common toad can lay several thousand eggs at once. Only a small number of them later become adult toads.
8464.m: A female lays thousands of eggs.

8465.q: What happens to the elk's (moose's) antlers every year?
a: They are shed and grow back
They stay the same for life
They only fall off in summer and stay gone
8465.e: After the rut, the bull sheds its antlers. In spring a new, usually bigger set grows back.
8465.m: The antlers grow back every year.

8466.q: What does a wild boar do when it feels threatened?
a: It usually flees, but it can also attack
8466.e: Normally a wild boar runs away from danger. But if it finds no way out, it can also defend itself.
8466.m: In danger, the wild boar usually flees.

8467.q: Can a panda climb trees well?
8467.e: Pandas are skilled climbers. Young pandas in particular like to climb to hide or play.

8468.q: Which well-known saying has to do with the swallow?
a: One swallow does not make a summer
The early bird catches the worm
If you chase two hares, you'll catch neither
8468.e: The saying “One swallow does not make a summer” means that a single sign doesn't prove anything yet. It came about because the return of the swallows is seen as a sign of spring.
8468.m: One swallow alone is not enough.

8469.q: Why do dictators usually dislike free newspapers?
a: Because they don’t want criticism of the government.
8469.e: Free newspapers could report on mistakes and wrongdoing. Dictators want to prevent that, so they control the media.

8470.q: How big are the okapi's ears?
a: Long like a hare's and stiff
8470.e: The large ears hear very well, which is important in the dense forest. They can be turned in many directions.
8470.m: Okapis hear well thanks to their big ears.

8471.q: What makes the marmots' escape burrows different from their main living burrows?
a: Escape burrows are small holes for a quick getaway
Escape burrows are much bigger than living burrows
8471.e: Escape burrows are small, simple holes that marmots can dive into quickly when danger appears suddenly. The main living burrows are bigger and have several tunnels and chambers.
8471.m: Escape burrows are for quick rescue.

8472.q: What does the wels catfish usually do in winter?
a: It becomes sluggish and eats little
8472.e: In cold water its metabolism slows down. It then often rests in deeper parts of the water.
8472.m: In winter the wels catfish rests a lot.

8473.q: What is the covering that protects the brain and spinal cord and is filled with fluid called?
8473.e: The meninges surround the brain and spinal cord and contain a protective fluid. They cushion knocks in addition to the skull.
8473.m: The meninges cushion the brain and spinal cord.

8474.q: Is the tiger threatened with extinction today?
a: Yes, it is considered an endangered species
No, there are huge numbers of tigers
No, tigers are not threatened at all
8474.e: The tiger is threatened in the wild because there is less and less habitat and because of poaching. Many organisations work to protect it.

8475.q: Why is the carp well suited to being farmed in ponds?
a: Because it is undemanding and grows quickly
Because it only eats very expensive food
Because it only lives in cold mountain water
8475.e: Carp are undemanding fish that are happy with simple food and grow well in ponds. This makes them good for fish farming.
8475.m: Carp are well suited to pond farming.

8477.q: How do wolves usually react when they meet people?
a: They tend to avoid people and move away
They usually attack people straight away
They actively seek contact like pets
They always follow people over long distances
8477.e: Wild wolves are naturally rather shy and try to avoid people. Attacks on humans are extremely rare.
8477.m: Wolves usually avoid people on their own.

8478.q: What is a committee in parliament?
a: A smaller group of members of parliament who prepare issues
8478.e: Committees prepare business for the National Council and the Council of States. They discuss proposals in detail before the whole chamber decides on them.

8479.q: What does an alpine marmot dig its burrows with?
a: Its strong front paws and claws
8479.e: The marmot's front paws are strong and have sharp claws. With them it loosens the soil and pushes it aside when digging.

8480.q: Which sea animal particularly likes to eat jellyfish?
8480.e: Sea turtles love jellyfish as food. Sadly, they sometimes mistake plastic bags in the sea for jellyfish.

8481.q: What does a hamster like to use to clean its fur?
8481.e: Hamsters like to roll around in fine sand. This keeps their fur clean and free of grease.

8482.q: Where does a young bumblebee queen hide in winter?
a: In a small hole in the ground
8482.e: For her winter sleep, the queen digs a little way into the ground. There she is protected from cold and enemies.
8482.m: The queen spends the winter in the ground.

8483.q: What is a danger for slow worms in the garden?
8483.e: When mowing, the slow-moving animals are easily injured. Road traffic is also a danger.

8484.q: Which statement about the sense of smell of detection dogs working for customs or the police is most accurate?
a: They can pick out tiny traces of certain substances from a complex mixture of smells
They basically smell worse than humans
Detection dogs work mainly with their hearing
8484.e: Thanks to their extremely fine noses, trained detection dogs can recognise even tiny traces of drugs, explosives or other substances among many other smells. This ability makes them very valuable for customs and police work.
8484.m: Detection dogs pick out smells extremely precisely.

8485.q: How does a rhinoceros mark its own territory?
a: With large piles of dung and urine
8485.e: Rhinos leave large piles in certain places to show other rhinos that this is their territory. Other rhinos can smell these piles.
8485.m: Rhinos mark their territory with dung.

8486.q: How does a least weasel typically hunt?
a: It follows its prey right into its tunnels
It only lies in wait at waterholes
It only hunts from the air
It digs its own deep burrows for hunting
8486.e: Thanks to its slim body, it can chase mice right into their underground tunnels. There the prey hardly has a chance to escape.
8486.m: It hunts right inside mouse tunnels.

8487.q: Which aphid relative can cause great damage in vineyards and came to Europe from North America in the 19th century?
8487.e: Phylloxera sucks on the roots of grapevines and destroyed many vineyards in the 19th century. Today vines are grafted onto resistant rootstocks.

8489.q: What is an adult female goat called?
8489.e: A female goat is called a nanny or doe. She gives milk once she has had a kid.
8489.m: A mother goat is called a nanny.

8490.q: What are a stag beetle's antennae?
8490.e: With their antennae, the beetles smell and feel their surroundings. The ends are spread out like a fan.
8490.m: Antennae are for smelling and feeling.

8491.q: What does the great tit eat most in summer?
8491.e: In summer, the great tit hunts lots of insects and caterpillars. This is important so that its young get enough protein to grow.
8491.m: In summer it mainly eats insects.

8492.q: What do cheetah cubs look like when they are newborn?
a: They are blind and very small
They already have their full coat colour
They can see and hunt straight away
8492.e: Cheetah cubs are born blind and are very helpless at first. Only after a few days do they open their eyes.
8492.m: Cheetah babies are blind at first.

8493.q: How many wings does a housefly have?
8493.e: True flies have only one pair of wings, which is why they are also called two-winged flies. This makes them especially agile in the air.

8494.q: Why does a stoat have to eat very often?
a: Its small, slim body loses heat quickly
It has no teeth for chewing
It hibernates for a long time
8494.e: A small, long body gives off a lot of heat. That is why the stoat needs lots of energy and has to catch a lot of prey every day.
8494.m: The stoat needs lots of food because it loses heat quickly.

8495.q: What does a common toad use to catch its prey?
8495.e: The common toad flicks its tongue forward at lightning speed to catch prey. Then it swallows the prey whole.
8495.m: The tongue shoots out lightning fast.

8496.q: What protection status does the otter have in Switzerland today?
8496.e: The otter is strictly protected because it is still rare. The law forbids disturbing or hunting it.

8497.q: Which protected area in the Congo is known for okapis?
8497.e: The Okapi Wildlife Reserve in the Ituri Forest protects these animals. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
8497.m: Many okapis live in the Okapi Wildlife Reserve.

8498.q: What does a kestrel do when, instead of hovering, it simply waits?
a: It sits still on fence posts, pylons or branches and watches the ground
It swims in the water lying in wait for fish
It digs itself into the ground
It walks around on the ground like a chicken
8498.e: As well as hovering, the kestrel also hunts from raised perches. From a fence post or pylon it can calmly search the ground for prey.
8498.m: Hunting from posts is common too.

8499.q: Which sense does the least weasel mainly use to track down mice?
8499.e: With its sensitive nose, the least weasel finds mouse tunnels and fresh trails. This sense is especially important for hunting.

8500.q: How do piglets communicate with their mother?
a: Not at all, they are silent
8500.e: Piglets and their mother communicate with different sounds, for example when it is time to drink. Researchers have been able to tell apart more than twenty different pig sounds.

8501.e: Wolves can swim surprisingly well and even cross large rivers or lakes. This helps them reach new territories.

8502.q: Which body parts help the beaver close its nose and ears when swimming underwater?
8502.e: Beavers have flaps of skin that close their nostrils and ears when diving. This stops water getting in while they swim under the surface.
8502.m: Skin flaps protect nose and ears.

8503.q: What is special about young alpine salamanders when they are born?
a: They are already fully developed little salamanders
They have gills like fish larvae
8503.e: Unlike the fire salamander, the young do not go through a tadpole-like stage in the water. They are born fully developed and don't need a pond.
8503.m: The young are fully developed at birth.

8504.q: What behaviour does a wolf show when it gives way to a higher-ranking wolf?
a: It crouches down and tucks its tail in
It bares its teeth and growls loudly
8504.e: Lower-ranking wolves show with a crouched posture and tucked-in tail that they give way. This way, conflicts in the pack are often settled without fighting.

8505.q: What does the name “orangutan” mean in Malay?
8505.e: The Malay “orang hutan” literally means “person of the forest”. The name shows how similar to humans the animals seemed.
8505.m: Orangutan means person of the forest.

8506.q: In what state are young least weasels born?
a: Able to see and hairy straight away
Able to walk and hunt straight away
Already with a full set of teeth
8506.e: Like many members of the weasel family, young least weasels are completely helpless at birth. They depend on their mother's care.
8506.m: The young are blind and naked at first.

8507.q: What do young golden eagles have to do once they are independent?
a: Find a territory of their own
Stay in their parents' territory for ever
Spend the winter in the water
8507.e: Young golden eagles have to leave their parents' territory at some point and wander to find a free territory of their own. This can take several years.
8507.m: Young eagles look for their own territory.

8509.q: Why do tapir populations recover only slowly?
a: They lay only a few eggs
8509.e: Tapirs have long pregnancies and only one baby at a time. That is why a population grows slowly.

8510.q: Why is pack size important for the wild dog?
a: Large packs hunt and protect better
8510.e: In a bigger pack, more animals can hunt and guard the pups. Defending against enemies also works better.

8511.q: On which island does the rare Tapanuli orangutan live?
8511.e: The Tapanuli orangutan lives only in a small forest area on Sumatra. It is considered one of the rarest great ape species.
8511.m: The Tapanuli orangutan lives on Sumatra.

a: Almost anything: grasses, fruit, insects and sometimes meat
8512.e: Baboons are omnivores. They eat grass, seeds, fruit, roots, insects and occasionally small vertebrates.

8513.q: What is the mute swan showing when it holds its neck in an S shape and lifts its wings slightly?
a: It looks bigger and is showing off
It is showing that it is tired
It is showing that it is cold
It is showing that it wants to sleep
8513.e: This posture makes the swan look bigger and more impressive. It wants to impress or scare off other animals.
8513.m: An S-shaped neck and raised wings mean showing off.

8515.q: When does a hedgehog usually wake up from hibernation?
a: In spring, when it gets warmer
As early as the end of December
8515.e: As soon as temperatures rise in spring, the hedgehog wakes up from hibernation. Then it has to find food quickly to build up its strength again.
8515.m: The hedgehog wakes up again in spring.

8516.q: Why is the barn owl useful for farmers?
a: It catches lots of mice on the farm
It lays lots of hens' eggs
8516.e: Because the barn owl eats lots of mice, it helps farmers naturally against plagues of mice. That is why many farmers like this bird.

8517.q: How does an adult giraffe defend itself against a lion?
a: With a powerful kick of its legs
8517.e: A kick from an adult giraffe is so strong that it can injure or even kill a lion. That is why lions usually attack young or weak giraffes instead.
8517.m: Giraffes defend themselves with powerful kicks.

8518.q: How do butterflies and moths often find a partner?
8518.e: Many butterflies and moths release special scents called pheromones. With their fine antennae, others can smell these scents from far away.
8518.m: Scents help them find a partner.

8519.q: Roughly how much does a kingfisher weigh?
8519.e: A kingfisher weighs only about as much as a small chocolate bar. Even so, it is a successful fish hunter.
8519.m: A kingfisher weighs only about 40 grams.

8520.q: What does a hamster like to eat best?
8520.e: Hamsters like seed mixes, nuts and fresh vegetables. In the wild they also collect seeds and small insects.

8521.q: What does the great tit build in its nesting hole?
a: A nest of moss and hair
8521.e: The great tit lines its hole softly with moss, hair and feathers. This keeps the eggs and young cosy and warm.
8521.m: The nest is soft, made of moss and hair.

8522.q: Roughly how often does a puma hunt large prey once it has eaten its fill?
a: Only again after a few days
8522.e: A puma can live off one large prey animal for several days. Only when the prey is used up does it hunt again.

8523.q: What does the Doppler effect describe, which you can hear, for example, when a siren goes past?
a: The perceived frequency of a wave changes due to the movement of the source or observer
Sound in the air always gets slower the further it travels
Loud noises automatically sound higher than quiet ones
Sound waves reverse direction as soon as they reach an ear
8523.e: When a sound source approaches, the waves are squeezed together and the sound is higher. When it moves away, the waves are stretched and the sound is lower.

8524.q: Which animals are natural enemies of the beaver in Switzerland?
a: Foxes and large birds of prey, for young beavers
8524.e: Young beavers in particular can fall prey to foxes or large birds of prey. Adult beavers, on the other hand, have hardly any natural enemies in Switzerland.

8525.q: Which group of animals does the lake trout belong to?
a: Fish, the vertebrates of the water
8525.e: Fish have a backbone, gills and usually scales. That makes them vertebrates.
8525.m: The lake trout is a vertebrate.

8526.q: What often happens when a squirrel jumps from branch to branch?
a: Its tail helps it keep its balance
It really flies like a bird
8526.e: When jumping from branch to branch, the squirrel stretches out its tail, which helps it stay balanced.
8526.m: The tail keeps it balanced when jumping.

8527.q: Which senses are especially good in the red deer?
8527.e: The red deer has very good senses of smell and hearing. This lets it recognise danger from far away.
8527.m: Red deer smell and hear very well.

8528.q: Which group of animals does the common toad belong to?
8528.e: The common toad is an amphibian, like the frog. Amphibians live on land and need water for their eggs.
8528.m: The common toad is an amphibian.

8530.q: What does the red cap of young great spotted woodpeckers look like?
a: It covers the whole top of the head
8530.e: Young great spotted woodpeckers have a red cap over the whole top of the head. Only later does the difference between males and females show.
8530.m: The young wear a red cap.

8532.q: How heavy can an adult male giraffe get?
a: About as heavy as a cat
8532.e: Male giraffes can weigh almost two tonnes. That makes them much heavier than female giraffes.
8532.m: Male giraffes can weigh almost 2 tonnes.

8533.q: Is the cuckoo a protected bird species in Switzerland?
a: No, it may be hunted everywhere
Yes, but only in the zoo
8533.e: Like most wild birds, the cuckoo is protected by law in Switzerland. So you must not catch or disturb it.
8533.m: The cuckoo is protected in Switzerland.

8534.q: What does a fox like to eat in autumn as well as mice and birds?
8534.e: In autumn, the fox likes to snack on sweet berries, fruit and windfalls. This way it adds to its diet depending on the season.

8535.q: Roughly how big does a great spotted woodpecker get?
a: About the size of a blackbird
8535.e: The great spotted woodpecker measures about 23 centimetres. That is about the size of a blackbird.

8536.q: Roughly how many hours a day does an elephant spend eating?
8536.e: Because elephants are so huge, they have to eat almost all day. They spend up to 16 hours a day looking for food.
8536.m: Elephants spend much of the day eating.

8537.q: How long do young magpies usually stay with their parents after they have fledged?
a: A few more weeks to months
Not at all, they fly off straight away
8537.e: Even after they can fly, young magpies often stay near their parents for a few weeks or months. During this time they learn important skills such as finding food.
8537.m: Young magpies still learn from their parents.

8538.q: What is withholding tax on wages (Quellensteuer)?
a: A tax deducted directly from wages, mostly for foreign employees without a settlement permit
A tax only on drinking water
A voluntary extra tax for the rich
A tax you transfer yourself at the end of the year
8538.e: With withholding tax, the employer deducts the tax directly from the wage and pays it to the state, instead of the person filling in a tax return. In Switzerland this mainly affects foreign employees without a C settlement permit.

8539.q: What does the UN Genocide Convention of 1948 lay down?
a: Genocide is defined and outlawed as an international crime
The death penalty is abolished worldwide
The borders of all states are redrawn
8539.e: The convention defined genocide in international law for the first time and obliges the states that signed it to prevent and punish it. It was a response to the crimes of the Second World War.
8539.m: The convention outlaws genocide under international law.

8540.q: What water temperature does a brown trout particularly like?
a: It doesn't care at all how warm the water is
8540.e: Brown trout need cool water to feel comfortable and get enough oxygen. If the water gets too warm, they struggle.

8541.q: Roughly how often does a dolphin have to come to the surface to breathe?
8541.e: Because dolphins have lungs, they have to keep coming up. Depending on what they are doing, they surface every few minutes.

8542.q: In German, parents who don't look after their children are called “raven parents”. Is that true of real common ravens?
a: No, they take good care of their young
Yes, they leave their young straight away
Yes, only the male sometimes feeds them
No, because they don't have any young
8542.e: Common ravens feed and protect their young for a long time. So the German expression “raven parents” doesn't fit their real behaviour.

8543.q: Roughly how much does an adult mallard weigh?
8543.e: An adult mallard weighs about as much as a large bag of sugar. The male is usually a little heavier than the female.

a: Great Britain leaving the European Union
A climate agreement between Europe and Asia
The founding of the United Nations
8544.e: After a referendum, Great Britain left the European Union. The word is made up of “Britain” and “exit”.
8544.m: Brexit means that Great Britain has left the EU.

8545.q: What is true of alpine newt larvae before they go on land?
a: They breathe with external gills in the water
They live on land straight away
8545.e: Alpine newt larvae first live entirely in water and have external, feathery gills. Only after metamorphosis do they leave the water.
8545.m: Larvae first breathe with external gills.

8546.e: Goat's milk is white, even a little whiter than cow's milk. You can drink it or make cheese from it.

8547.q: Roughly how long does a gorilla mother carry her baby before it is born?
8547.e: Pregnancy in gorillas lasts about as long as in humans, around nine months.
8547.m: A baby gorilla grows for nine months before birth.

8548.q: What makes the development of young alpine salamanders very different from that of many fish species?
a: There are no free-swimming larvae in the water
The young hatch from hard-shelled eggs
Development takes only a few hours
8548.e: Fish usually lay many eggs from which free-swimming larvae hatch. In the alpine salamander, on the other hand, the few young develop completely inside the mother's body.
8548.m: No free-swimming larvae in the water.

8549.q: What do you use to taste whether something is sweet or salty?
8549.e: There are tiny taste buds on your tongue. They detect sweet, salty, sour, bitter and savoury.

8550.q: At what time of day does the wels catfish mainly hunt?
a: Only early in the morning in winter
It never hunts, it only eats plants
8550.e: The wels catfish is nocturnal. It hunts mainly after sunset and finds its prey with its long barbels.
8550.m: Nocturnal animals are out and about at night.

8552.q: In which countries are Bactrian camels mainly kept as domestic animals today?
a: For example in Mongolia and Central Asia
8552.e: There they are important as pack animals and for wool. They can be seen in zoos all over the world.
8552.m: Domestic camels live in Central Asia.

8553.q: What does the Roman snail use to scrape its food off leaves?
8553.e: The snail has a rough, rasping tongue with lots of tiny teeth. With it, it scrapes little pieces off leaves.
8553.m: The snail rasps with its tongue.

8554.q: What is the part of a plant called that takes in water from the soil?
8554.e: The root sits in the soil and soaks up water and nutrients there. It also holds the plant firmly in the ground.
8554.m: The root drinks water from the soil.

8555.q: How does a polar bear often hunt seals?
a: It waits patiently at a hole in the ice
It catches them with a net
8555.e: The polar bear sits quietly by a breathing hole in the ice and waits for a seal to come up. Then it strikes at lightning speed.
8555.m: The polar bear waits patiently at the ice hole.

8556.q: Do male bumblebees have a sting?
8556.e: Only female bumblebees have a sting. So the males can't sting at all.

8557.q: Which bird family does the blackbird belong to?
8557.e: The blackbird belongs to the thrush family. The song thrush is also part of this family.

8558.q: Which body parts are rather small on a polar bear?
8558.e: Compared to its huge body, the polar bear's ears and tail are rather small. This means it loses less heat through these parts.
8558.m: Its ears and tail are rather small.

8559.q: What colour is the fur of newborn spotted hyenas?
8559.e: Young spotted hyenas are dark when they are born. The spots appear later, and the fur gets lighter.
8559.m: Young spotted hyenas are dark at first.

8560.q: What are pheromones used for in social insects such as ants?
a: For communicating with scents, for example along food trails
8560.e: Pheromones are scents that ants use to communicate with each other. With them they mark, for example, the path to a food source, which other ants then follow.
8560.m: Pheromones are the language of ants.

8561.q: What is done next with alpaca wool after shearing?
a: It is cleaned and spun into yarn
It is knitted into jumpers straight away, unwashed
It is glued back onto the animal
8561.e: The wool is sorted, washed and combed. Then it is spun into yarn, which can be knitted or woven.

8562.q: What protects the harbour seal from the cold water?
a: A thick layer of fat under the skin
8562.e: Under the harbour seal's skin there is a thick layer of fat called blubber. This layer keeps the body warm even in cold sea water.
8562.m: A layer of fat keeps the seal warm.

8563.q: What does a common toad do with its skin every now and then?
a: It sheds it from time to time
It falls off completely and doesn't grow back
8563.e: Common toads shed their skin regularly so that it can grow along with their body. The old skin splits open and comes off.
8563.m: Common toads shed their skin from time to time.

8564.q: How many toes does the red deer walk on on each foot?
a: Two, it is an even-toed ungulate
8564.e: The red deer is an even-toed ungulate and walks on two toes. These are covered with a hard hoof.
8564.m: Red deer walk on two toes.

8565.q: Why does the kingfisher often sit motionless on a branch above the water for a long time?
a: It is patiently watching the water for fish
It is only resting after long flights
It is waiting for its partner to court
8565.e: From its perch, the kingfisher has a good view of the water and can lie in wait for fish. Only when it spots prey does it suddenly dive into the water.

8566.q: How do chickens usually react when you scatter food for them?
a: They come running quickly and peck at it
8566.e: Chickens are curious and usually come running quickly when there is food. Then they eagerly peck up the grains from the ground.

8567.q: How does restoring streams to a natural state help the lake trout?
a: Natural streams offer gravel and hiding places
The stream is put into a pipe
The stream is straightened and concreted
The stream is filled with salt
8567.e: Natural streams have gravel banks, shade and hiding places. There trout can spawn and their young can grow up.

8569.q: What is the basic difference between a comet and an asteroid?
a: A comet is made of ice and dust and forms a tail
A comet is always bigger than a planet
An asteroid has a tail of gas
A comet never orbits the Sun
8569.e: Comets are made of ice, dust and frozen gases and form a glowing tail near the Sun. Asteroids, on the other hand, are rocky lumps without a tail.
8569.m: Comets have a tail of ice and dust.

8570.q: How does the Roman snail usually react to light and darkness?
a: It prefers to hide in the shade during the day
It always stays in the brightest spot
8570.e: The Roman snail does not much like bright sunlight because it dries out the ground. So during the day it often hides in the shade.
8570.m: During the day it prefers to stay in the shade.

8571.q: What does a large pike sometimes eat as well?
8571.e: Pike are not fussy eaters; sometimes they even eat smaller members of their own species. This is called cannibalism.
8571.m: Large pike also eat small pike.

8572.q: Can hyenas pull in their claws like cats?
a: They have no claws at all
8572.e: Hyenas have claws that cannot be pulled in. The blunt claws wear down as they walk.
8572.m: Hyena claws cannot be pulled in.

8574.q: What kind of coat does a newborn donkey foal usually have?
8574.e: A newborn donkey foal has a soft, fluffy coat. It can stand and walk soon after birth.

8575.q: What can a jaguar crack open thanks to its powerful bite?
8575.e: The jaguar can bite through turtle shells. Not many other predators can do that.
8575.m: Jaguars can even crack turtle shells.

8576.q: How does an adult stoat usually live?
8576.e: Except during the mating season, the stoat lives alone and defends its own territory. Other stoats are usually chased away.

8577.q: Roughly how long is a guinea pig pregnant?
8577.e: Guinea pigs are pregnant for longer than many other rodents, around nine to ten weeks. That is also why the young are already so well developed at birth.
8577.m: Guinea pigs have a long pregnancy.

8578.q: Which of these is one way jaguars communicate?
8578.e: Jaguars can roar loudly, especially during the mating season. The call carries far through the forest.

8579.q: What is a group of baboons called?
8579.e: Baboons live in groups, often called troops. A troop can have dozens of animals.

8580.q: Besides the golden eagle, which animal is also an enemy of the Alpine marmot?
8580.e: Foxes creep up to marmot burrows along the ground and can catch the young in particular. The ibex, chamois and mountain hare, on the other hand, eat plants. That is why marmots always stay close to their escape holes.
8580.m: Foxes hunt marmots on the ground.

8581.q: What often happens at the shared roosts of carrion crows in winter?
a: many crows gather there for the night
the crows build a swimming pool there
8581.e: In winter, carrion crows often gather in large numbers at certain shared roosts, for example in dense clumps of trees. Being in a group gives warmth and protection from enemies.
8581.m: In winter many crows sleep together.

8582.q: What is the difference between wild salmon and farmed salmon?
a: Farmed salmon grows up in net pens, wild salmon grows up free
Farmed salmon is a completely different fish species
Wild salmon only lives in mountain lakes
8582.e: Farmed salmon grows up in net pens or tanks and is fed. Wild salmon grows up free in rivers and in the sea.
8582.m: Farmed salmon grows up on farms.

8583.q: How can you often recognise a male cockchafer?
a: By the sting on its abdomen
8583.e: Males have seven fan leaves on their antennae, females only six smaller ones. That is how you can tell them apart.

8584.q: How does a robin usually move on the ground?
8584.e: Instead of walking, the robin makes little hops along the ground. That is how it quickly searches for food.

8585.q: What is special about some male orangutans?
a: They get cheek pads late or never
8585.e: Some males stay without cheek pads for a long time. Whether and when they get them also depends on competition from other males.

8586.q: What threatens the cheetah most today?
a: Loss of its habitat because of humans
8586.e: Because people use more and more land for fields and settlements, the cheetah's habitat is getting smaller. This makes it hard for them to survive.
8586.m: Habitat loss is a big threat to the cheetah.

8587.q: What does the larva do before it becomes an adult beetle?
a: It builds a nest of twigs
8587.e: The larva eats lots of aphids and grows. Then it attaches itself to a leaf and becomes a pupa, from which the adult beetle finally hatches.
8587.m: The beetle hatches from the pupa.

8588.q: How is the golden eagle often shown in culture and on coats of arms?
a: As a symbol of strength and freedom
8588.e: Because of its size, strength and impressive appearance, the golden eagle has always been seen as a symbol of strength and freedom. That is why many countries and coats of arms show eagles.
8588.m: It is seen as a symbol of strength and freedom.

8589.q: What do some male penguins do to impress a female?
a: They give her a particularly nice stone
8589.e: In some penguin species, the male picks a particularly nice stone for the nest and gives it to the female. This is part of their courtship behaviour.
8589.m: Male penguins give stones for the nest.

8590.q: When does a blackbird particularly like to sing?
a: Early in the morning and in the evening
Only in the middle of the night
Blackbirds do not sing at all
8590.e: Blackbirds particularly like to sing at dawn and in the evening. Their song is one of the most beautiful of all our birds.
8590.m: Blackbirds sing in the morning and evening.

8591.q: What does a tiger do when another tiger enters its marked territory?
a: It invites the other tiger to play
8591.e: Tigers defend their territory against intruders of their own kind. They want enough hunting ground for themselves.

8592.q: What is said about the spotted hyena when it laughs?
a: That it often shows excitement or submission
That it is happy like a human
8592.e: The giggling is not a sign of fun. It usually shows excitement, fear or submission.

8593.q: What are the tiny openings on the underside of leaves, the stomata, used for?
a: For exchanging gases such as CO2 and oxygen
8593.e: Through the stomata the plant takes in carbon dioxide and gives off oxygen and water vapour. They open and close as needed.
8593.m: Stomata control the plant’s gas exchange.

8594.q: What is the parliament of a canton often called?
8594.e: Every canton has its own parliament, which depending on the canton is called the Cantonal Council, the Grand Council or something else. Cantonal laws are passed there.

8595.q: What are the webs between a mallard's toes for?
8595.e: The skin between the toes works like a little paddle. This helps the duck move well through the water.

8596.q: What happens at low tide in the Wadden Sea that helps harbour seals?
a: Sandbanks appear out of the water
More fish come onto the beach
The sea becomes very still and dark
8596.e: At low tide the water level drops and sandbanks become visible. Harbour seals like to rest on these dry areas.
8596.m: At low tide seals rest on sandbanks.

8597.q: What is the large nest of a buzzard called?
8597.e: The nest of a buzzard is called an eyrie and is made of many branches. The pair often uses the same eyrie for several years.
8597.m: A bird of prey's nest is called an eyrie.

8598.q: What does a blackbird often do with its tail just after landing?
a: It tucks it under its wing
It rolls it up like a snail
8598.e: After landing, the blackbird often flicks its tail up briefly and back down again. You can easily recognise this typical behaviour from a distance.
8598.m: Blackbirds flick their tails up after landing.

8599.q: Roughly how long is a dromedary pregnant?
8599.e: Dromedaries carry their young in their belly for a very long time. That is longer than in humans.
8599.m: A dromedary's pregnancy lasts around thirteen months.

8601.q: How many legs does a housefly have?
8601.e: Like all insects, the housefly has six legs. With them it can run very fast and even hold on to smooth surfaces.

8602.q: Which shark has a head that looks like a hammer?
8602.e: The hammerhead shark gets its name from its wide, flat head. Its eyes sit right out at the sides.
8602.m: The hammerhead shark has a hammer-shaped head.

a: A spontaneous purchase made without thinking first
A planned purchase with a budget
A purchase that is always cheaper
A purchase you sell again later
8603.e: With an impulse buy you decide on the spot, often on a whim, without thinking about whether you really need the product. This can quickly upset your budget.
8603.m: An impulse buy is bought without thinking.

8604.q: How do some mites make use of dung beetles?
a: They let the beetles carry them to fresh dung
They build a wooden nest there
8604.e: The mites cling to the beetle and travel to fresh dung that way. This hitching a ride is called phoresy.

8605.q: Where does the sand lizard prefer to hide its eggs?
a: In loose, sun-warmed sand or soil
8605.e: The warmth of the sun helps the eggs to hatch, because the mother does not warm them herself. Loose soil is easy to dig.
8605.m: The eggs lie warm and loose in the soil.

8606.q: What shows that a mallard is a good swimmer?
a: Its webbed feet sit far back on its body
Its wings are shaped like fins underwater
It has gills like a fish
8606.e: The mallard's legs sit far back on its body, which helps with swimming. Together with the webbed feet, this lets it move skilfully through the water.
8606.m: The position of the legs helps with swimming.

8607.q: How is a woodlouse's back armour built?
a: From many plates one behind the other
8607.e: The woodlouse's back is made of several plates one behind the other. This keeps the body flexible.
8607.m: A woodlouse's armour is made of plates.

8608.q: What is the typical, cheerful twittering of a budgie called?
8608.e: Budgies like to make a cheerful twittering sound, which is often called chattering. It shows that they feel comfortable.

8609.q: Roughly how long does the female buzzard sit on her eggs?
8609.e: The buzzard mother sits on the eggs for about 33 to 35 days. During this time the male brings her food.

a: A sum of money left as security at the start of a tenancy and usually returned when you move out
A monthly extra charge for the flat
A bonus paid by the landlord
8610.e: The rental deposit is an amount you pay into a special account as security when you move into a flat. If there is no damage when you move out, you get it back.
8610.m: The deposit is security for the landlord.

8611.q: Roughly how long is a snow leopard from head to rump?
8611.e: On top of that comes the tail, which is around 80 to 100 centimetres. So in total it is over two metres long.
8611.m: Head and body measure about 1.2 metres.

8612.q: Which places does the grass snake often use to lay its eggs?
8612.e: The warmth produced by rotting helps the eggs to hatch. That is why females like to lay them in compost heaps.
8612.m: Warmth from compost hatches the eggs.

8613.q: How did Karl Marx see the difference between socialism and communism?
a: Socialism was to be a transitional stage on the way to classless communism
Socialism and communism mean exactly the same
Socialism is a form of capitalism
8613.e: According to Marx, a socialist transitional society would first emerge after a revolution. Only after that would the classless communist society follow.
8613.m: Socialism is an intermediate stage on the way to communism.

8614.q: What are the long hairs on the bison's head and front body called?
8614.e: The bison has long, shaggy fur on its head and shoulders. It also has a beard on its chin.
8614.m: Bison have a shaggy mane and beard.

8615.q: What does it mean that martens are crepuscular animals?
a: They are mainly out and about at dawn and dusk
They are only active at midday
They are only active in winter
They are only active on rainy days
8615.e: Crepuscular animals, like many martens, are especially active around sunrise and sunset. During the day they hide in dens, hollows or lofts.
8615.m: Martens are active at dawn and dusk.

8616.q: What is it called when several giraffe mothers look after the calves together?
8616.e: While some mothers look for food, others stay with the calves and keep watch. This group of young giraffes is also called a nursery.

8617.q: Which statement about body size is true when comparing a male and a female ibex?
a: Males are much bigger and heavier than females
Females are always bigger than males
Both sexes are exactly the same size
Size depends only on where they live, not on whether they are male or female
8617.e: Male ibex are much bigger and heavier than the females. This difference is called sexual dimorphism.

8618.q: Which feeding strategy does the Alpine salamander tend to use?
a: It lies in wait and snaps up suitable prey
It hunts animals in large groups
It filters plankton from the water
8618.e: The Alpine salamander lives alone and catches small prey animals nearby, usually with a quick snap. It does not hunt in groups.
8618.m: It catches insects one at a time, with precision.

8619.q: Is the koala mainly active during the day or at night?
a: It is mainly active at dusk and at night
It is only active at midday
It is always on the move
8619.e: Koalas are mainly active at dusk and at night and rest a lot during the day. This is called being crepuscular and nocturnal.
8619.m: Koalas are more active at night.

8620.q: Is the blue whale a fish or a mammal?
8620.e: The blue whale gives birth to live young and feeds them with milk. That makes it a mammal, even though it lives in the sea like a fish.
8620.m: Whales are mammals that live in water.

8621.q: What does a hippo like to eat most?
8621.e: Hippos mainly eat grass, which they look for on land at night. They only eat plants.

8622.q: Which animal is the state mammal of the US states Wyoming and Kansas and is often called the national mammal of the USA?
8622.e: The bison was declared the national mammal of the USA in 2016. It stands for strength and nature conservation.
8622.m: The bison is the national mammal of the USA.

8623.q: How is the adder protected in Switzerland?
8623.e: All native reptiles are protected in Switzerland. You may not catch them or kill them.

8624.q: How many eyes does a wasp have altogether?
8624.e: The wasp has two large compound eyes and three small simple eyes on its head. This helps it see light and movement well.

8625.q: On which continents does the kestrel live apart from Europe?
a: Only on one single small island
8625.e: The kestrel is widespread and lives not only in Europe but also in large parts of Asia and Africa. This makes it one of the most widespread birds of prey of all.
8625.m: It lives in Europe, Asia and Africa.

8626.q: How does the red kite usually fly when it is looking for food?
a: only flapping quickly like a hummingbird
almost always walking on the ground
always swimming close to the water
8626.e: The red kite is an excellent glider. It uses rising warm air, called thermals, to circle for hours with hardly a wingbeat.
8626.m: The red kite glides skilfully on thermals.

8627.q: Where does a barn swallow especially often sit when it sings?
a: On power lines or roof ridges
Deep below the surface of the water
8627.e: Barn swallows like to sing while sitting on power lines or roof ridges. From there they have a good view of their territory.
8627.m: They often sing on wires or roofs.

8628.q: Roughly how fast can a common swift fly in a straight line?
8628.e: Swifts are among the fastest birds in normal flight. Their sickle-shaped wings make them very fast and agile.
8628.m: Swifts fly very fast and are very agile.

8629.q: What is the group that okapis and giraffes belong to called?
8629.e: Okapis have two hoofed toes on each foot. That is why they count as even-toed ungulates.

8630.q: What does a sparrow mainly build its nest from?
8630.e: Sparrows collect dry stalks, grass and soft feathers to build their nest. This makes the nest soft and warm for the eggs.
8630.m: The nest is made of stalks and feathers.

8631.q: How many cubs does a female cheetah usually have in one litter?
8631.e: A female cheetah usually gives birth to three to five cubs. She raises them all on her own.
8631.m: Female cheetahs usually have several cubs.

8632.q: Where is the brown trout originally native?
8632.e: The brown trout originally comes from Europe. Later, people took it to many other countries.

8633.q: What is the correct name for the brown bear's long sleep in winter?
a: Winter rest, because its body temperature only drops slightly
Hibernation, because its body temperature drops a lot
8633.e: Unlike true hibernators such as the hedgehog, the brown bear's body temperature only drops a little. So it can wake up quickly at any time.
8633.m: Brown bears take a winter rest, not true hibernation.

8634.q: Why is the amino acid taurine especially important for cats?
a: Their body can hardly make it and needs it from animal food
It makes the fur more colourful
It is only needed for digesting plants
It has no importance at all for cats
8634.e: Cats can only make very small amounts of the amino acid taurine themselves and must take it in through animal food. A lack of it can lead to serious heart and eye damage.

8635.q: In which season do you usually first see young badgers outside the sett?
a: Never, they do not leave the sett
8635.e: Badger cubs are born in late winter and first grow up inside the sett. Only in spring do they dare to go out into the daylight.

8636.q: What does the typical call of the raven sound most like?
8636.e: The raven has a deep, strong voice that often sounds like ‘krrok’. This call can be heard over long distances.
8636.m: Its call sounds deep and croaky.

8638.q: What does a stork do when it wants to defend its nest?
a: it clatters loudly and threatens with its beak
it leaves the nest for ever
8638.e: If a stork feels threatened, it clatters loudly and makes threatening movements with its beak. It wants to keep intruders away from the nest.

8639.q: Who mainly brings food to the young buzzards in the nest?
a: Only other birds from the neighbourhood
Nobody, the young find everything themselves
8639.e: Both the male and the female buzzard help to feed the young. In the first weeks the female often stays closer to the nest, while the male does most of the hunting.

8640.q: When is the okapi mainly active?
8640.e: Okapis are active during the day. At night they usually rest.
8640.m: Okapis are forest animals active by day.

8641.q: Which plant does the caterpillar of the peacock butterfly like to eat most?
8641.e: The black, spiky caterpillars of the peacock butterfly often live in large groups on stinging nettles. There they find plenty of food.
8641.m: Peacock butterfly caterpillars love stinging nettles.

8642.q: What is cutting off an alpaca's wool called?
8642.e: Alpacas are usually sheared once a year, often in spring. This is so that they do not overheat in summer.

8643.q: How often is a centipede's venomous bite dangerous for people in Central Europe?
a: Rarely, it is usually only painful like a wasp sting
It works like a strong magic spell
8643.e: The native species are usually harmless to people. A bite can hurt and swell up, but it is rarely dangerous.

8644.q: Where does a least weasel often hide or nest?
a: In burrows taken over from mice
It builds huge earth castles of its own
It lives only high up in trees
It builds nests of twigs in treetops
8644.e: Instead of digging hard itself, the least weasel likes to use the existing tunnels of its prey. This saves energy and time.
8644.m: It uses other animals' mouse burrows as shelter.

8645.q: How does the grass snake overpower its prey?
a: It grabs it and usually swallows it alive
It kills it with strong venom
It strangles it like a giant snake
8645.e: The grass snake has no venom that is dangerous to people. It holds its prey with its backward-curved teeth and swallows it.
8645.m: The grass snake swallows its prey.

8646.q: On which continent does the Sumatran tiger live?
8646.e: The Sumatran tiger only lives on the island of Sumatra. It belongs to Indonesia in Asia.
8646.m: The Sumatran tiger lives in Asia.

8647.q: What is hard for a Roman snail when there is hardly any lime in the soil?
8647.e: Without enough lime in the soil, the snail cannot build its shell properly. That is why it likes chalky soil.

8648.q: What is the largest native toad species in Central Europe?
8648.e: The common toad is the largest toad species native to our region. Females can grow to more than ten centimetres long.
8648.m: The common toad is our largest toad.

8649.q: What does a blackbird do when it finds berries on a bush?
a: It pecks them straight off the twig
It digs them out of the ground
It dives into the water for them
8649.e: Blackbirds simply peck ripe berries straight off the bush. Berries are an important source of food, especially in autumn and winter.
8649.m: Blackbirds peck berries off the bush.

8650.q: Which factors are regarded as the main causes of the worldwide decline of insects?
a: Loss of habitat, pesticides and monocultures
An increase in birds and bats as predators
Colder winters as the Earth cools
8650.e: Intensive farming using pesticides and the loss of wildflower meadows in particular hit insects hard. Light pollution and climate change also play a part.
8650.m: Pesticides and habitat loss threaten insects.

8651.q: What is the typical wing shape of the peregrine falcon?
a: Long and pointed, ideal for fast flight
Short and round, ideal for gliding
8651.e: The narrow, pointed wings reduce air resistance and allow high speeds. This shape is typical of fast hunting birds.
8651.m: Pointed wings make the falcon fast.

8652.q: How does a stone marten mark its territory?
a: With scent glands and fixed droppings sites
8652.e: Stone martens regularly leave droppings at certain spots, called latrines, and spread their scent there. This shows other martens that the area is taken.
8652.m: Latrines mark the stone marten's territory.

8653.q: The photo shows a snow leopard. Where does it live?
a: In the high mountains of Central Asia
8653.e: The snow leopard lives in high mountains such as the Himalayas. It is a separate species, not a subspecies of the leopard.
8653.m: Snow leopards live in the mountains of Central Asia.

8654.q: Which of these animals is a scavenger?
8654.e: Scavengers feed on dead animals. Vultures, hyenas and some beetles are scavengers.

8655.q: Which fruit do orangutans particularly love, and is known for its smell?
8655.e: Orangutans like to eat durian, a spiky fruit with a very strong smell. They skilfully open the hard skin.
8655.m: Durian is one of their favourite fruits.

8656.q: How do elephants most often move around?
a: At a walk, faster when in danger
8656.e: Elephants usually walk calmly. When they run, they can reach a good speed for a short time.

8657.q: What does the sand lizard do to survive cold weather?
a: It goes into winter torpor and hides in the ground
It moves into a burrow underwater
It eats a lot and stays awake
8657.e: It spends the winter in a frost-free hiding place in the ground, without moving or eating. In spring it comes out again.
8657.m: In winter it stays motionless in the ground.

8658.q: When does a female lynx usually have her young?
8658.e: The young are born in late spring. Then there is enough prey and mild weather for raising them.
8658.m: Lynx kittens are born in early summer.

8659.q: How do people protect the snow leopard in its homeland?
a: With protected areas and by informing local people
With fences around the whole world
8659.e: Protected areas and projects with herders help the animals. Safe enclosures reduce the loss of farm animals.
8659.m: Protected areas help the snow leopard.

8660.q: In areas where the eagle owl lives, what often happens with smaller owl species?
a: They avoid being near the eagle owl, as it can catch them
They actively seek out the eagle owl for protection
They regularly attack the eagle owl together
They always live in the same nest as the eagle owl
8660.e: Smaller owl species often avoid being near the eagle owl because it can catch them as prey. So the eagle owl is both a kind of competitor and an enemy of smaller owls.
8660.m: Small owls avoid being near the eagle owl.

8661.q: How are newborn hares and rabbits different?
a: Baby hares are born furry and able to see, baby rabbits naked and blind
Baby rabbits are born able to fly
8661.e: Young hares are born with fur and open eyes and can soon run. Baby rabbits, on the other hand, are naked, blind and helpless.
8661.m: Baby hares are more developed than baby rabbits.

8662.q: What is special about the dromedary's upper lip?
a: It is split and very flexible
It is hard like a beak
8662.e: With its flexible lip, a dromedary can grab plants precisely. This helps it eat thorny bushes.
8662.m: A split upper lip helps with eating.

8663.q: What is different about the chimpanzee compared with the gorilla, although both are great apes?
a: The chimpanzee is much smaller than the gorilla
The chimpanzee has a tail, the gorilla does not
Only the chimpanzee lives in Africa
8663.e: Chimpanzees are much smaller and lighter than gorillas. But both belong to the great ape family.

8664.q: Why do we sometimes hear an echo?
a: Because the sound is reflected by a wall
Because our ears are too small
8664.e: Sound spreads out as a wave and is reflected by hard surfaces such as rock faces. We call this returning sound an echo.

8665.q: What does the skin of a slow worm feel like?
8665.e: Its scales are smooth and lie close together. That is why it looks shiny and not slimy.
8665.m: Slow worms are smooth, not slimy.

8666.q: How does the International Court of Justice (ICJ) differ from the International Criminal Court (ICC)?
a: The ICJ settles disputes between states, the ICC convicts individuals
The ICC only deals with trade disputes
The ICJ only convicts war criminals
8666.e: The ICJ is an organ of the UN and decides disputes between states. The ICC is a separate institution that can charge individuals with genocide, war crimes or crimes against humanity.
8666.m: At the ICJ states argue, at the ICC individuals are charged.

8667.q: In which Swiss city is the Universal Postal Union based?
8667.e: The Universal Postal Union makes sure that letters and parcels can be sent from one country to another. It is based in Bern, Switzerland’s capital.
8667.m: The Universal Postal Union is based in Bern.

8668.q: Roughly how wide can the wingspan of a carrion crow be?
8668.e: With its wings spread out, a carrion crow reaches a wingspan of about 90 to 100 centimetres. This lets it fly elegantly and powerfully.
8668.m: The wings span almost a metre.

8669.q: Which kind of shark glows in the dark deep sea?
8669.e: The lantern shark lives deep in the dark ocean. Its body can glow slightly to attract prey or to camouflage itself.
8669.m: The lantern shark glows in the deep sea.

8670.q: How many litters can a female least weasel have per year?
