8670.e: When there is plenty of food, meaning lots of mice, the least weasel can have young especially often. This lets the population quickly adapt to the amount of food available.
8670.m: Several litters a year are possible.

8671.q: Which Chinese city is especially well known for its large panda breeding centre?
8671.e: In Chengdu there are large centres where pandas are bred and protected. Many visitors go there to see pandas.
8671.m: Chengdu is famous for its panda centres.

8672.q: How many body sections do insects have, unlike the woodlouse with its many segments?
8672.e: Insects always have exactly three body sections and six legs. Woodlice, on the other hand, have many pairs of legs.

8673.q: Which animals are among the predators of baboons?
8673.e: In Africa, baboons are hunted by big cats such as the leopard and the lion. Hyenas can also be dangerous.

8674.q: Which of these animals is prey for a leopard?
8674.e: The impala is a medium-sized antelope and fits the leopard's choice of prey well. Adult elephants and rhinos are far too big.

8675.q: Why are loose gravel beds so important for the eggs of the lake trout?
a: Water can flow through and bring oxygen
The gravel keeps the eggs warm like a heater
The gravel is food for the young fish
The gravel turns the eggs red
8675.e: The eggs need oxygen, which the flowing water brings between the little stones. If the gravel is clogged, the eggs suffocate.
8675.m: Clean gravel supplies the eggs with oxygen.

8676.q: What is the grey fur on the backs of cheetah cubs for?
a: So that they can run faster
So that their mother can see them at night
8676.e: With the grey fur on their backs, the cubs look similar to a honey badger. Many enemies are wary of this fierce animal. So the cubs are better protected.
8676.m: The grey fur protects the little cheetahs.

8677.q: What does a dragonfly larva look like compared with the adult?
a: It has no wings, only wing buds
8677.e: In the larva, the wings are only present as small wing buds. They only grow during the last moults.

8678.q: What are the dark back and lighter belly of many fish for?
a: For camouflage from enemies and prey
8678.e: From above, the fish looks like the dark water; from below, like the bright sky. So it is harder to see.
8678.m: A dark back and light belly give camouflage.

8679.e: The dwarf hamster is a separate, smaller species of hamster. It stays much smaller than the golden hamster.

8680.q: What is a male chamois called?
8680.e: The male animal is called a buck. It is usually a little bigger and heavier than the female.

8681.q: Can a cheetah climb trees as well as a leopard?
a: Cheetahs love climbing most of all
8681.e: The cheetah is not as well built for climbing as the leopard. Its body is designed more for running fast.
8681.m: Cheetahs climb less well than leopards.

8682.q: How does the European tree frog catch its prey?
8682.e: The tree frog shoots its sticky tongue forwards in a flash. The prey sticks to it and is pulled in.
8682.m: The tongue shoots out in a flash.

8683.q: What is it called when trout swim to their spawning grounds?
8683.e: At spawning time, trout often move upstream to gravelly spots. There must be no obstacles in the way.
8683.m: The spawning migration leads to the spawning ground.

8684.q: How do carrion crows often behave outside the breeding season?
a: they travel alone out to sea
8684.e: Outside the breeding season, carrion crows often join together in large flocks, especially at shared roosts. This gives them protection from enemies.
8684.m: Outside the breeding season crows form flocks.

8685.q: What is a place where trout are deliberately bred called?
8685.e: On a fish farm, trout are bred and raised by people. From there they are often taken to lakes and rivers or end up on people's plates.
8685.m: Trout grow up on fish farms.

8686.q: What do rabbits do when they sense danger?
a: They thump the ground with their back legs
8686.e: Rabbits thump the ground hard with their back legs to warn other rabbits. You can clearly hear this thumping.

8687.q: Which small animals can greatly weaken moose when thousands of them sit in their fur?
8687.e: A heavy tick infestation takes a lot of blood from moose. Calves in particular are badly weakened by it.

8688.q: Why do pigs especially like to bathe when it is very hot?
a: Because otherwise they cannot cool down
Because they love water like fish
Because it makes them grow faster
8688.e: Because pigs can hardly sweat, a bath in mud or water on hot days is very important for them. This protects them from overheating.
8688.m: Pigs bathe to beat the heat.

8689.q: What is a female leopard called?
8689.e: The female is called a leopardess. The male is simply called a leopard.
8689.m: The female is called a leopardess.

8690.q: Why are African buffalo considered dangerous to people?
a: Injured or cornered animals sometimes attack
8690.e: They are strong and can defend themselves fiercely when in danger. That is why you should keep your distance.

8691.q: What is special about the tapir's nose?
a: Together with the upper lip it forms a short trunk
It is as long as an elephant's trunk
8691.e: The nose and upper lip have grown together into a short, flexible trunk. The tapir uses it to grab leaves and twigs.
8691.m: The tapir has a short grasping trunk.

8692.q: Who feeds the young great spotted woodpeckers in the nest?
8692.e: Mum and Dad woodpecker take turns bringing insects to the nest. This helps the young grow quickly.
8692.m: Mother and father feed them together.

8693.q: Why are many shark species under threat today?
a: Because too many sharks are caught
Because they eat too much plankton
Because the water is too cold
8693.e: People catch a great many sharks, for example for their fins. This makes some shark species rarer and rarer.
8693.m: Too much fishing threatens many shark species.

8694.q: What damage do cockchafer grubs cause to plants in farming?
a: They eat roots, so plants die
8694.e: When grubs eat lots of roots, grasses and young trees wilt. When there are huge numbers of them, they cause great damage.

8695.q: What does Anguilla anguilla mean in the name of the European eel?
a: It means fish without a head
8695.e: Anguilla anguilla is the scientific species name. The genus is called Anguilla.
8695.m: Anguilla anguilla is the scientific name.

8696.q: What colour is the skin of many dolphins usually?
8696.e: Most dolphins, such as the bottlenose dolphin, have grey skin. The belly is often a little lighter than the back.

8697.q: How does the sand lizard have its young?
a: It lays eggs and buries them in the ground
It gives birth to live young
It lays eggs in nests in trees
8697.e: The female digs a small hole in warm, loose soil and lays her eggs there. After that she does not look after the eggs any more.
8697.m: Sand lizards lay their eggs in the soil.

8698.q: How many official languages does the Confederation use for its official texts?
8698.e: The Confederation officially uses German, French and Italian as official languages. Romansh is only used in certain cases, even though it is a national language.
8698.m: The Confederation works in three official languages.

8699.q: What is a buzzard's eyrie mainly made of?
8699.e: The eyrie is built mainly from branches and twigs and is often lined with green twigs or soft material. Year after year the birds make it bigger.
8699.m: An eyrie is made of branches and twigs.

8701.q: What stripes does an okapi have on its legs and rear?
a: White horizontal stripes on a dark background
Black vertical stripes on a yellow background
8701.e: The legs and rear have white and dark horizontal stripes. The rest of the body is dark reddish brown to blackish brown.
8701.m: Okapis have zebra patterns on their legs.

8702.q: In Switzerland, what is it called when herds of goats are taken up to the alpine pastures in summer?
a: The Alpaufzug, the move up to the alp
8702.e: In early summer, farmers take their goats and cows up to the green mountain pastures. This is called the Alpaufzug.
8702.m: In summer the animals go up to the alp.

8703.q: What do young tapirs look like?
a: Brown with light stripes and spots
8703.e: The young have a pattern of light stripes and spots. It camouflages them in the undergrowth.
8703.m: Young tapirs are striped and spotted.

a: Through tracheae, fine air tubes in the body
8704.e: Air enters through small openings on the sides of the body into a network of tubes. This carries the oxygen straight to the organs.

8705.q: What does it mean that the common frog is cold-blooded?
a: Its body temperature adjusts to its surroundings
It can change its colour whenever it likes
8705.e: Unlike humans, the common frog cannot control its own body temperature. It depends on how warm or cold it is outside at the time.
8705.m: Cold-blooded animals adjust to the temperature.

8706.q: In which habitats does the puma live?
8706.e: The puma is very adaptable. It lives in many habitats, from mountains to forests and semi-deserts.

8707.q: What is the reddish liquid on a hippo's skin for?
a: It protects against sun and germs
8707.e: The reddish liquid protects the sensitive skin from strong sunshine and from germs. It is sometimes called blood sweat, even though it is not blood.
8707.m: The red liquid protects the skin.

8708.q: What is part of a moose's diet in summer?
8708.e: In summer, moose eat leaves, herbs and also water plants. To get them, they wade into shallow lakes.

8709.q: Roughly how many different kinds of shark are there in the world?
8709.e: Sharks come in many different shapes and sizes. Some are tiny, others are huge.
8709.m: There are over 500 different kinds of shark.

8710.q: Why does a roe deer fawn have white spots on its coat?
a: For camouflage in grass and light
So that it can jump better
So that it can call more loudly
8710.e: The white spots look like little spots of light in the grass. So the fawn is hardly ever spotted.
8710.m: Spots camouflage the fawn in the grass.

8711.q: What is the name of the large desert where the wild camel lives?
8711.e: The Gobi stretches across Mongolia and China. The last refuges of the wild camel are there.
8711.m: Wild camels live in the Gobi.

8713.q: Where does the common frog live for most of the year?
a: On land, for example in woods or meadows
8713.e: The common frog only goes to the water in the mating season in spring. For the rest of the year it lives on land in woods, meadows and gardens.
8713.m: Common frogs mostly live on land.

8714.q: What is the main difference between dabbling ducks and diving ducks?
a: Dabbling ducks stay near the surface, diving ducks go deeper
Diving ducks only live on land
8714.e: Dabbling ducks like the mallard mostly look for food near the surface of the water. Diving ducks, on the other hand, go right under and fetch food from the bottom.
8714.m: Diving ducks go deeper than dabbling ducks.

8715.q: Why are butterflies important for nature?
8715.e: When they visit flowers, butterflies carry pollen from one flower to another. This helps the plants make seeds.

8716.q: Where does the striped hyena live?
a: In North Africa, the Middle East and India
8716.e: The striped hyena lives in parts of Africa and Asia, from North Africa to India. It prefers dry, open landscapes.
8716.m: Striped hyenas live in Africa and Asia.

8717.q: Why is breeding okapis in zoos important?
a: It helps to preserve the species
8717.e: Zoos work together in breeding programmes to keep healthy populations with plenty of genetic variety. This supports species protection.

8718.q: What does a horse especially often use its long tail for?
8718.e: With its long tail, a horse can swat away annoying flies and insects. This protects its sensitive skin.

8719.q: Do carrion crows in Switzerland usually stay in the same place all year round?
a: yes, they are mostly resident birds and do not migrate
no, they fly to Africa every winter
no, they spend the summer at sea
no, they always spend the winter at the North Pole
8719.e: Most carrion crows in Switzerland are resident birds, which means they stay in their area all year round. Only in very harsh winter weather do some move briefly to milder places.
8719.m: Carrion crows mostly stay here all year.

8720.q: Where does the swim bladder worm that weakens the European eel come from?
8720.e: The swim bladder worm was brought in from Asia. It infects many eels and weakens them, especially on their long migration.
8720.m: A worm brought in from elsewhere weakens eels.

8721.q: What is seen as a special ability of many crows, such as the carrion crow?
a: they solve clever problems and are seen as very intelligent
8721.e: The crow family, which includes the carrion crow, are among the most intelligent birds of all. They can solve tricky tasks and remember things well.
8721.m: Carrion crows are very clever birds.

8723.q: What is the stage called in which the young tree frog lives in the water before it grows legs?
8723.e: This stage of development is called a tadpole. Tadpoles first breathe with gills and live entirely in the water.
8723.m: Tadpoles still live entirely in the water.

8724.q: How are bonobos important for the rainforest?
a: They spread seeds in their droppings
They fertilise the soil with eggshells
8724.e: Bonobos eat lots of fruit and later pass the seeds out somewhere else. This helps new plants to grow.
8724.m: Bonobos spread seeds in the rainforest.

8725.q: Why do some butterflies have eyespots on their wings?
8725.e: When a predator comes near, the butterfly opens its wings. The large eyespots then look like the eyes of a dangerous animal.
8725.m: Eyespots are meant to scare enemies.

8726.q: How does a fuel cell basically work?
a: It converts the chemical energy of hydrogen and oxygen directly into electricity
It uses wind energy to produce electricity
8726.e: In a fuel cell, hydrogen and oxygen react with each other, producing electricity and leaving water as a by-product. It is seen as a promising, clean technology for producing energy.

8727.q: How can experts roughly tell how old a horse is?
a: By the colour of its coat
By the size of its ears
By the length of its tail
8727.e: A horse's teeth change in particular ways as it gets older. So experts can roughly estimate its age from its teeth.
8727.m: The teeth reveal a horse's age.

8728.q: Roughly how old can a giraffe get in the wild?
8728.e: In the wild, giraffes live to about 25 years on average. In zoos they can sometimes live a little longer.

8729.q: What is a group of lions called?
8729.e: Unlike most cats, lions live together in groups. Such a group is called a pride.
8729.m: Lions live together in a pride.

8730.q: What does the name “United Nations” mean?
a: Countries that have joined together to act together
Countries that have a shared king
Countries that all speak the same language
Countries that form a football team together
8730.e: The name shows that many states in the world have united to solve problems together. Almost all the countries in the world belong to it.
8730.m: United Nations means that countries work together.

8731.q: What does the International Monetary Fund (IMF) do?
a: It helps countries in financial crises with loans
8731.e: The IMF supports countries that have got into economic difficulties with loans and advice. Switzerland is also a member.
8731.m: The IMF helps countries that are short of money.

8732.q: What does a wood mouse's burrow look like?
a: A system of tunnels and chambers underground
A large straw nest in a tree
8732.e: The wood mouse's burrow is made of many tunnels and small chambers underground, where it sleeps and stores food.

8733.q: How many eggs does a female barn swallow usually lay in one clutch?
8733.e: A barn swallow's clutch usually has 4 to 5 eggs. They are white with small reddish spots.
8733.m: Four to five eggs per clutch.

8734.q: What colour is the skin on an adult gorilla's face usually?
8734.e: An adult gorilla's face is usually dark and wrinkly. In young animals it can be lighter at first.
8734.m: A gorilla's face is usually black.

8735.q: On which continent does the bobcat live?
8735.e: The bobcat lives in many regions of North America. It is a little smaller than the Eurasian lynx, which also lives in Switzerland.
8735.m: The bobcat lives in North America.

8736.q: Which way does a mother koala's pouch open?
8736.e: Unlike the kangaroo's, the mother koala's pouch opens towards the back. This keeps the baby well protected while she climbs.

8738.q: When do brown trout normally spawn?
a: Only at full moon in July
8738.e: Unlike many other fish, the brown trout lays its eggs in autumn and winter. The young fish then hatch in winter or spring.
8738.m: Brown trout spawn in autumn and winter.

8739.q: What is a well-known good luck symbol at New Year in Switzerland?
a: A small marzipan or lucky pig
8739.e: The pig has long been a symbol of wealth and good luck. That is why people often give little lucky pigs made of marzipan or chocolate at New Year.
8739.m: The pig stands for luck and wealth.

8740.q: In which countries, for example, can you still find African wild dogs today?
8740.e: Important populations live in southern and eastern Africa, for example in Botswana, Zimbabwe and Tanzania. There are no wild populations in Europe.

8741.q: Roughly how heavy is an adult snow leopard?
8741.e: Males are usually heavier than females. This makes it much lighter than a lion or a tiger.

8742.q: How does an eagle owl behave when it spends the day at a resting place?
a: It usually sits still, well camouflaged, and hardly moves
It flies around all the time, calling loudly
It bathes in water all day
It walks around on the ground for hours
8742.e: During the day the eagle owl usually stays quiet and sits well camouflaged in a sheltered spot. This saves energy for hunting at night.
8742.m: The eagle owl rests still and camouflaged by day.

8743.q: How many lambs does a ewe usually have at once?
8743.e: A ewe usually has one or two lambs at the same time. Sometimes three lambs are born.
8743.m: A sheep usually has one or two lambs.

8744.q: Where in the world does the peregrine falcon live?
a: On almost every continent except Antarctica
Only on islands in the Pacific
8744.e: The peregrine falcon is one of the most widespread bird species in the world. It lives on almost every continent in very different habitats.
8744.m: The peregrine is at home almost worldwide.

8745.q: What is a sign of ‘checks on power’ in a working state under the rule of law?
a: Regular free elections and independent courts.
A strong secret service without oversight.
8745.e: In a state under the rule of law, power is regularly renewed through elections and checked by independent courts. These checks prevent a person or group from ruling permanently without control.
8745.m: Elections and courts keep power in check.

8746.q: Which animal gave the stag beetle its name?
8746.e: Its jaws look like the antlers of a red deer stag. The fights between the males are also similar to the fights of stags.
8746.m: The name comes from the stag.

8747.q: What can a housefly do especially well when flying?
8747.e: Thanks to its special wings, the housefly can change direction in the air in a flash. That makes it hard to catch.
8747.m: Flies change direction in a flash.

8748.q: What does perch spawn look like?
a: Single eggs buried deep in gravel
A foam nest on the surface
8748.e: The perch lays its eggs in long, net-like ribbons of jelly. These can be several dozen centimetres long.

8750.q: What does the term “convergent evolution” describe, using the streamlined bodies of dolphins and the extinct ichthyosaurs as an example?
a: Independent development of similar features in unrelated species
Random genetic mutation with no adaptive value
8750.e: Convergent evolution describes how species that are not closely related develop similar features under similar selection pressure. Dolphins (mammals) and the extinct ichthyosaurs (reptiles) independently developed a streamlined body shape for swimming.

8751.q: Which feature of its body helps tell a slow worm apart from a snake?
a: Its tail can break off and its body seems stiff
8751.e: Slow worms seem stiffer than snakes and move less smoothly. Their head also runs into the body without a clear neck.
8751.m: Slow worms seem stiffer than snakes.

a: No, they have no outer ear openings
8752.e: Snakes have no outer ears. They mainly sense vibrations through the ground and their bones.
8752.m: You cannot see ears on snakes.

8753.q: What are the soles of a cheetah's feet especially good for?
a: For good grip when running fast
8753.e: The cheetah's soles have small grooves, a bit like running shoes. Together with its claws they give a lot of grip when sprinting.
8753.m: Its paws give the cheetah good grip.

8754.q: How often per year does a female dog normally come into season?
8754.e: Most female dogs come into season about twice a year, although this can vary by breed and by dog. During this time they can become pregnant.
8754.m: Female dogs usually come into season twice a year.

8755.q: What often happens when a dictator dies?
a: Often a family member takes over power.
The country immediately becomes a democracy.
There is no government any more.
8755.e: In some dictatorships, such as North Korea, power passes down in the family, for example from father to son. That way control stays in a few hands.
8755.m: Power often stays in the family.

8756.q: Where did the wild ancestors of guinea pigs originally come from?
8756.e: Guinea pigs are descended from wild animals in the Andes in South America. People were already keeping them there many hundreds of years ago.
8756.m: Guinea pigs come from South America.

8757.q: What do young storks practise in the nest before they can fly?
8757.e: Before young storks leave the nest, they train their flight muscles by flapping their wings hard. This makes them strong enough to fly.
8757.m: Flapping their wings is practice for the first flight.

8758.q: Which three species are traditionally counted as jackals?
a: Golden jackal, black-backed jackal, side-striped jackal
Golden jackal, red jackal, ice jackal
Desert jackal, jungle jackal, mountain jackal
Silver jackal, copper jackal, golden jackal
8758.e: The three well-known species are the golden jackal, the black-backed jackal and the side-striped jackal. They all belong to the dog family.
8758.m: The three jackal species are the golden, black-backed and side-striped jackal.

8759.q: Which group of insects do pond skaters belong to?
8759.e: Pond skaters are true bugs and so they have a piercing mouthpart. They are not beetles or dragonflies.

8760.q: How does a common frog prefer to move on land?
a: It jumps with its strong back legs
8760.e: The common frog's back legs are long and strong. With them it can make long jumps to escape from enemies.
8760.m: Common frogs jump with strong legs.

8761.q: Apart from Switzerland, in which countries does the Alpine salamander live?
a: For example in Austria, Italy and Slovenia
8761.e: The Alpine salamander lives throughout the Alps and neighbouring mountain ranges. Besides Switzerland, these include Austria, Italy, Germany and Slovenia.

8762.q: What role does Switzerland play for the red kite compared with many other countries?
a: it is an important breeding area for the species
it has no red kites at all
the red kite only lives there in zoos
Switzerland is only a stopover area with no breeding pairs
8762.e: For its size, Switzerland is home to a large number of breeding red kites. There are many breeding pairs, especially in the Swiss Plateau.
8762.m: Switzerland is important for the red kite.

8763.q: What does the male kestrel often do while the female is sitting on the eggs?
a: He hunts and brings food to the female at the nest
He leaves the territory for ever
He sits on the eggs himself in turns all day
He builds a new nest for the next brood during this time
8763.e: While the female keeps the eggs warm almost all the time, the male does the hunting. He brings the mice he catches to the nest and so feeds his partner.
8763.m: The male hunts, the female sits on the eggs.

8764.q: In the wels catfish, who guards the eggs?
a: Nobody, the eggs are left alone
8764.e: The male builds a nest hollow and guards the eggs and the newly hatched young fish. He fans oxygen-rich water over the eggs.
8764.m: Male wels catfish guard the eggs.

8765.q: How many litters can a female red squirrel have per year?
a: Never more than one in her whole life
8765.e: A female squirrel can have young up to twice a year, usually in spring and in summer.
8765.m: Up to two litters a year are possible.

8766.q: What does the ‘majority of the cantons’ mean in a vote?
a: Most of the cantons must agree
Only the Council of States decides
Every canton votes the same way as the people
8766.e: For changes to the constitution, as well as a majority of the voters, a majority of the cantons is needed too. This is called the majority of the cantons.
8766.m: For the majority of the cantons, most cantons must agree.

8767.q: What do young storks look like shortly after hatching?
a: small and covered in white down
already as big as their parents
with black feathers all over their body
with a red beak like their parents
8767.e: Newly hatched storks are small and covered in soft, white down. Their beak is dark at first and only turns red later.
8767.m: Young storks have white down at first.

8768.q: What colour are the feathers of a typical greylag goose mainly?
8768.e: As its name suggests, the greylag goose has greyish brown plumage. This also helps it to blend in well in nature.
8768.m: The greylag goose has greyish brown feathers.

a: Mostly standing up, only very briefly
Always lying down like a dog
8770.e: Giraffes sleep very little and often standing up. This means they can run away quickly if there is danger.

8771.q: Why is the Alpine salamander especially interesting for experts who study amphibians?
a: Because of its rare live birth with no water stage
Because it lives in salt water
8771.e: Having young without larvae that live in water is quite rare among amphibians, and it makes the Alpine salamander an exciting subject for research. Researchers study how this adaptation developed.
8771.m: Its special way of having young interests researchers.

8772.q: Which group of vertebrates does the leopard belong to?
8772.e: Leopards have fur, give birth to live young and feed them with milk. These are typical features of mammals.

8773.q: Which danger especially threatens the bearded vulture today?
a: Lead poisoning from hunting ammunition in carcasses
8773.e: When bearded vultures eat the remains of animals shot with lead ammunition, they can be poisoned. That is why conservationists campaign for lead-free ammunition.

8774.q: Where does the edible frog have webbing between its toes?
a: On none of its four feet
8774.e: The edible frog's back feet have strong webbing that helps it swim. The front feet are built more for propping itself up.
8774.m: The webbing is on the back feet.

8775.q: What does it mean that dolphins are warm-blooded?
a: Their body always stays about the same temperature
They only get warm in summer
They have no body heat at all
They only warm up in the sun
8775.e: Dolphins are mammals and therefore warm-blooded. This means their body keeps its temperature fairly constant, even in cold water.

8776.q: Why is the common frog useful in the garden?
a: It loosens the soil like an earthworm
8776.e: The common frog eats many small animals, such as slugs and snails that nibble garden plants. At the same time it is food for storks and hedgehogs.
8776.m: The common frog is important in the food web.

8777.q: What does blood do in your body?
a: It takes oxygen and food everywhere
8777.e: Blood flows through your whole body and brings oxygen and nutrients to the cells. With a small cut, a little of it comes out.

a: Weather that is too cold in the tropics
8778.e: Logging and farming destroy the tapirs' forests. Hunting also threatens them.

8779.q: Roughly how long does it take for barn swallow eggs to hatch?
8779.e: The barn swallow's incubation lasts about 13 to 17 days. It is mainly the female that sits on the eggs.

8781.q: Roughly speaking, how many stomachs does a llama have?
8781.e: Llamas have a stomach with three chambers. Cattle, on the other hand, have four.

8782.q: Where does the red-eared slider, which is often released into ponds, come from?
8782.e: It was sold as a pet for a long time and then often released. In the wild it can push out native species.
8782.m: The red-eared slider comes from North America.

8785.q: Where in the world does the house sparrow live today?
8785.e: Today the house sparrow lives on almost every continent, because people took it with them long ago. It is one of the most widespread birds of all.
8785.m: The sparrow lives almost everywhere in the world.

8786.q: What is the best way a mole protects itself from enemies?
a: It squirts poison like a toad
8786.e: The mole's best protection is its underground tunnel system. Most enemies cannot get in there.

8787.q: Roughly how old can a lynx get in the wild?
8787.e: In the wild, lynx usually live for 10 to 15 years. In human care they can live a little longer.
8787.m: Lynx often live for more than 10 years.

8788.q: Is the brown bear a good swimmer?
a: Yes, it likes swimming and swims well
No, it never goes into water
It can only stand in shallow water
8788.e: Brown bears like to swim, for example to cross rivers or catch fish. They are strong swimmers with lots of stamina.
8788.m: Brown bears swim strongly and like it.

8789.q: What happens to a marmot's body temperature during hibernation?
a: It drops sharply, to just a few degrees
It always stays just as high
It drops far below zero degrees
8789.e: During hibernation, the marmot lowers its body temperature from about 37 degrees to just a few degrees. This means its body needs much less energy.
8789.m: During hibernation the body gets cold.

8790.q: Which group of animals does the giant panda belong to?
8790.e: Even though it looks so different, the panda is a real bear. But it eats almost nothing but plants.

8791.q: How many pairs of antennae do woodlice have?
a: Two, one pair is very small
8791.e: Woodlice have two pairs of antennae. In land woodlice the first pair is tiny; what you mainly see are the long antennae of the second pair.
8791.m: Woodlice have two pairs of antennae.

8792.q: Into how many departments, each led by a member of the Federal Council, is the federal administration divided?
8792.e: The federal administration is divided into seven departments. Each is led by a member of the Federal Council.

8793.q: Can a tiger purr like a pet cat?
a: No, but it can roar loudly instead
Yes, it purrs just like a pet cat
No, tigers cannot make any sounds
Yes, but only as a baby
8793.e: Tigers cannot purr, but they can roar loudly instead. In this way big cats are different from pet cats.

8794.q: What happens if people disturb a golden eagle's eyrie too often?
a: The pair may abandon the brood or not breed at all
The young grow faster because of it
The parents immediately build a bigger eyrie
Nothing, golden eagles are never disturbed
8794.e: Frequent disturbance near the eyrie can make the parents give up the brood or leave the eyrie. That is why special protection zones apply in many breeding areas.
8794.m: Disturbance can put breeding success at risk.

8795.q: In which region of the world do wild gibbons live?
a: In Southeast Asia and parts of South Asia
8795.e: Gibbons live in the tropical forests of Asia, for example in Indonesia, Thailand and Malaysia. There are no wild gibbons in Africa or America.

8796.q: What does the pattern of spots on a harbour seal's coat show?
a: It is unique to each animal, like a fingerprint
It reveals its exact age to the day
All harbour seals have exactly the same pattern
8796.e: Researchers can often recognise individual harbour seals by their particular pattern of spots. No two patterns are exactly the same.
8796.m: Every harbour seal has its own spot pattern.

8797.q: Roughly how many vertebrae does the human spine have?
8797.e: The spine is made of several sections with about 33 vertebrae altogether. It supports the body and protects the spinal cord.

8798.q: How big are the blue whale's flippers compared with its body?
a: It has no flippers at all
8798.e: The blue whale's flippers are several metres long. They help it to change direction in the water.

8799.q: Which kind of jackal has appeared in Switzerland in recent years?
8799.e: The golden jackal is spreading north from south-eastern Europe. For some years it has also been seen in Switzerland.
8799.m: The golden jackal is now also found in Switzerland.

8800.q: Which animals sometimes hunt the garden spider?
8800.e: Some birds and also certain wasps catch garden spiders as food. So the spider is not only a hunter but also prey.

a: All frozen water such as ice, snow and permafrost
The upper layer of the atmosphere
All the desert regions on Earth
8801.e: The cryosphere includes glaciers, sea ice, snow cover and frozen ground. It plays an important role in the global climate system, partly because of its high albedo.
8801.m: The cryosphere includes all frozen water.

8802.q: What shines in the sky at night and circles the Earth?
8802.e: The Moon circles the Earth. It does not shine by itself but is lit up by the Sun.

8803.q: How many sharp canine teeth, also called fangs, does a tiger have?
8803.e: A tiger has four long, pointed fangs that it uses to hold its prey. Two at the top and two at the bottom.

8804.q: Where do researchers often work to do experiments?
8804.e: A laboratory is a special room with equipment in which researchers carry out experiments. There they can test and investigate safely.
8804.m: Experiments are done in the laboratory.

8805.q: Does a pike tend to live alone or in large groups?
a: Always in twos like a couple
8805.e: The pike is a loner. It has its own territory and does not like sharing it with other pike.

8806.q: Which sense organ do you need to see?
8806.e: With your eyes you take in light, colours and shapes. The brain then puts these pictures together.

8807.q: Where does the perch most often live?
8807.e: The perch likes still to slow-flowing water with plants and hiding places. In Switzerland it lives in many lakes.

8808.q: The spotted redshank is a wading bird with long legs. Where does it look for food?
a: In shallow water and in mud
Diving deep in the open sea
8808.e: Wading birds use their long legs to wade through shallow water. They poke around in the mud with their beaks for worms and insects.
8808.m: Redshanks look for food in shallow water.

8809.q: How are slow worms protected in Switzerland?
a: They are protected animals and must not be caught or killed
They may be collected as pets
There are no rules at all
8809.e: Reptiles are protected by law in Switzerland. You may not kill them or simply take them away.

8810.q: Roughly how heavy can a fully grown harbour seal get?
8810.e: An adult harbour seal is much heavier than a person. Male harbour seals are often a little bigger and heavier than females.
8810.m: Harbour seals are fairly heavy animals.

8811.q: Roughly how old can wild ravens get?
8811.e: In the wild, ravens usually reach an age of around 10 to 15 years. However, many young birds do not survive their first year.
8811.m: In the wild, often 10 to 15 years.

8812.q: Which group of animals does the sand lizard belong to?
8812.e: The sand lizard has scaly skin and lays eggs, which is typical of reptiles. So it is not a mammal and not an amphibian.
8812.m: Sand lizards are reptiles, not amphibians.

8813.q: How many months does the edible dormouse's hibernation typically last?
8813.e: The edible dormouse spends around seven months in hibernation on average. In some years it can last even longer.
8813.m: Around seven months of hibernation is typical.

8814.q: When does the common frog travel to the water where it lays its spawn?
8814.e: As soon as it gets warmer in spring, common frogs set off for ponds. There they meet to mate.
8814.m: In spring common frogs travel to the pond.

8815.q: Roughly how long does it take for robin chicks to hatch?
8815.e: After about two weeks of incubation, the little chicks hatch from the eggs. At that point they are still completely naked and helpless.
8815.m: Chicks hatch after about two weeks.

8817.q: How many chambers does a dromedary's stomach have?
8817.e: As in all camels, the stomach is divided into three sections. This helps it make use of plants that are hard to digest.

8819.q: Which animals are among the predators of dragonflies?
8819.e: The hobby, a kind of falcon, even catches dragonflies in flight. Frogs, spiders and fish also eat them or their larvae.

8820.q: How does a chimpanzee mother usually carry her baby?
a: In a pouch on her belly
Not at all, it walks on its own straight away
8820.e: A small chimpanzee baby clings to its mother's fur. She carries it on her belly, or later on her back.
8820.m: Chimpanzee mothers carry their baby on their body.

8821.q: When an edible frog is hiding, what often sticks out of the water first?
8821.e: When an edible frog wants to hide from danger, it stays almost completely underwater. Usually only its eyes and nostrils poke out of the water.
8821.m: Only the eyes and nose poke out of the water.

a: Plants such as leaves, twigs and fruit
8822.e: Tapirs are herbivores. They eat leaves, buds, fruit and water plants.

8823.q: What do some seahorse couples do every morning?
a: They change the colour of the sea
8823.e: Some seahorse couples dance together briefly in the morning. This helps them recognise each other and stay together.
8823.m: A dance greets the new day.

8824.q: What does a salmon's body have to manage when it travels from the river to the sea?
a: It has to adapt to salty water
8824.e: Fresh water and seawater contain different amounts of salt. The salmon's body changes its salt balance during the journey.
8824.m: Salmon adapt to salt water and fresh water.

8825.q: What is on the brown trout's menu?
8825.e: The brown trout eats animals such as insect larvae, freshwater shrimps, worms and small fish. It also snaps up insects that fall onto the water.
8825.m: It eats insects, crustaceans and small fish.

8827.q: Which mammal is partly resistant to snake venom and eats adders?
8827.e: The hedgehog is largely resistant to adder venom. So it can catch adders.

8828.q: What happens when a strange grey heron enters another heron's territory?
a: The two always share everything peacefully
8828.e: Grey herons often defend their fishing spot with threatening postures and loud calls. Serious fights are fairly rare.

8829.q: Which group of animals does the jaguar belong to?
8829.e: The jaguar has fur, gives birth to live young and feeds them with milk. These are typical features of mammals.

8830.e: Pandas can swim well, even if they do not do it every day. This helps them cross rivers, for example.

8831.q: Many people say donkeys are stubborn. What are they really?
8831.e: Donkeys are often thought of as stubborn, but they are actually very clever and careful. Before they go on, they prefer to check whether the path is safe.

8832.q: What does a donkey's coat typically feel like?
8832.e: A donkey's coat is usually thick and a little shaggy. In winter it grows thicker to keep the donkey warm.
8832.m: A donkey's coat is thick and shaggy.

8833.q: Why do people work to protect rhinos today?
a: Because many rhinos are threatened with extinction
Because rhinos are supposed to become pets
Because there are too many rhinos
Because rhinos are dangerous to people
8833.e: Because poaching and loss of habitat harm many rhino species, conservationists work to protect the animals. The aim is to stop them dying out completely.

8834.q: Why is it better not to give bread to ducks in the park?
a: Because bread can make ducks ill
Because bread smells poisonous to ducks
Because ducks only eat at night
8834.e: Bread is unhealthy for ducks and fills them up without giving them important nutrients. Lettuce, oats or special duck food are better.

8835.q: How many main sections does a dung beetle's body have?
a: Four: head, neck, thorax and tail
Five: head, arms, chest, belly and legs
8835.e: This is true of all insects. The six legs and the wings are attached to the thorax.
8835.m: An insect's body is made up of head, thorax and abdomen.

8836.q: How long can a blue whale stay underwater before it has to breathe again?
8836.e: Blue whales can hold their breath for quite a while. But after that they have to come up again and breathe.
8836.m: After a while it has to come up.

8837.q: What enemies does the wood mouse have?
8837.e: Many animals hunt the wood mouse, for example owls, foxes and cats. That is why it usually stays hidden.
8837.m: Owls and foxes hunt wood mice.

8838.q: What does the wood mouse do if its burrow is destroyed?
a: It never builds a burrow again
It moves into a bird's nest
From then on it sleeps outside on a stone
8838.e: If its burrow is destroyed, the wood mouse simply digs a new one somewhere else.

8839.q: What do two male kangaroos do when they argue?
a: They box with their front paws
8839.e: Male kangaroos lean back on their tail and box with their front paws. This is how they find out who is stronger.

8840.q: Why do donkeys sometimes visit people in care homes?
a: Because calm donkeys are good for people
8840.e: Because donkeys are calm and patient, they sometimes help people to relax. This is called donkey-assisted therapy.

8841.q: What is the development of an aphid from larva to adult called?
8841.e: Aphid larvae already look like little aphids and moult several times. There is no pupa stage.

8842.q: What do bees eat in winter when no flowers are blooming?
8842.e: In summer, bees collect lots of honey as a store. They live on it throughout the winter.
8842.m: Honey is the bees' winter store.

8843.q: What are an elephant's tusks made of?
8843.e: The tusks are really very long incisor teeth. They keep growing throughout the elephant's life.
8843.m: Tusks are very long incisor teeth.

8844.q: What do lionesses often do when several females in the pride have cubs at the same time?
a: They feed and look after the cubs together
They put all the cubs in a nest outside the pride
Each one only looks after her own cubs
They send the cubs away alone
8844.e: Lionesses in the same pride often help each other raise the cubs. Sometimes they even feed other lionesses' cubs with their milk.

8845.q: How do earwigs often behave in their hiding places?
8845.e: Often several earwigs sit close together in the same hiding place. You can see this under flowerpots, for example.

8846.q: Which feathers does the grey heron wear, especially in the breeding season?
a: Long ornamental feathers on the back of its head
8846.e: In the breeding season, the grey heron grows a striking crest on the back of its head. These ornamental feathers are meant to impress a partner.
8846.m: A crest grows in the breeding season.

8847.q: What is an elephant's trunk made of?
a: The nose and upper lip grown together
8847.e: The trunk is a combination of nose and upper lip. It has no bones, only muscles.
8847.m: The trunk is nose and upper lip in one.

8848.q: Roughly how many kinds of kingfisher are there worldwide?
8848.e: There are over 100 different kingfisher species worldwide. Our native kingfisher is just one of them.
8848.m: There are over 100 kingfisher species worldwide.

8849.q: How does the substance nepetalactone in catnip affect many cats?
a: It makes cats instantly aggressive towards people
It makes cats fall asleep for days
It has no effect at all
8849.e: Nepetalactone in catnip binds to smell receptors and triggers short, playful to euphoric behaviour in many cats. Not all cats react to it, however; sensitivity is determined by their genes.
8849.m: Nepetalactone makes many cats briefly euphoric.

8850.q: How big can a fully grown lob worm (a large kind of earthworm) get?
8850.e: The lob worm is one of the largest native earthworm species. It can grow up to 30 centimetres long.
8850.m: Lob worms grow up to 30 cm long.

8851.q: What does the okapi mainly eat?
8851.e: Okapis are herbivores and mainly eat leaves from trees and bushes. They also eat fruit, grasses and fungi.

8852.q: What happens to a ray of light when it passes at an angle from air into water?
a: It is refracted and changes direction
8852.e: Because light is slower in water than in air, the ray bends as it passes from one to the other. This is called refraction.

8853.q: Which is the only country in the world with a triangular rather than rectangular national flag?
8853.e: Nepal is the only country in the world with an official national flag that is not rectangular. It consists of two triangles, one above the other.
8853.m: Nepal is the only country without a rectangular flag.

8854.q: Who is considered the inventor of the World Wide Web?
8854.e: In 1989 Tim Berners-Lee developed the World Wide Web, which made information on the internet easy to access. Today billions of people use it every day.
8854.m: Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web.

8855.q: How can you often recognise a buzzard even before you see it?
a: By its loud drumming on trees
8855.e: The buzzard's call sounds like a loud mew, something like ‘peeyah’. It can be heard far away, often before you spot the bird in the sky.
8855.m: A mewing call gives the buzzard away.

8856.q: What is the name of the sparrow that often lives on houses in our area?
8856.e: The house sparrow is the best-known sparrow. It likes to nest in nooks on houses and looks for food in gardens and towns.
8856.m: The house sparrow lives close to people.

8858.q: What is special about rabbits' teeth?
a: They keep growing throughout their life
They are pointed like a cat's
They stop growing after a year
8858.e: Rabbits' teeth keep growing all the time. That is why they have to gnaw and chew a lot, so that their teeth do not get too long.

8859.q: How can you recognise individual snow leopards in photos?
a: By their individual pattern of spots
8859.e: Every animal has its own pattern, a bit like a fingerprint. This makes it possible to tell individuals apart.

8860.q: Which animals look similar to pill millipedes and also roll up into a ball?
8860.e: Pill woodlice are crustaceans and look like pill millipedes from the outside. But they are only distantly related.

8861.q: What is the name of the bird whose name sounds like its own call?
8861.e: The cuckoo calls a loud ‘cuckoo’ and was named after exactly this call. Naming something after the sound it makes is called onomatopoeia.
8861.m: The cuckoo is named after its call.

8862.q: How many eyes does a cow have to see its surroundings?
8862.e: Like most mammals, a cow has two eyes, on the sides of its head. This lets it see almost all the way round and notice danger early.
8862.m: Cows have two eyes on the sides of their head.

8863.q: How does a wood mouse behave if you get too close to it?
a: It stays and plays with you
8863.e: The wood mouse is very shy and runs away as soon as someone comes near.
8863.m: It flees immediately when in danger.

8864.q: Which snake is often mistaken for the adder?
8864.e: The harmless smooth snake also has a pattern of spots and is often mistaken for the adder. But it has round pupils.
8864.m: The smooth snake is harmless but looks similar.

8866.q: How are the great crested grebe's feet especially adapted to swimming?
a: They have flaps of skin on the toes instead of webbing
They have claws like an eagle
They are completely covered in fur
8866.e: Instead of joined webbing, great crested grebes have separate flaps of skin on each toe. This makes them excellent swimmers and divers.
8866.m: Lobed feet make grebes expert divers.

8867.q: What is special about migrating dragonflies?
a: They travel long distances, sometimes across the Alps
They cannot fly and only walk
They never leave their pond in their whole life
8867.e: Some species, such as the migrant hawker, travel long distances. Some journeys even take them across the Alps.

8868.q: Which season is most dangerous for the wood mouse because of the cold and lack of food?
8868.e: In winter there is less food and more cold, so this time is especially difficult for the wood mouse.
8868.m: Winter is the most dangerous time.

8869.q: What colour is a penguin's belly usually?
8869.e: Penguins usually have a white belly and a dark back. This helps them hide from enemies in the water.
8869.m: A penguin's belly is white and its back dark.

8870.q: What do orcas sometimes do to get a seal off an ice floe?
a: Together they make a wave that washes the seal into the water
They fly out of the water
8870.e: Orcas swim towards the ice floe together and make a wave. This tips the seal into the water.

8871.q: Which senses are especially important for African buffalo?
8871.e: They often notice danger through smells and sounds. Their eyesight, on the other hand, is fairly average.

8872.q: Why does the grass snake often sunbathe?
8872.e: The sun warms its body and it becomes active. Without warmth it is sluggish.

8873.q: How does the wels catfish mainly hunt?
a: It lies in wait and sucks its prey into its mouth
It chases prey quickly in a shoal
It spears its prey with a spine
It catches prey in a net of slime
8873.e: The wels catfish opens its huge mouth in a flash, and the prey is sucked in with the water. Its good sense of touch and smell helps it do this.
8873.m: The wels catfish sucks in its prey.

8874.q: Why are buzzards sometimes wrongly taken for eagles?
a: Because they also look big and majestic in flight
Because they are exactly the same size as a golden eagle
Because they have golden feathers like eagles
Because they have to hunt the same prey as eagles
8874.e: Because buzzards look quite big and impressive with their wings spread out, people who do not know birds well sometimes take them for eagles. In fact, they are much smaller than a golden eagle.

8875.q: How does the coat of wild boar piglets change after a few months?
a: The stripes disappear and the coat becomes one colour
8875.e: Over time, wild boar piglets lose their stripes. The coat then becomes plain brown.
8875.m: The stripes disappear as they grow.

8876.q: Roughly how many eggs can a female cuckoo lay in one season?
a: Up to about 20 eggs in different nests
Only a single egg a year
8876.e: A female cuckoo can lay many eggs in one breeding season, often around one to two dozen, each in a different nest belonging to other birds. This increases the chance that as many young birds as possible survive.
8876.m: Many cuckoo eggs, many other birds' nests.

8877.q: How does a hippo move along the bottom of a river?
a: It walks and pushes off from the bottom
It swims fast like a fish
It only floats on the surface
8877.e: Hippos are not actually good swimmers. They walk and bounce along the riverbed.

8878.q: What best tells a blackbird apart from a starling?
a: The blackbird has a longer tail and no speckled feathers
The starling is completely black with no markings
The starling only lives in water
8878.e: The blackbird has a longer tail, while the starling is rather short-tailed and often looks a little glossy and speckled. That makes the two birds easy to tell apart.
8878.m: The blackbird has a longer tail than the starling.

8879.q: Which country do budgies originally come from?
8879.e: In the wild, budgies live in large flocks in the dry interior of Australia. From there they came to Europe as pets.

8880.q: Which element has the atomic number 1 in the periodic table?
8880.e: Hydrogen is the lightest and most common element in the universe and comes first in the periodic table with the atomic number 1. It has only one proton in its nucleus.

8881.q: Which predatory fish can be dangerous to adult whitefish?
8881.e: Pike and lake trout are predatory fish and also eat whitefish. Carp, tench and roach, on the other hand, eat plants, worms or small animals.
8881.m: Pike and lake trout are predatory fish.

8882.q: When do young common toads leave the water?
a: never, they stay in the water
only after three years in the water
8882.e: By summer the tadpoles have turned into little toads. Then they leave the water and move onto land.
8882.m: In summer young toads leave the pond.

8883.q: How do woodlice react to bright light?
a: They run away and look for shade
They immediately dig themselves in deep
8883.e: Woodlice avoid light, which you often see when you lift a stone. They then scurry quickly into hiding places.

8884.q: Apart from playing dead, how does the grass snake defend itself when it is cornered?
a: It hisses and makes fake attacks
It rattles its tail like a rattlesnake
8884.e: It hisses and strikes out with its mouth closed. This looks dangerous, but it is only a bluff.
8884.m: Fake attacks are meant to fool enemies.

a: A group of military officers who have taken power.
8885.e: A junta usually consists of senior officers who rule together after a coup. It often shuts down democratic institutions.
8885.m: Military officers rule together as a junta.

8886.q: What does the striped hyena do when it feels threatened?
8886.e: With its mane raised, it looks bigger. This is meant to scare off enemies.
8886.m: Striped hyenas look bigger with their mane raised.

8887.q: What does a beaver lodge often clearly show from the outside?
a: A large heap of branches and mud on the bank
A nest high up in a tree
A hole in the ground with no material
8887.e: From the outside you can recognise a beaver lodge by a noticeable heap of branches and mud on the bank of a river or lake. Inside there is a dry chamber above the waterline.
8887.m: A beaver lodge is a heap of branches and mud.

8888.q: Why does the hedgehog have sharp spines on its back?
8888.e: When the hedgehog senses danger, it rolls up into a spiky ball. Enemies then usually do not dare to attack.
8888.m: The spines protect the hedgehog from enemies.

8889.q: How do male adders fight over a female in spring?
a: They wrestle with each other without biting
They bite each other to death
They squirt venom at each other
They do not fight at all
8889.e: The males rear up and try to push their rival to the ground. Usually nobody gets hurt.

8890.q: What does the typical call of the buzzard sound like?
a: A deep bark like a dog
A fast twitter like a sparrow
A dull croak like a frog
8890.e: The buzzard's call sounds like a loud mewing cat, often described as ‘peeyah’. You often hear it before you spot the bird in the sky.
8890.m: A mewing call gives the buzzard away.

8891.q: In which season do you often see especially large numbers of jellyfish on beaches?
8891.e: In summer the water is warmer and jellyfish often multiply especially fast then. That is why you find them more often on some beaches.
8891.m: You often see more jellyfish in summer.

8892.q: How do dung beetles indirectly help against annoying flies in the pasture?
a: They take the dung away from the fly larvae
They stab flies with their horns
8892.e: Flies like to lay their eggs in fresh dung. When beetles break it down quickly, fewer larvae find food.
8892.m: Less dung means fewer fly larvae.

8893.q: What do adult bonobos do as well?
a: They store food for the winter
8893.e: Playing is not just something for young bonobos. Adults play too, and this strengthens their relationships.

8894.q: What is a female donkey called?
8894.e: The female animal is called a jenny. She looks after her foal.

8895.q: Why do chickens sometimes peck each other?
a: To show who is the boss
8895.e: By pecking, chickens show who is more important in the group. This keeps the order in the flock clear.
8895.m: Pecking sorts out the pecking order.

8897.q: Why are earthworms an important source of food for birds like the blackbird?
a: They are easy to find and nutritious
They cannot escape from large animals
They are poisonous to other animals
8897.e: Earthworms are rich in protein and live in many gardens. That is why birds especially like to look for them as food for themselves and their young.

8898.q: What does it mean that Switzerland is “neutral”?
a: It does not get involved in other countries’ wars
It has no government of its own
It is not allowed to vote
It does not belong to any continent
8898.e: Being neutral means that Switzerland does not take sides in wars between other countries. This has been the case for a very long time.
8898.m: Neutral means not taking sides in a war.

8899.q: Why are llamas' feet gentle on the ground?
8899.e: The soft pads under their toes hardly press the ground down. That is why llamas are gentle on paths and meadows.
8899.m: Soft soles are gentle on the ground.

a: Some species have simple eyes, many are blind
They all have large compound eyes
No species has ever had eyes
They have eyes at their back end
8900.e: Many species can hardly see and find their way with their antennae. Some have simple eyes that can only tell light from dark.

a: Yes, it can swim if it needs to
It can only float on its back
8901.e: Even though the badger is not a water animal, it can swim well enough to cross a river or pond. But it does not do this every day.
8901.m: Badgers can swim if they have to.

8902.q: Why does a young calf stay close to its mother?
8902.e: In its first weeks, a calf stays close to its mother to drink her nourishing milk. Only later does it start eating grass as well.
8902.m: Calves first drink milk from their mother.

8903.q: What happens during nuclear fission in a nuclear power station?
a: Heavy atomic nuclei are split and release energy
Light atomic nuclei merge into heavy nuclei
Electricity is produced directly from sunlight
8903.e: In nuclear fission, a uranium nucleus, for example, is split by a neutron, releasing large amounts of energy as heat. This heat is used to turn water into steam, which drives turbines.

8904.q: Which great power never joined the League of Nations, even though its President had suggested it?
8904.e: US President Woodrow Wilson had proposed the League of Nations after the First World War. But the US Senate rejected joining, which weakened the League. It was based in Geneva, and after the Second World War the UN replaced it.
8904.m: The League of Nations was the forerunner of the UN.

8905.q: Is the raven a migratory bird that flies south in winter?
a: no, it is mostly a resident bird and stays in its territory
yes, it always migrates as far as Africa
yes, it migrates to South America every winter
no, it migrates in summer instead
8905.e: Unlike many other bird species, the raven usually does not make long journeys. It stays in its usual territory all year round.
8905.m: The raven is mostly a resident bird.

8906.q: Which feature do all lizard species, including the common wall lizard, share?
a: They are reptiles with scaly skin
They all give birth to live young
8906.e: All lizards are reptiles and have protective scaly skin. This clearly sets them apart from fish and birds.

8907.q: How do scientists and rescue centres protect gibbons?
a: They care for rescued animals and release them back into the wild
They lock them all in small cages
They let them live with pets
8907.e: In rescue centres, rescued gibbons are nursed back to health and, if possible, released in the forest. This helps threatened populations.
8907.m: Rescue centres help gibbons back into the wild.

8908.q: Can a bumblebee sting more than once?
a: Yes, it can, unlike the honeybee
8908.e: A bumblebee's sting is smooth, so it does not get stuck. That means it can sting several times if it feels very threatened.
8908.m: Bumblebees can sting more than once.

8909.q: Why do rabbits have such long ears?
a: To hear well and to give off heat
8909.e: Their long ears help rabbits hear enemies early. They can also get rid of extra heat through their ears.
8909.m: Big ears help with hearing and cooling down.

8910.q: What is the female red deer called?
8910.e: The adult female is called a hind. She has no antlers.
8910.m: Female red deer are called hinds.

8911.q: How well can sea turtles see underwater?
a: Very well, better than on land
They cannot see anything at all
8911.e: Sea turtles see very well underwater, because their eyes are made for exactly that. On land, on the other hand, their vision is rather blurry.

8912.q: Why does a trout need especially clean water?
a: Because it needs a lot of oxygen to breathe
Because otherwise it grows too fast
Because otherwise it loses its colour
Because otherwise it cannot find eggs
8912.e: There is more oxygen in clean water. Trout need this oxygen to breathe through their gills.

8913.q: What do you see when you compare where the eagle owl lives with the Swiss Plateau?
a: Rocky areas of the Alpine foothills and the Jura suit the eagle owl better than flat, built-up land
The flat Plateau is the ideal habitat for the eagle owl
The eagle owl completely avoids all areas with rocks
There are no differences in habitat at all
8913.e: Because the eagle owl needs rock ledges for nesting, rocky areas in the Jura and the Alpine foothills suit it better than the densely populated Plateau. There it finds suitable nesting sites and undisturbed places to retreat to.
8913.m: The eagle owl prefers rocky Alpine foothills and the Jura.

8914.q: What does an elephant's skin feel like?
8914.e: An elephant's skin is very thick and full of wrinkles. The wrinkles even help it hold on to moisture for longer.
8914.m: Elephant skin is thick and wrinkly.

8915.q: In which year did women in Switzerland get the right to vote at federal level?
8915.e: Only in 1971 were Swiss women allowed to vote and elect at federal level for the first time. Compared with other countries, that was very late.
8915.m: Women have had the vote at federal level since 1971.

8916.q: What is the belt-like band on an earthworm's body called?
8916.e: The pale band in the middle of the worm is called the clitellum. It plays a part in producing young.
8916.m: The belt is called the clitellum.

8917.q: How do bees find their way back to their hive?
a: They use the sun and landmarks
8917.e: Bees remember the position of the sun as well as trees, houses and other landmarks. This way they find their way back to the hive even from far away.
8917.m: Bees find their way using the sun and the landscape.

8918.q: Which family does the edible frog belong to?
8918.e: The edible frog belongs to the family of true frogs, called Ranidae in Latin. This family includes many frog species around the world.
8918.m: The edible frog is one of the true frogs.

8919.q: What is special about the wood mouse's back legs?
a: They are longer and help it jump
They are much shorter than the front legs
It has no back legs at all
8919.e: The wood mouse's back legs are a little longer and stronger, which helps it jump quickly away from enemies.
8919.m: Longer back legs help with jumping.

8920.q: What are young stoats like when they are born?
a: Already able to see and with fur
8920.e: Young stoats are blind and hairless at birth. So they need a lot of care from their mother.
8920.m: The young are blind and hairless.

8925.q: When does the white stork usually come back to Switzerland?
8925.e: In spring, often as early as March, storks return from the south. Then their breeding season begins.
8925.m: The stork comes back in spring.

8926.q: What happens to the tail that a common wall lizard has shed?
a: It grows back, usually a bit shorter and a different colour
It immediately becomes a new lizard
8926.e: The new tail is not made of bone like the original one, but of cartilage. That is why it often looks a little different.

8927.q: What most clearly sets the carrion crow apart from the raven in appearance?
a: it is smaller and has a fan-shaped tail
8927.e: The carrion crow is much smaller than the raven, and its tail is fan-shaped in flight, while the raven has a wedge-shaped tail. Their calls also sound different.
8927.m: Carrion crows are smaller than ravens.

8928.q: What does a carp have on its mouth?
8928.e: Four small barbels hang from the carp's mouth. With them it can feel for food in murky water.
8928.m: Barbels help the carp to feel.

8929.q: What kind of mouthparts does the pond skater have?
8929.e: It pierces its prey with its beak and sucks it out. This is typical of bugs.
8929.m: A piercing beak for sucking out prey.

8930.q: What does a horse often show when it paws the ground with its front hooves?
a: That it is impatient or excited
That it is tired and asleep
That it is hungry for meat
8930.e: When a horse paws the ground with its hoof, it is often impatient or wants attention. This is part of its body language.
8930.m: Pawing shows a horse is impatient.

8931.q: What does the white stork usually build its nest from?
8931.e: The stork collects branches and twigs and puts them together to make a large nest. Over time it gets bigger and bigger.
8931.m: Branches and twigs make up the nest.

8932.q: What is the oldest female elephant that leads a herd called?
8932.e: The oldest and most experienced female elephant is called the matriarch. She leads the whole family through the savannah.
8932.m: The leader is called the matriarch.

8933.q: Which reptile is on the jaguar's menu?
8933.e: In South America, the jaguar also hunts caimans, which are related to crocodiles. It attacks them on the bank or in the water.

8934.q: Which natural enemies can be dangerous to young chamois kids?
8934.e: Golden eagles can attack and catch small, still weak chamois kids from the air. Adult chamois, on the other hand, are usually too big for eagles.
8934.m: Golden eagles are a danger to young chamois.

a: Yes, it can swim if it needs to
No, it is afraid of water and never goes in
No, it can only stay in trees
8935.e: Squirrels really can swim when they need to. But usually they avoid water.
8935.m: Squirrels can swim if they have to.

8936.q: What danger do electricity pylons sometimes pose for storks?
a: they can get an electric shock
8936.e: Storks like to sit on electricity pylons, and sadly they can get dangerous electric shocks there. That is why pylons are often built to be safer today.
8936.m: Electricity pylons can be dangerous for storks.

8937.q: Does the carp have teeth in its mouth?
a: No, but it has teeth further back in its throat
Yes, sharp teeth like a shark
Yes, but only in its upper jaw
No, it has no teeth at all
8937.e: The carp has no teeth in its mouth itself. But further back in its throat it has what are called throat teeth for breaking up its food.
8937.m: Carp have teeth in their throat, not in their mouth.

8938.q: What can be done to protect dung beetles in Switzerland?
a: Graze pastures gently and keep medicines out of the dung
8938.e: On natural pastures, beetles find enough dung. If it is free of harmful substances, they can develop well.

a: Loss of old woodland and dead wood
8939.e: Where dead wood and old tree stumps are removed, there are no young beetles. Road traffic and lights are also dangers.
8939.m: Tidied-up woods take away the stag beetle's habitat.

8940.q: What does the leopard in the picture like to eat most?
8940.e: The leopard is a meat-eater. It mainly catches medium-sized hoofed animals such as antelopes, but smaller animals too.

a: It changes the voltage of alternating current using two coils and a magnetic field
It converts direct current into heat
It produces light from kinetic energy
8941.e: A transformer consists of two coils of wire around a shared iron core. The changing magnetic field in the first coil produces a different voltage in the second coil, depending on the number of turns.

8942.q: What colour is a giraffe's tongue usually?
8942.e: The giraffe's dark tongue probably protects it from sunburn. It is often exposed to the sun for a long time while the giraffe is eating.

8943.q: Why can you see nothing at all in a completely dark room?
a: Because there is no light there
Because the air there is different
Because it is too quiet there
8943.e: We can only see things when light from them enters our eyes. Without light there is nothing for our eyes to catch.
8943.m: Without light we cannot see anything.

8944.q: How do many gibbons live socially?
a: In small family groups with a pair and their young
In huge herds with hundreds of animals
In large groups with many males and one female
8944.e: Most gibbon species live as a pair together with their young. The young leave the family when they grow up.
8944.m: Gibbons mostly live in small families.

8945.q: What is special about the snow leopard's eyes?
8945.e: Like other big cats, snow leopards have round pupils. Small cats often have slit pupils.

8946.q: Which kind of trout often spends its whole life in the same stream?
a: The rainbow trout, always in the sea
8946.e: The brown trout usually stays its whole life in the same stream or river where it was born. It does not travel as far as other kinds of trout.
8946.m: The brown trout often stays in the same stream.

8947.q: What happens if you squeeze a metal spring and then let go?
8947.e: A spring stores force when it is squeezed. When you let go, it releases the force again and springs back.
8947.m: Springs store force and give it back.

8948.q: How do migrating geese often take turns when flying in a V formation?
a: The lead bird at the front changes regularly
Only one single goose ever flies at the front
No goose ever flies at the front
They only ever fly in circles
8948.e: The goose at the front faces the most air resistance and gets tired quickly. That is why the geese take turns, so that none of them gets too exhausted.
8948.m: The lead birds take turns when flying.

8949.q: Roughly how long is an adult red kite from beak to tail tip?
8949.e: With a body length of around 60 to 70 centimetres, the red kite is one of Europe's medium-sized birds of prey. Even so, it looks very large in the sky because of its long wings.
8949.m: The red kite is about 65 cm long.

8950.q: What sound does an elephant often make with its trunk?
8950.e: When elephants are excited or angry, they give a loud trumpeting call through their trunk. You can hear this sound from far away.

8951.q: Which sense especially helps the eel to find food at night?
8951.e: Eels have an excellent sense of smell. With it they find prey even in the dark and in murky water.
8951.m: Eels find prey with their nose.

8952.q: What is special about reindeer antlers?
a: Both males and females have them
8952.e: In reindeer, both bulls and cows have antlers. In all other deer species, only the males have them.
8952.m: Both males and females have antlers.

8953.q: Which senses are especially well developed in the stone marten?
a: Only feeling in the tips of its ears
8953.e: When hunting at night, stone martens rely mainly on their good hearing and their keen sense of smell. This way they find prey even in the dark.
8953.m: Nose and ears guide the stone marten at night.

8954.q: Roughly how many eggs can a female perch lay?
8954.e: Female perch lay a great many eggs, often several tens of thousands. But only a small number of them become adult fish.
8954.m: Perch lay a great many eggs.

8955.q: Why is the orca seen as a very clever animal?
a: Because it learns clever hunting tactics and communicates with others
8955.e: Orcas learn from each other and plan their hunts together. That is why researchers think they are very intelligent.

a: A group of countries that share the French language
8956.e: La Francophonie links countries and regions where French is spoken, including French-speaking Switzerland. It promotes culture and cooperation.

8957.q: What happens shortly before a butterfly comes out of its pupa?
8957.e: Shortly before it hatches, you can already see the colours of the wings through the thinning case. Then it will not be long until it comes out.
8957.m: The case becomes see-through before hatching.

8958.q: Which country is often called “Europe’s last dictatorship”?
8958.e: Belarus under Alexander Lukashenko is often called “Europe’s last dictatorship”. Elections there are not considered free and fair, and critics are persecuted.
8958.m: Belarus is seen as Europe’s last dictatorship.

8959.q: Roughly how heavy does an adult male puma get?
8959.e: Males are usually heavier than females. They often weigh between 60 and 100 kilograms.
8959.m: Pumas weigh about as much as a person.

8960.q: What is a large group of sheep called?
8960.e: Lots of sheep together are called a flock. Sheep like to stay in a group because they feel safer that way.
8960.m: Lots of sheep make up a flock.

8961.q: How many young does a female orangutan usually have at once?
8961.e: Usually only one baby is born. Twins are very rare.
8961.m: Usually only one baby is born.

8962.q: Why are wetlands so important for the white stork?
a: there it finds lots of frogs and insects
there are fewer other birds there
it is warmer there than elsewhere
8962.e: In wetlands such as marshes and damp meadows there is lots of food for the stork. That is why these places are very important for it.
8962.m: Wetlands offer plenty of food for storks.

8963.q: How long does an adult mosquito usually live?
8963.e: An adult mosquito usually lives for only a few weeks. But some females survive the winter hidden in a cellar.
8963.m: Mosquitoes only live a few weeks.

8964.q: How are okapis usually kept in zoos?
a: On their own, with lots of space and places to retreat to
In large herds in a small space
8964.e: Okapis live alone and need peace and quiet. That is why zoos usually keep them on their own in large enclosures with hiding places.

a: Yes, many species can, especially the males
8965.e: Males are lighter and often fly better. The females of some species are too heavy and can only flutter at most.

8966.q: What does the common wall lizard usually do in cool, cloudy weather?
a: It tends to stay hidden and is not very active
It becomes especially fast and active
8966.e: Without the warmth of the sun, the wall lizard lacks the energy for quick movements. So on days like that it prefers to hide.

8967.q: How do giraffes warn each other of danger?
a: They watch each other and run away together
They change the colour of their coat
They lie flat in the grass
8967.e: When a giraffe suddenly becomes alert or runs away, other giraffes nearby notice too. In this way a warning spreads quickly through the whole group.
8967.m: Giraffes warn each other by watching.

8968.q: Compared with many other pets, what is noticeable about how guinea pigs hide illness?
a: They often only show pain very late
They show pain very clearly straight away
They become loud when in pain
8968.e: As prey animals, guinea pigs in the wild try to hide weakness so that enemies do not see them as easy prey. That is why you often only notice illness in them late.
8968.m: Guinea pigs hide illness for a long time.

8969.q: What do tigers have on the backs of their ears that they use to communicate?
8969.e: Tigers have white spots on the backs of their ears. These help tiger cubs to follow their mother through tall grass.
8969.m: White ear spots help the cubs follow.

8970.q: Which animals are among the enemies of the grass snake?
8970.e: Birds of prey, storks, foxes and martens catch grass snakes. Pet cats are also a danger.
8970.m: Birds of prey and foxes hunt grass snakes.

8971.q: What are so-called listed dogs in Switzerland?
a: Certain breeds that are subject to special keeping rules depending on the canton
Dogs that are on a waiting list
Dogs that perform in the circus
Dogs that belong to no breed
8971.e: Some cantons in Switzerland keep lists of dog breeds for which extra rules apply, such as permits or having to be kept on a lead. The rules differ greatly between cantons.
8971.m: Listed dogs are subject to special rules.

8972.q: What is the scientific species name of the domestic cat?
8972.e: The domestic cat has the scientific name Felis catus. It belongs to the cat family and to the order of carnivores.
8972.m: The domestic cat's scientific name is Felis catus.

8973.q: What does the beak of shanks, a group of wading birds, usually look like?
a: Wide and flat like a duck's
8973.e: With their slender beak they look for food in mud and shallow water. It can also grip small animals well.
8973.m: A long, slender beak for probing.

8974.q: What danger does the decline in flying insects pose for common swifts?
a: less food, which can reduce breeding success
it makes them too heavy to fly
it makes them die earlier than usual
it makes them lose the ability to fly completely
8974.e: Because swifts feed almost only on flying insects, the worldwide decline in insects affects them directly. Less food can mean that fewer young birds survive.

8975.q: How fast does a young pike grow?
a: Quite fast in its first year
It does not grow at all in its life
Only a little every ten years
It only gets bigger in winter
8975.e: Young pike grow quite fast in their first year. The more food they find, the faster they grow.

8976.q: How can you often tell that a goldfish is not well?
a: It swims strangely or lies still on the bottom
It jumps out of the water for joy
8976.e: Sick goldfish often swim in an unusual way or lie still on the bottom or at the surface. This is a sign that they need help.
8976.m: Unusual swimming is a sign of illness.

8977.q: Which body parts do millipedes and centipedes have that insects do not have in this form?
a: Many similar body segments with legs
A hard shell like a mussel's
8977.e: The body of millipedes and centipedes is made of many similar segments with legs. Insects are divided into head, thorax and abdomen.
8977.m: Many similar segments shape the body.

8978.q: How does the mother stone marten raise her young?
a: Alone in a sheltered hiding place
In an open field with no hiding place
8978.e: The mother gives birth to her young in a well-sheltered hiding place and looks after them there on her own. Only after a few months do the young become independent.
8978.m: The mother raises her young alone, in safety.

8979.q: What is the change from a solid to a liquid called?
8979.e: When melting, a solid becomes liquid through heat, for example ice becomes water. The opposite process is called freezing.

8980.q: Where does the name ‘white rhinoceros’ probably really come from?
a: From a word for ‘wide’ that was wrongly translated
From the white colour of its horn
Because it turns white in winter
Because it lives in the snow
8980.e: It is thought that a word meaning ‘wide’ was wrongly turned into ‘white’ in English. That is how the name ‘white rhinoceros’ came about, even though it is not white at all.
8980.m: White probably comes from wide, not from the colour.

8981.q: How many mute swan cygnets usually hatch from one clutch?
8981.e: From the five to eight eggs, usually just as many cygnets hatch. But not all of them always survive.
8981.m: Usually five to eight cygnets hatch.

8982.q: How can the snow leopard also use its coat to help it?
a: To hide from prey among the rocks
8982.e: The grey colour and the spots make it blend in with the rock. This lets it get close to its prey.

8983.q: What is it called when wool is made into a thread before you knit something with it?
8983.e: The sheared wool is first spun into a thread before you can knit a jumper from it, for example. In the past, this was often done by hand on a spinning wheel.

8984.q: What does a dog use to smell much better than a person?
8984.e: A dog's nose is incredibly sensitive. It can tell apart a thousand times more smells than a human nose.
8984.m: A dog's nose smells much better.

8985.q: What especially sets a wolf's teeth apart from those of plant-eating animals?
